blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: The issuer settles this in one sentence of its own launch release: 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form, and shareholders can move between the two through EQ's Shareholder Central portal.' The authoritative register is Equiniti's, and the chain is a synchronised representation of it — 'Shareholder records are maintained in real-time synchronization between EQ's regulated registry and Bullish's blockchain infrastructure.' Marketing in the same document pulls the other way ('a single authoritative ledger', 'a unified real-time record of ownership', 'settlement of shares end-to-end'), and the 2026-08-12 SEC-furnished release says the tokens are 'recorded at the registry level' — which concedes the register is the thing that records. Corroborating on-chain: 151.8M tokens sit in 21 accounts, which is the shape of a register mirror, not a shareholder ledger. Real-time mirroring is a materially better answer than batch reconciliation, but a mirror is not the record.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Both sides must be EQ-whitelisted, and the block is enforced in the token program. Issuer statement: 'Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses; AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled. Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level.' Verified on-chain 2026-09-16: the mint carries DefaultAccountState=Frozen, so any account created for an un-whitelisted wallet is frozen at birth and cannot receive; the freeze authority that alone can thaw it is a single wallet, 4Be7JXd6JaiXd6KkSMBEya5yt19gq1d11NEWTZC6Bsgk. The mint additionally carries PausableConfig, so all transfers can be stopped globally by one instruction. Worse for auditability than the peer: there is no allowlist program, so the permitted set cannot be enumerated by anyone outside EQ.

bearerRedemption.reason: You cannot present the token to any third party and obtain the share. The only conversion path is EQ's Shareholder Central portal — 'Shareholders can withdraw, hold, and return tokens through EQ's Shareholder Central portal' — which requires an EQ account and identity verification. No burn address is published, no timeframe is stated, no fee is stated, and returning tokens produces a book-entry position rather than cash. A holder without EQ access holds a token that is frozen-by-default at any new address and convertible nowhere.

forcedTransfers.reason: Mechanically overdetermined, verified on-chain 2026-09-16. The mint carries a PermanentDelegate (DPT54eBQJf7ghEQTzX7vjAb8WaDRMJFQchX6MKm3dFcD) which can transfer or burn from any token account without the holder's signature; the freeze authority (4Be7JXd6...) can re-freeze any account; and PausableConfig can halt the whole mint. So tokens sent to an unreachable address, stolen tokens, an estate transfer or a court-ordered seizure can all be effected on-chain. This is the axis on which issuer-sponsored registered-share tokenization beats every SPV/tracker wrapper. Caveat, and it is a real one: unlike Superstate — which documents forced burns 'if required by exogenous legal circumstances' and states that recovery procedures exist — Bullish publishes NO policy, no named role and no procedure governing these powers. The capability is proven; the governance of it is entirely undisclosed.

titleDeed.reason: The token is the ordinary share, not a derived or partial right. SEC-furnished statement (6-K Exhibit 99.1, 2026-08-12): 'These tokens are issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership and the same legal standing as conventional shareholders - not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper.' Launch release: 'shareholders can now hold BLSH ordinary shares as tokens'; 'Bringing real ordinary shares onto a public blockchain'; EQ 'maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form' — one register, one class, two forms. Corroborating quantitatively: the mint supply is ~100.6% of the shares outstanding reported on the FY2025 20-F cover, which is only possible if the tokens represent the ordinary shares themselves. Note the residual gap: no CUSIP/ISIN is published for the tokenized form and the token metadata carries none, so unlike the peer there is no identifier-level proof that the tokenized and NYSE-listed forms are the same security — the proof is the issuer's word plus the supply arithmetic.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Self-custody is an explicit design goal: the launch release lists 'self-custody of shares in shareholder-controlled wallets' among what holding tokens opens up, and the transfer model is bilateral movement between whitelisted wallet addresses rather than platform-internal bookkeeping. The 2026-05-05 release also places key risk on the holder ('risks related to the loss of private keys and wallet access'). Two heavy caveats: (1) self-custody is conditional — the account is frozen at birth and only EQ's whitelisting makes it usable, and the freeze authority can re-freeze it; (2) on the evidence it is barely used, with 21 token accounts against a fully-tokenized 151.8M-share register, so the capability exists and the practice essentially does not.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token's usability depends continuously and single-threadedly on Bullish/EQ. One plain wallet (4Be7JXd6...) is the sole mint and freeze authority, so if it stops signing, no new address can ever be thawed and no share can be tokenized; one plain wallet (DPT54eBQ...) holds the permanent-delegate, pause, split, hook and metadata authorities. Neither is a program PDA and neither shows any multisig program account, so there is not even the program-mediated continuity the Superstate Allowlist provides. The SHARE survives — it stays on EQ's register and EQ is an independent SEC-registered transfer agent with its own regulatory obligations, which is the one genuine comfort here. The TOKEN does not. And note the direction of travel: once the Equiniti acquisition closes (expected Q1 2027), the issuer, the transfer agent and the trading venue will all be the same group, removing the last independent party from the stack.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Not because no law applies, but because nobody has said which. The share's framework is clear enough (Cayman Islands company law, US Securities Act registration, NYSE listing, an SEC-registered transfer agent with a public file number 084-00416). The TOKEN's is not: no token terms of service, no holder agreement, no digital transfer agency agreement and no governing-law or dispute-resolution clause for the tokenized form was located anywhere, and the arrangement straddles a Cayman issuer, a US transfer agent and a Gibraltar exchange. The issuer itself says only that 'Tokenized securities are a novel instrument and there is limited legal, regulatory, judicial, operational and market precedent for their treatment.' The contrast with the peer is stark and is the clearest single reason Bullish should not simply inherit Superstate's grade: Superstate publishes New York law, exclusive New York jurisdiction and named arbitration fora. Here, if the chain and EQ's register disagree, or if a whitelisting is refused, no located document says whose law decides.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent is attached to the token and nothing independent is published about it. The mint's TokenMetadata additionalMetadata array is empty and its update authority is the issuer-side wallet; the metadata URI resolves to name/symbol/description/image only. There is no attestation mechanism, no proof-of-reserve, no auditor report, no smart-contract audit, no published reconciliation between mint supply and EQ's register, and no public API of any kind. EQ is a genuine independent second pair of eyes today — an SEC-registered transfer agent subject to Exchange Act §17A and the 17Ad rules — but it publishes no confirmation, and after the acquisition closes it will no longer be independent at all.

aiReady.reason: KYC/AML sits directly in the transfer loop. A wallet cannot hold or receive BLSH until EQ whitelists it, and the whitelist exists specifically to maintain 'compliance with U.S. securities laws and anti-money-laundering rules' — meaning a natural or legal person must be identified behind the address. An autonomous agent cannot obtain its own whitelisting, and unlike the peer there is not even the partial escape hatch of allowlisting a DEX pool, since 'AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled'. Fails on unconditionalTransfers in any case.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The mechanism exists and the responsible party is regulated. Mechanically the PermanentDelegate can move or burn from any account, the freeze authority can freeze any account, and PausableConfig can halt the mint — so a court order for seizure, reversal, inheritance or loss recovery is executable on-chain. Institutionally the register is maintained by Equiniti Trust Company, LLC, an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-00416) subject to Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21 including the Rule 17Ad-17 lost-securityholder obligations, and the issuer is an Exchange Act reporting company. Marked 'yes' on capability plus regulated-intermediary standing, but with the caveat that — unlike the peer — no contractual undertaking to honour judicial or regulatory orders, and no named role holding the reversal keys, was located.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Buyer-and-seller agreement is not sufficient. Both wallets must have been pre-approved by EQ before a transfer can settle, and an attempt to send to any other address 'will fail at the smart-contract level'. A trade between two already-whitelisted wallets does settle without per-trade sign-off, which is a real improvement over street-name settlement — but the counterparty set is chosen by the transfer agent, not by the parties, and because there is no public allowlist a would-be buyer cannot even determine in advance whether they are eligible.

attestations.attestor: US Securities and Exchange Commission (registration record), asserted by Bullish
attestations.statement: Equiniti Trust Company, LLC (CIK 0000005876, formerly American Stock Transfer & Trust Company, LLC) is a registered transfer agent, SEC File No. 084-00416, with live filings (TA-1/A 2026-07-31, TA-2 2026-03-31). Bullish: 'The launch is administered by Equiniti (EQ), Bullish's SEC-registered transfer agent.' There is no separate digital transfer agent: EQ is the single transfer agent for both book-entry and token form.

attestations.attestor: Bullish (press release furnished to the SEC on Form 6-K)
attestations.statement: 'These tokens are issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership and the same legal standing as conventional shareholders - not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper.' No CUSIP or ISIN is published for either form, so there is no identifier-level cross-check.

'shareholders can now hold BLSH ordinary shares as tokens on the Solana blockchain'; 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form'. One class, one register, two forms, corroborated by arithmetic: mint supply 151,810,063.5 against 150,833,916 ordinary shares outstanding at 2025-12-31.

'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form, and shareholders can move between the two through EQ's Shareholder Central portal.' This contradicts the same release's 'single authoritative ledger' phrasing; the register-assigning sentence controls. No document states which record prevails if the chain and EQ's register disagree, or who bears the loss.

'Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses ... Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level.' Verified on-chain: the mint carries defaultAccountState=Frozen, so every new token account is frozen at birth, and the freeze authority is the single wallet 4Be7JXd6JaiXd6KkSMBEya5yt19gq1d11NEWTZC6Bsgk. There is no allowlist program, so the restriction is verifiable but its membership is not.

The mint carries a permanent delegate (DPT54eBQJf7ghEQTzX7vjAb8WaDRMJFQchX6MKm3dFcD) able to transfer or burn from any token account without the holder's signature, a freeze authority (4Be7JXd6JaiXd6KkSMBEya5yt19gq1d11NEWTZC6Bsgk) able to freeze any account, and a pausable extension able to halt every transfer of the mint at once. Positive for legal integration in this vocabulary and a concentrated governance risk at the same time.

attestations.attestor: US Securities and Exchange Commission / NYSE (registration of the underlying ordinary shares)
attestations.statement: Bullish's ordinary shares were registered on Form F-1 (final prospectus 424B4 filed 2025-08-13), are listed on the NYSE, and Bullish is an Exchange Act reporting foreign private issuer (Commission File No. 001-42797) filing 20-F and 6-K. The tokenized form has no separate registration, qualification or relief, and the issuer cautions that 'there is limited legal, regulatory, judicial, operational and market precedent for their treatment.'

The core product claims - real ordinary shares, EQ as SEC-registered transfer agent, EQ as keeper of the official record, EQ-whitelisted bilateral transfers only, smart-contract-level rejection of non-whitelisted transfers, conversion via Shareholder Central and the canonical mint address - are all published on an issuer-hosted page, and the two most load-bearing claims are additionally furnished to the SEC on Form 6-K.

'Bullish becomes the first NYSE-listed company to fully tokenize its own equity cap table.' Verified: mint supply 151,810,063.5 against 150,833,916 ordinary shares outstanding at 2025-12-31 on the FY2025 20-F cover, about 100.6% - the full class rather than an opt-in tranche. Supply therefore measures the register, not adoption; the companion metric is the token-account count, which was 21.

'The official BLSH token contract address on Solana is 6d5zakCaxjjRALNRyudC6ArivxeBGT3XUAci7ybWQY8U - tokens claiming to represent BLSH from any other contract address are fraudulent.' Directly load-bearing: a third-party Ondo wrapper (BLSHon, A9PFmw9Hu8zzxDUoU351pio1E1XWBWBfWnjT9qoondo) trades on Solana under the Bullish name.

attestations.attestor: Bullish (press release furnished to the SEC on Form 6-K)
attestations.statement: 'several market participants executed trades of its tokenized shares (BLSH) on Bullish Exchange, settled against a USD stablecoin. The trades mark the first time tokenized equity has traded on a Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC)-regulated digital asset exchange.' In June 2026 Bullish received GFSC approval to offer tokenized securities trading. Note the conflict of interest in the same fact: after the Equiniti closing, issuer, transfer agent and venue are one group.

findings.statement: No token terms of service, holder agreement, transfer agency agreement, technical documentation, allowlist policy or fee schedule for onchain BLSH was located. The entire public record of holder rights and restrictions is two press releases; the general site Terms of Use govern the website and exchange, not the tokenized share.

Whitelisting is asserted by purpose rather than by procedure - it exists 'maintaining compliance with U.S. securities laws and anti-money-laundering rules' - but no onboarding documentation, KYC provider, evidentiary standard, sanctions-screening commitment or refusal process was located, and EQ's whitelisting criteria are not published.

Both authority addresses are plain system-program-owned accounts with space 0 and large balances: 4Be7JXd6... (mint and freeze, 441.98 SOL) and DPT54eBQ... (permanent delegate, hook, pause, split, metadata, confidential transfer, 607.69 SOL). Single-key compromise would reach minting new shares, thawing arbitrary addresses, clawing back any holder and pausing the register's on-chain form.
Neither authority address has a Squads or other multisig program account behind it, and no N-of-M threshold, quorum, timelock or key-management provider is disclosed anywhere.

No document says whether the freeze/mint key and the permanent-delegate/pause key are held by Bullish, by Equiniti or jointly; no role, officer, committee or escalation path is named. Given that EQ is asserted to maintain the official record while Bullish operates 'Bullish's blockchain infrastructure', which party can freeze or claw back a shareholder's position is unresolved.

The Token-2022 pausable extension is present and active (authority DPT54eBQJf7ghEQTzX7vjAb8WaDRMJFQchX6MKm3dFcD, paused false), so a single instruction from one wallet can halt every transfer of the security at once - a market-wide halt distinct from per-account freezing, exercisable without any court, regulator or notice period.

There is no custom program to timelock, but the equivalent risk is live: the authority wallet can set a transfer-hook program (the slot is initialized with programId null), flip the pause flag or change the split multiplier with immediate effect and no notice period. ScaledUiAmount's newMultiplierEffectiveTimestamp (currently 0) is the only delay primitive present anywhere in the design.

Bullish asserts 'real-time synchronization between EQ's regulated registry and Bullish's blockchain infrastructure' but publishes no reconciliation report, no attestation and no public supply or register endpoint, so an outside party cannot test the claim at all - not even the API-versus-chain comparison that exposed a measurable break at Superstate.

'Shareholders can withdraw, hold, and return tokens through EQ's Shareholder Central portal' is the whole of it: no eligibility criteria, no burn address, no processing time or SLA, no fee schedule, no jurisdictional exclusions and no statement of what happens if EQ refuses. Returning tokens yields a book-entry position, not cash.

The gap is acknowledged in marketing terms - the token settles with 'near-instant settlement in place of the T+1 batch cycle' and trades 'execute and settle outside of business hours' - but nothing states how long the token-to-book-entry conversion takes, which is the gap that matters for arbitrage and for a holder who needs to sell on NYSE.

No audit report was located. Mitigating: there appears to be no bespoke on-chain program to audit, since the compliance logic lives off-chain in EQ's whitelisting process and on-chain in stock Token-2022 extensions. Aggravating: the absence of any published technical documentation means this cannot be confirmed, and a transfer-hook program could be introduced later without disclosure.

No oracle feed for onchain BLSH was located (no Pyth, Chainlink or other publisher), which follows from there being no DeFi integration: 'AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled.' Price discovery happens on Bullish Exchange's order book, off-chain.

No PDA, no Squads account, no allowlist program and no disclosed threshold or key-management provider.

Redemption is for cash/stablecoin only — never for the underlying shares (Sales Terms expressly bar any conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities). Bank wire redemption not supported.
redemption.fees: No explicit redemption fee; Ondo retains the spread between the quoted token price and the price at which it trades the underlying, plus any fees. Investor pays gas. Dividends are reinvested net of 30% US withholding tax on the BVI issuer.

issuers.corporateActions: Voting: since 2026-04-28, via a Broadridge integration, tokenholders can express non-binding voting PREFERENCES to the issuer regarding the shares the issuer beneficially owns; the issuer has no legal obligation to follow them, and the holder has no shareholder voting right. Dividends are reinvested into the referenced stock net of withholding tax and expressed as an increase in the 'shares per token' multiplier; on Solana this is surfaced through the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension, so the displayed balance grows rather than the price (NVDAon multiplier 1.0017152487959897, AAPLon 1.003376073740221, SPYon 1.0077209101501272, TSLAon 1.0 as read on-chain 2026-09-16). Stock splits are handled the same way. Trading is paused around ex-dividend dates (roughly 7:50-8:10pm ET the day before the ex-date) and halted for ETF distributions until the amount is known; assets enter a reduced-size 'limited' state around earnings. Halts are listed at status.ondo.finance. The issuer may replace the Underlying held as collateral, and may exercise an Issuer Call Option to terminate and redeem all (not part) of a token series after a Termination Notice.

pricing.notes: Primary-market mint/redeem quotes are derived from the NYSE/NASDAQ price of the underlying plus the reinvested-dividend multiplier, delivered as a signed attestation with a short validity window and a spread retained by Ondo; the on-chain program validates against a Pyth oracle feed with sanity checks. The GM API exposes both 'primaryMarket' (token) and 'underlyingMarket' (off-chain stock) prices. Arbitrage between primary and secondary markets is available only to onboarded/whitelisted participants, so secondary DEX prices can drift: secondary liquidity is thin (Jupiter reported ~$491 of liquidity against ~$3.55m FDV for NVDAon on 2026-09-16). Trading follows US market sessions with an off-hours session; the issuer disclaims any representation about secondary-market price.

venues: Binance MTF, Abu Dhabi Global Market (admission-to-trading notice for some assets)
Binance Wallet, Bitget Wallet, Trust Wallet, OKX Wallet, MetaMask; custodial support from BitGo, Fireblocks, Zodia, Ledger

incidents.summary: Observed (not reported by the issuer): the Ankura daily verification reports are not published where the Sales Terms require. Sales Terms s.8.1(b) directs posting to https://ondo.finance/global-markets; that page contains no report links, and the reports are instead served from a Dropbox share link hardcoded in the web app's JS bundle. Publication also runs 2-4 business days behind (latest file 2026-09-10 as of 2026-09-16).

Observed (not reported by the issuer): press and Solana ecosystem write-ups state that Ondo enforces eligibility and transfer restrictions on Solana using Token-2022 Transfer Hooks. On-chain the TransferHook extension is initialized but its programId is null on all four mints sampled, so no hook program is invoked on transfer. Compliance on Solana is therefore currently enforceable only by the mint's freeze authority and the Pausable extension, not by a transfer hook.
No security incident, depeg, failed redemption or regulatory enforcement action against Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited was found in this research.

openQuestions: What is the numeric overcollateralisation factor for 'Other Collateral' per asset type? The Sales Terms say it is defined therein and varies, but the value was not located in the public text, and the daily report gives only a pooled Asset-to-Obligation Ratio (108.02% on 2026-09-10).

How much of the collateral is actually the underlying shares versus permitted substitutes (cash, unlisted instruments, crypto assets)? The daily report shows a large stablecoin and cash component (~$66m USDC/USDT plus ~$35m Alpaca cash) but does not label any of it as Standard vs Other Collateral for a given series.

Why are the Ankura reports not published at https://ondo.finance/global-markets as Sales Terms s.8.1(b) requires, and is the Dropbox folder considered contractual compliance? Also: is the 2-4 business day publication lag a process issue or a change in practice?

Will a TransferHook program be installed on the Solana mints, and if so what will it enforce? The hook authority is set and press describes hooks as the compliance mechanism, but programId is null today — installing one would silently convert unconditionalTransfers from yes to no.

Who controls the freeze authority key 51QVCuHfL1FeNjd8BDeffCKhCcAYoULnVB3yjNhShiuK and the mint/scaled-UI/pause authority 9foMHsSDq7nMg4WPusSz9eY7tyxyukqborA8GyU5cUxD — single signer or multisig, and with what timelock? The Solana program README describes role-based access control but the on-chain authorities were not resolved to multisigs.

The NVDAon Final Terms (11.11.2025) name Ethereum Mainnet only as the Blockchain. Have FMA-filed Final Terms been supplemented to cover the Solana issuance (Jan 2026), and does the Base Prospectus Supplement of 04.05.2026 do that?
Are the Spearbit and Cyfrin audit reports published, dated, and do they cover the Solana Anchor program (github.com/ondoprotocol/global-markets-solana) rather than only the EVM contracts?
Is there an annual audited financial statement for Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited? The docs promise annual independent audits 'made available to investors' but none was found published.

Practical effect of the Prohibited-Persons clause: a secondary buyer can receive the token but 'shall have no rights under any Offering Documents'. Does the issuer track and act on this, and how would it treat a chain of transfers through an ineligible holder?
The 2026-04-13 SEC no-action request would put the collateral security entitlements on Ethereum via Oasis Pro TA. Has the SEC responded, and would that change the OGM holder's claim?

Broadridge voting-preference passthrough (live 2026-04-28): does it require KYC/onboarding, a minimum holding, or an Ondo account, and is it available to Solana holders? The issuer's discretion to disregard preferences is not quantified or reported on.

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Authority keys in practice / Multisig evidence, 2026-09-16): one mint authority, PDA-like (getAccountInfo returns no account), running daily mintTo, burnChecked and transferChecked for primary-market issuance and redemption; two freeze authorities, of which the active one (51QVCuHfL1FeNjd8BDeffCKhCcAYoULnVB3yjNhShiuK) transacts through the Squads v4 program and has five transactions ever including one freezeAccount and one thawAccount. No Ondo mint carries a permanentDelegate, so there is no delegate authority to govern.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: The Sales Terms elect Swiss law and constitute the tokens as Ledger-Based Securities under arts. 973d et seqq. CO: 'The Ledger-Based Securities are transferable ... by way of transfer via the Securities Ledger', and the register is identified as the token contract addresses themselves. There is no parallel authoritative holder register for the notes. (The underlying collateral shares are separately recorded at DTC via Alpaca, but that is the collateral, not the token.)

unconditionalTransfers.reason: No allowlist gates secondary transfers: docs state the tokens are freely 'transferable outside the US' and 'can be held by any smart contracts or other externally owned accounts or wallets'. On-chain (2026-09-16) the Token-2022 TransferHook extension has programId null, defaultAccountState is 'initialized' (not frozen), and there is no permanent delegate — so a transfer needs no issuer signature. Caveats: a freeze authority (51QVCuHfL1FeNjd8BDeffCKhCcAYoULnVB3yjNhShiuK) and the Pausable extension exist, the Sales Terms contemplate sanctions-address blocking via a third-party screening provider, and the hook authority could install a hook program at any time. Also, transfer being technically free does not make the buyer a rights-holder: 'Prohibited Persons shall have no rights under any Offering Documents'.

bearerRedemption.reason: Redemption is explicitly conditioned on KYC: 'As a condition to redeeming any of its Tokens, a Token holder must satisfy the Issuer's customer due diligence, or know your customer, requirements', and the docs warn that a secondary-market acquirer may not meet them and 'may not be able to redeem'. Redemption also requires a signed off-chain attestation from Ondo's API and a whitelisted address. Presenting the token alone gets nothing, and no holder may ever demand delivery of the underlying shares.

forcedTransfers.reason: No on-chain mechanism exists to move tokens without the holder signing: the mints carry no permanent delegate or clawback authority (verified 2026-09-16 on four mints). What exists is immobilisation — a live freeze authority plus the Pausable extension — and the Sales Terms limit the Tokenizer's burn function to 'Ledger-Based Securities held by itself', describing a broader 'freezing function and/or extend[ed] burning function' as a future addition subject to the updating power. So theft/mis-send recovery and inheritance cannot be executed by moving the token today.

titleDeed.reason: The token is a debt instrument — a 'blockchain-based tracker certificate' / structured note — not the share. 'Because you hold a note rather than the share itself, you do not receive shareholder voting or information rights'; holders get a redemption claim plus a security interest in collateral, and are expressly barred from ever demanding delivery of certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Tokens are standard SPL Token-2022 / ERC-20 assets holdable by 'any smart contracts or other externally owned accounts or wallets (e.g. Metamask, Bitget Wallet, Trust Wallet, OKX Wallet)'; the Final Terms contemplate the investor holding in 'a non-custody wallet or blockchain-based address, which the Investor has exclusive access to'. No custodian is required to hold.

issuerIndependent.reason: Every economically meaningful function depends on Ondo: the redemption claim runs only against OGM Limited with no further recourse ('Purchasers shall have no further recourse to the Issuer'), the shares-per-token multiplier is updated by an Ondo-controlled ScaledUiAmount authority, pricing comes from Ondo's attestation API, and the mint/freeze/pause authorities are Ondo keys. The mitigation is partial and off-chain: on a Realisation Event the requisite tokenholders can direct Ankura to foreclose on the collateral, liquidate it and distribute cash — which is a wind-down, not continued function.

presetJurisdiction.reason: The applicable law is stated, if layered: Swiss law for the tokens as Ledger-Based Securities (arts. 973d et seqq. CO) and for the Sales Terms, with Swiss Rules arbitration seated in Zurich; New York law for the Collateral Agreement and the Alpaca control agreement; South Dakota law for the BitGo control agreement; BVI for the issuer's corporate law and AML; Liechtenstein FMA as prospectus authority. Nothing is left undetermined.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: An independent third party (Ankura Trust Company, LLC) verifies the existence, amount and valuation of the collateral every business day and publishes a signed report, continuously since 2025-10-01 (245 reports through 2026-09-10). Limitations: the attestation is an off-chain PDF, nothing links it to a specific mint (the figures are issuer-level and pooled across Ondo Stocks, USDon and USDY), tokenMetadata additionalMetadata is empty, and Ankura verifies 'based solely on account data and reports submitted by Issuer' via read-only access, disclaiming responsibility for their accuracy.

aiReady.reason: Derived: unconditionalTransfers = yes and tokenSelfCustody = yes, so an autonomous agent can hold the token in its own keypair and trade it on Jupiter or a DEX without passing a humanity test. The limit is the primary market only — minting and redeeming require KYC onboarding and a whitelisted address, so an agent can trade the token but cannot create or destroy it.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The Sales Terms give the Tokenizer express, pre-defined authority to 'freeze the relevant Tokens', to rescind 'any or all putative transfers in violation of these Sales Terms', to cancel tokens 'with or without making any payment therefor', and to execute 'the order of a court or authority recognized in the British Virgin Islands'. Swiss art. 973h CO additionally provides a judicial cancellation route for lost tokens followed by burn-and-reissue to a new address. Caveat: the freeze authority is live on-chain, but the extended burning function needed to execute a cancellation against a third party's balance is described as a future extension, so enforcement today is realistically limited to immobilising a balance.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A secondary transfer is effective on the ledger transfer alone under art. 973d CO — no issuer or platform sign-off is required, and no on-chain hook or allowlist intercepts it. The buyer, however, is deemed by acquisition to represent that it is not a Prohibited Person, and if it is, it 'shall have no rights under any Offering Documents' — so the transfer of the token can be valid while the transfer of the claim is not.

attestations.statement: Ankura, as Verification Agent under the Sales Terms dated 2025-07-17, reviewed and confirmed the amounts, valuations and calculations of the collateral as of 8:00pm ET on 2026-09-10, based solely on issuer-submitted data and read-only access to the collateral accounts. Daily since 2025-10-01.

Asset-to-Obligation Ratio 108.02%: total assets $1,229,196,568.57 against total liabilities $1,137,983,260.72, of which Ondo Stocks outstanding market value $1,037,858,343.08 (10,450,205.93 tokens) and USDY $79,664,349.93. Pooled across products, not per mint.

The daily report itemises holdings by location: long market value of positions, USD at BitGo / SVB / Coinbase, Alpaca trading and clearing accounts, Ondo Stocks in the BitGo custodian wallet, Anchorage, USDC at BitGo/Circle/Coinbase/Bridge/PSM, BSC-USDT and SOL-USDC at PSM, and funds in transit.

Sales Terms s.8: daily verification of the collateral with a report due by 4:30pm GMT the next calendar day, commencing with Calculation Day 2025-10-01; monthly reconciliation within 15 days of month end with a report within 5 business days thereafter.

Custodians named in the FMA-filed Final Terms: Alpaca Securities LLC, 2 E 49th St., Floor 11, New York, NY 10017; and BitGo Trust Company, Inc., 6216 Pinnacle Place, Suite 101, Sioux Falls, SD 57108. Alpaca is also the Fiat Account Provider and Broker.

Sales Terms s.3.2: Alpaca Securities LLC covenants to remain 'duly registered and in good standing with the SEC, a member of and in good standing with FINRA' and in material compliance with FINRA/SEC/state broker-dealer requirements for the term of the Institutional Account Agreement dated 2025-06-25.

Final Terms: 'The Issuer is not allowed to lend out Collateral, unless explicitly agreed in advance between the Issuer and the Investor.' Sales Terms: the Custodian 'is neither allowed to do any securities lending nor any other proprietary transactions with the Underlyings held as Collateral at all times, except as expressly permitted by law or the Issuer.' Note the issuer-consent carve-out; no on-loan figure is published in the daily report.

First-priority perfected security interest in the collateral granted to Ankura Trust Company, LLC as Security Agent for the benefit of tokenholders, perfected via account control agreements with Alpaca (NY law) and BitGo (SD law). Each purchaser has a sole pro-rata claim to the collateral allocated to its token type; recourse is limited to collateral proceeds with no further recourse to the issuer or its directors.

The Base Prospectus defines what may stand in for the shares - 'Other Collateral' of cash, listed securities, non-listed book-entry instruments or highly liquid crypto assets listed on three exchanges with 30-day volume over USD 50m - and subjects each to an asset-type overcollateralisation factor monitored once per business day with T+1 cure.

Base Prospectus: 'The Tokens are designed as Blockchain-based Tracker Certificates (debt instruments) seeking to track underlying asset(s)'. Product Security Type in the NVDAon Final Terms: 'Debt Instrument'. ISIN VGG7001AAH73. This supersedes the earlier rwa-sonar record of token-represents-equity, which was wrong.

'you do not have shareholder voting rights, shareholder information rights or other shareholder rights from the issuer of the underlying securities'; and no party may demand conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities. Non-binding Broadridge voting preferences have been passed through since 2026-04-28.

Base Prospectus for a Program for the issuance of tokenized Securities approved by the Liechtenstein FMA on 11.11.2025 under Art. 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, with per-series Final Terms filed with the FMA and PRIIPs KIDs. Validity expires 11.11.2026 unless supplemented. FMA approval attests completeness, comprehensibility and consistency only.

Sales Terms: 'Register and source code: Contract addresses (the Ledger-Based Securities Contract or Ledger)'. Transfer of the security is effected 'by way of transfer via the Securities Ledger' under arts. 973d et seqq. CO. Note s.973g(1)(1) CO registration of a security interest 'is technically not supported by the Securities Ledger'.

On four sampled mints the Token-2022 transferHook extension has programId null, defaultAccountState is initialized, and no permanent delegate exists, so secondary transfers execute without issuer approval and with no allowlist or KYC to hold. This corrects the earlier rwa-sonar record of transfer restriction.

Contractually the Tokenizer may freeze tokens, rescind putative transfers made in violation of the Sales Terms, cancel tokens 'with or without making any payment therefor', pause all transfers, and execute BVI-recognised court orders. On-chain today only freeze and pause are wired; the burn function is limited to tokens held by the Tokenizer itself.

Sales Terms, Base Prospectus, Supplement, per-asset Final Terms and PRIIPs KID are all publicly downloadable from the asset product detail pages without login - notwithstanding that the docs FAQ says offering materials are provided only after onboarding, and that the Sales Terms are headed 'CONFIDENTIAL'.

findings.statement: Sales Terms s.8.1(b) requires the verification reports to be posted at ondo.finance/global-markets. Nothing is there: the 245 Ankura PDFs live in a Dropbox share link hardcoded in the app JS bundle, are not machine-readable, and on 2026-09-16 the latest report was dated 2026-09-10.

The Base Prospectus permits 'Other Collateral' of cash, listed securities, non-listed book-entry instruments or highly liquid crypto in place of the underlying shares, and the daily report does not break out how much of the collateral is Standard versus Other.

The issuer describes itself as a bankruptcy-remote SPV with an independent director, segregated assets, books and accounts, and a non-petition covenant. This is the issuer's own description; no third-party insolvency opinion was found published.

Ondo's docs state the tokenized-stock contracts 'have undergone independent audits by Spearbit and Cyfrin', but no report, date or scope was located and it is unconfirmed whether the Solana Anchor program in this repository was in scope.

Ondo press material claims transfer hooks enforce eligibility. On-chain the transferHook extension has programId null on every one of the 212 Ondo mints, so no hook gates transfers; the actual mechanism is the freeze authority and the pausable extension.
The Ondo freeze key has five transactions in its entire history, including one freezeAccount and one thawAccount between 2026-04-27 and 2026-05-01: the power has been used on a real holder account.

The freeze authority transacts through the Squads v4 multisig program. The single mint authority, by contrast, returns no account from getAccountInfo (a PDA-like address) and runs daily mintTo, burnChecked and transferChecked for primary-market issuance and redemption.

Every Ondo mint carries the Token-2022 pausable extension (authority 9foMHsSDq7nMg4WPusSz9eY7tyxyukqborA8GyU5cUxD, paused false on 2026-09-16), so one instruction halts every transfer of a series at once. No mint was paused at read time.

Ondo's own assets API reported 97 of 452 listed assets paused at read time with reason 'unavailable_in_session', 27 off-hours tradable and 354 tradeable: the primary market is session-gated by the issuer, not continuously open.

Ondo's 164 priced Solana tokens carried roughly $72k of combined DEX liquidity on 2026-09-16, 158 of them under $1k, against about $1.04bn of outstanding token value. The Solana listing is not a DEX market; the real market is Ondo's own mint/redeem price.
Organic share of 24h DEX volume was 2.2%, the lowest in the universe, and 80 of the 212 Ondo mints had zero 24h DEX volume.
Median top-10 holder share per Ondo token was 98.4% on 2026-09-16: the supply sits with the issuer rather than being distributed to end holders.

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Authority keys in practice / Multisig evidence, 2026-09-16): one mint authority, PDA-like (getAccountInfo returns no account), running daily mintTo, burnChecked and transferChecked for primary-market issuance and redemption; two freeze authorities, of which the active one (51QVCuHfL1FeNjd8BDeffCKhCcAYoULnVB3yjNhShiuK) transacts through the Squads v4 program and has five transactions ever including one freezeAccount and one thawAccount. No Ondo mint carries a permanentDelegate, so there is no delegate authority to govern.

issuers.issuingEntity: Not named. ToS: "PreStocks is a distributed network of contributors located around the world who collaborate primarily through digital means." No incorporated issuer, SPV sponsor or counterparty is identified anywhere in the public materials.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: unknown - undisclosed. ToS states components "may be operated, performed, or provided by different legal entities in different jurisdictions" and that the entity contracting with the user "may differ between products, tokens, jurisdictions, and points in time, and may be added, removed, substituted, restructured, or replaced at any time without notice".
issuers.governingLaw: No substantive governing law is stated. Disputes go to good-faith negotiation for 30 days, then binding arbitration under the London Court of International Arbitration Rules; seat London, England; sole arbitrator; English language; individual basis only (no class actions).
issuers.regulatoryStatus: Unlicensed and self-disclaiming. Site disclaimer: "PreStocks is not a broker-dealer, investment advisor, exchange operator, transfer agent, custodian, virtual asset service provider, or similar regulated entity." No securities registration or exemption is cited; the ToS instead asserts "All blockchain transfers via the Services are secondary transfers effected outside the United States and are not primary offerings to U.S. persons" (Regulation S-style posture, but Reg S is never named).
issuers.holderClaim: A bearer Token-2022 token that "reference[s] economic exposure to designated pre-IPO companies" and confers "no ownership, voting, dividend, information, or other legal rights". The ToS grants no proprietary interest in any SPV, share or asset; the holder's only stated entitlement is to request redemption for USDC "or another mutually agreed form of value", which the operator may satisfy instead by pointing the holder at on-chain liquidity.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: Undisclosed by design. FAQ: "Counterparty legal names are not disclosed because they require contractual confidentiality to avoid unwanted solicitation, reputational targeting, and potential adverse actions from issuers or intermediaries." Backing is described only as "one or more vetted holding entities that verifiably own the underlying exposure".

custodyVerification.frequency: "published periodically or available on request if costs are covered" (FAQ) - no cadence committed
custodyVerification.notes: Claimed only. CoinDesk (2026-05-13): "neither the platform nor any third-party auditor has published the attestation reports the company promised at launch." Verified 2026-09-16: /attestations, /transparency, /proof-of-reserve and /reserves all return HTTP 404, and no attestation page appears in sitemap.xml. The only machine-readable feed is the issuer's own unsigned price/supply API.

redemption.eligibility: Any non-US, non-Restricted holder "may request redemption" - discretionary, not an entitlement. Which path is used "depends on those circumstances"; the operator may direct the holder to on-chain liquidity instead of processing a redemption.
redemption.rails: USDC or "another mutually agreed form of value"; alternatively realisation via on-chain liquidity, conversions, wraps, migrations or exchanges. Post-IPO the stated path is conversion into an equivalent tokenized public stock rather than cash.
redemption.fees: Unbounded and unilateral. ToS reserves redemption, settlement, conversion and withdrawal fees plus markups/spreads, enforced "at the token, smart-contract, or program level" via transfer-fee configurations and hooks, changeable "without prior notice and without your consent", with no obligation "to publish, itemize, or explain the basis of any fee". Observed on-chain: 50 bps transfer fee, raised from 0 bps (fee epoch 848 -> 1032).

issuers.corporateActions: IPO: underlying positions become convertible on-chain (without KYC) into an equivalent tokenized public stock; typical 6-month post-IPO lockup during which the token may trade at a discount; holders have 9 months post-IPO (3 months after lockup) to convert, after which "the tokens will expire worthless and will no longer be supported". M&A: cash deals distribute net proceeds pro rata as USDC; equity deals may become convertible into a tokenized version of the acquirer's equity "if we create and support one", with a 6-month conversion window, then expiry. Separately, balances can be restated unilaterally through the scaledUiAmountConfig multiplier (OPENAI x1.4861347 effective 2026-07-17).

pricing.notes: Issuer publishes markPrice ("the gross price per share of the referenced company") alongside the on-chain tokenPrice. FAQ claims mint/redeem arbitrage keeps them aligned. Observed divergence on 2026-09-16 undercuts that: SPACEX markPrice 144.38 vs tokenPrice 113.56 (token ~21% below mark); ANTHROPIC 1008.37 vs 960.99. No external NBBO exists for a private company, so the mark is issuer-determined and unaudited. CoinDesk (2026-05-13) noted ANTHROPIC implied valuation above $1.3T against roughly $23M of total assets.

venues: any wallet or app integrating Jupiter
listed ecosystem integrations include Phantom, Trust Wallet, Bitget Wallet, Binance Wallet, Robinhood Wallet, Gate, CoinGecko, DefiLlama

incidents.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI publicly declared SPV-routed transfers of their stock invalid, and the two PreStocks tokens fell sharply. Anthropic: "We do not permit special purpose vehicles to acquire Anthropic stock and any transfer of shares to an SPV are void under our transfer restrictions", warning that third parties selling exposure via "direct sales, forward contracts, tokenized securities, or other mechanisms" are "likely either engaged in fraud or offering an investment that may have no value". CoinDesk reported ANTHROPIC -34% and OPENAI -39% over seven days.

Same event reported with different magnitudes and levels by The Block: ANTHROPIC about -38% to roughly $879 (market cap about $8.3M) and OPENAI about -46% to roughly $1,080 (market cap about $2.2M), measured "since late Tuesday" rather than over seven days. The Block said it sought comment from PreStocks and published no response.

Backing adequacy questioned: CoinDesk reported roughly $23M of total assets behind an ANTHROPIC implied valuation above $1.3T, on-chain liquidity of about $333,000 in stablecoins plus about $18,000 in SOL, and that the attestation reports promised at launch had never been published by the platform or any third-party auditor.

OPENAI mint scaledUiAmountConfig multiplier scheduled to move from 1 to 1.4861347 effective 2026-07-17T16:30:00Z, restating every holder's displayed balance upward by about 48.6% without any transfer. Confirms the issuer can unilaterally rebase balances; no public explanation was found.

Verified that no reserve attestation is published: /attestations, /transparency, /proof-of-reserve and /reserves all 404 and sitemap.xml lists only the home, products, ecosystem, faq and per-company pages.

openQuestions: Who actually issues the tokens? No legal entity is named anywhere; "a distributed network of contributors" is not a counterparty a holder could sue, and the LCIA clause names no respondent.
Which holding entities hold the exposure, and in what form? Names are withheld as policy, so the 1:1 backing claim in the API description is unverifiable in principle, not just in practice.
Is ANTHROPIC exposure backed at all after Anthropic declared SPV transfers void under its transfer restrictions? The token still trades and the supply was never reduced.
Has any attestation report ever been produced to any holder on request, and at what cost?
Why was the OPENAI scaledUiAmount multiplier set to 1.4861347 on 2026-07-17 - a share split at OpenAI, a restatement of units per token, or a correction of over/under-collateralisation?
What substantive law governs the contract? Only an arbitration seat is specified.
Why does SPACEX trade about 21% below the issuer's own mark if mint/redeem arbitrage works as the FAQ describes?
xAI has a live product page in sitemap.xml but no API entry or mint - is it unlaunched, delisted, or was it withdrawn?

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Authority keys in practice, 2026-09-16): one key WV9PJN7XTmTLVwbutCLFxp8TyePee6Xq5mRq6Fti5Wc holds mint, freeze, permanent-delegate, pause, metadata and transfer-fee authority on all 8 mints, and is Squads-multisig-controlled (Squads v4 program seen in its transactions, which are mostly withdrawWithheldTokensFromMint fee harvesting). Multisig on signers, fully concentrated on roles.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Tokens are described in the ToS as "bearer digital tokens"; there is no shareholder register, transfer agent or off-chain holder list, and the operator explicitly disclaims being a transfer agent. Whoever holds the mint's token accounts is the holder. Note this is the ledger for the claim, not for the underlying shares, which sit in an undisclosed holding entity's own books.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Compliance is reactive, not proactive: defaultAccountState is "initialized" (new accounts are not frozen), the transferHook extension carries a null programId, and no allowlist gates transfers. Any wallet can send to any wallet today, subject only to a 50 bps fee. The freeze, pause, clawback and blocklist powers are exercised after the fact, which is exactly the reactiveCompliance model this flag implies.

bearerRedemption.reason: Redemption is a discretionary request, not a bearer right. A holder "may request redemption of Tokens for USDC or another mutually agreed form of value", and whether a redemption is the path used "depends on" operational, legal and market circumstances - the operator may instead point the holder at on-chain liquidity. US persons are excluded entirely, and the counterparty holding the exposure is undisclosed, so there is no identified third party against whom presenting the token compels delivery.

forcedTransfers.reason: Confirmed both in law and on-chain. ToS: tokens are subject to "freezing, forced transfer, burning, refund, compulsory redemption, migration, and the addition of addresses to transfer allowlists or blocklists", and the mints carry a live permanentDelegate plus freeze and pausable authorities all held by WV9PJN7XTmTLVwbutCLFxp8TyePee6Xq5mRq6Fti5Wc. The operator may act "without prior notice and without your consent" and is "under no obligation to investigate before acting".

titleDeed.reason: Explicitly disclaimed: PreStocks "confer no ownership, voting, dividend, information, or other legal rights" and are "not affiliated with, endorsed by, or issued by" the referenced company. The token references economic exposure held by a third party; it is a derived partial right, not title.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Ordinary Token-2022 mints held in any Solana wallet (Phantom, Trust, Bitget and others are listed integrations); no custodial account is required and no KYC gates holding.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token is worthless without the operator. Post-IPO value depends on the operator creating and supporting a tokenized public stock to convert into, and tokens "expire worthless and will no longer be supported" after a 9-month (IPO) or 6-month (M&A) conversion window. The operator can also pause all transfers globally, and the backing counterparties are unnamed, so no holder could pursue them if the operator disappeared.

presetJurisdiction.reason: No issuing entity, no jurisdiction of incorporation and no substantive governing law are stated; the ToS says the contracting entity may be "added, removed, substituted, restructured, or replaced at any time without notice". The only fixed legal locus is an LCIA arbitration seat in London, which fixes the forum but not the applicable law or the counterparty.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Attestation is promised but nothing exists to attach. Reports are "published periodically or available on request if costs are covered", no attestor is named, CoinDesk reported on 2026-05-13 that none had ever been published, and every plausible transparency URL 404s as of 2026-09-16. There is no on-chain attestation or proof-of-reserve feed.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers is yes and tokenSelfCustody is yes, and the FAQ confirms "Buying and selling onchain in DeFi (peer-to-peer) does not require KYC." An agent can hold and trade these tokens. The caveat is that an agent cannot pass the non-US-person representation the Participant Agreement requires, and holds an asset subject to clawback.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The strongest legal-integration feature here. The ToS commits the operator to act on any "court or administrative order, or request or inquiry from any governmental, regulatory, tax, or law-enforcement authority" by freezing, clawing back, compulsorily transferring, burning or compulsorily redeeming tokens, and the permanentDelegate extension makes that enforceable on-chain without holder cooperation.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A peer-to-peer or DEX transfer settles on the agreement of buyer and seller alone - no issuer sign-off, allowlist check or KYC step sits in the transfer path. Validity can be revoked afterwards by clawback, but the transfer itself needs no third party.

attestations.statement: Tokens "confer no ownership, voting, dividend, information, or other legal rights" and holders do not appear on the referenced company's cap table.

The ToS reserves freeze, forced transfer, clawback, burn and compulsory redemption without notice or consent; on-chain every mint carries permanentDelegate, freezeAuthority, mintAuthority and pausableConfig, all held by the single key WV9PJN7XTmTLVwbutCLFxp8TyePee6Xq5mRq6Fti5Wc.
Full Terms of Service and Participant Agreement are published, including the Prohibited Jurisdictions list and the Monitoring, Compliance and Enforcement powers.

findings.statement: No incorporated issuer, SPV sponsor or counterparty is named anywhere: the ToS says PreStocks is "a distributed network of contributors", the contracting entity "may differ between products, tokens, jurisdictions, and points in time" and may be replaced "at any time without notice", and the only forum is LCIA arbitration seated in London.

Backing "may take any one or more forms ... including but not limited to a direct or indirect interest in one or more SPVs, funds, feeders, series, nominee, trust, or custodial arrangements; a contractual, participation, profit-sharing, forward" instrument, so a token marketed as backed 1:1 by SPV exposure need not be backed by shares at all.

On delay, blockage, write-down, fraud, default, insolvency, defective title, refused consent or seizure affecting the exposure, "the circulating or maximum mintable supply of the affected Token is not automatically reduced" and the operator "may, but [is] under no obligation to" top up or substitute exposure.
Tokens may be added corresponding to exposure "that we reasonably expect to be acquired, arranged, committed, or obtained in the ordinary course": minting may precede acquisition of the backing.
After a 9-month post-IPO (or 6-month post-M&A) conversion window, "the tokens will expire worthless and will no longer be supported".

The scaledUiAmountConfig authority lets the issuer restate every displayed balance: the OPENAI mint moved from multiplier 1 to 1.4861347 effective 2026-07-17T16:30:00Z, a unilateral +48.6% rebase that the issuer never explained.
Fees are enforced "at the token, smart-contract, or program level" and may be changed "at any time and from time to time, in our sole and absolute discretion, without prior notice".

Every PreStocks mint carries transferFeeConfig with an unbounded maximum fee; the rate was raised from 0 to 50 bps between fee epochs 848 and 1032, and the authority spends its recent transactions on withdrawWithheldTokensFromMint.

Attestation reports were promised at launch; CoinDesk reported on 2026-05-13 that none had been published by the platform or any auditor, and /attestations and /proof-of-reserve both returned 404 on 2026-09-16.
Composition is defined only as an open-ended menu of permitted forms and counterparty legal names are withheld as a matter of policy, so the share-versus-derivative mix is not determinable.

The single key that holds mint, freeze, permanent-delegate and pause authority across all 8 mints transacts through the Squads v4 multisig program, so the concentration is of roles rather than of signers.
The referenced companies are private, so the premium is measured against the issuer's own markPrice. SPACEX traded 22.4% below that mark on 2026-09-16, and no third party publishes a competing price.

The ToS grants no proprietary interest in any SPV, share or asset. In May 2026 Anthropic stated that SPV transfers of its shares are void and that such sellers are "likely either engaged in fraud or offering an investment that may have no value"; ANTHROPIC fell 34-38% and OPENAI 39-46% over the following days.

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Authority keys in practice, 2026-09-16): one key WV9PJN7XTmTLVwbutCLFxp8TyePee6Xq5mRq6Fti5Wc holds mint, freeze, permanent-delegate, pause, metadata and transfer-fee authority on all 8 mints, and is Squads-multisig-controlled (Squads v4 program seen in its transactions, which are mostly withdrawWithheldTokensFromMint fee harvesting). Multisig on signers, fully concentrated on roles.

issuers.name: Remora Markets
issuers.issuerText: Remora Markets (formerly Moose Capital; subsidiary of Step Finance) — WOUND DOWN February 2026
products: rStocks / rTokens: Token-2022 tokens on Solana tracking single US equities — TSLAr (Tesla), NVDAr (NVIDIA), CRCLr (Circle), SPYr (SP500), MSTRr (Strategy) and others, live from 2025-09-02
Metals rTokens — GLDr (gold), SLVr (silver), CPERr (copper), PPLTr (platinum), PALLr (palladium), live from 2026-01-16
issuers.issuingEntity: unknown. No primary source names a legal issuing entity. The platform was 'formerly Moose Capital', acquired by Step Finance in December 2024 and rebranded; Step Finance said it had integrated Moose Capital's team and regulatory licences. The public site never named a company, and its own Terms & Conditions, Whitepaper and KYC Info pages were published as empty stubs (verified in the Wayback capture of 2025-05-16). Note: 'Remora Capital Corporation' (Maryland, SEC CIK 2045370) is a middle-market credit BDC and is NOT related.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: unknown. The About page claimed only an 'Asset management license in premium offshore jurisdictions' and that 'Custodial services [are] managed by Wealth Management providers regulated in UAE'; secondary reporting says Remora was registered in Canada and the UAE. Circumstantial support for the UAE: app.remora.markets is a CNAME to mooseprodapialb-2015871155.me-central-1.elb.amazonaws.com — an AWS load balancer in the UAE (me-central-1) region, whose name preserves the 'Moose' origin. The CNAME target no longer resolves.
issuers.governingLaw: unknown — never published. The /terms-conditions/ page existed but contained no terms.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: unknown / self-asserted only. Claimed an unnamed offshore asset-management licence and UAE-regulated custodial providers; no regulator, licence number, prospectus or exemption was ever published. The platform was not available to users in the United States or Europe pending approvals, and required KYB for business users.
issuers.holderClaim: Undocumented. In practice the holder held a platform-issued token that the operator asserted was backed 1:1 by the corresponding security or metal held through an unnamed regulated custodian, redeemable through the platform for USDC. No terms, prospectus or note conditions were ever published, so the legal nature, ranking and enforceability of the claim are unknown; post-wind-down the operator characterised it as a USDC redemption claim rather than a claim to the share.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: unknown — never named. The About page said only 'Custodial services managed by Wealth Management providers regulated in UAE'. (A prior claim in the rwa-sonar attestations DB naming BitGo, sourced to https://remoramarkets.xyz/proof-of-reserves, could not be corroborated: that domain does not resolve as of 2026-09-16 and no archived copy of such a page was retrievable.)

custodyVerification.frequency: Claimed 'Monthly Proof of Reserve audits' on the About page; no auditor named, no report ever located
custodyVerification.notes: No proof-of-reserve page, report, feed or oracle was found from any primary source. There is no Chainlink PoR feed, no attestation firm named, and no API. Post-wind-down the operator merely asserted that 'all rTokens are still fully backed at a 1:1 ratio' with no supporting evidence. The claim of monthly third-party PoR audits should be treated as unverified marketing, not an attestation.

redemption.eligibility: Originally: hold a Remora platform account (KYC for individuals, KYB for businesses); deposit USDC to mint, redeem through the platform. Post-wind-down: the operator said it was 'developing a redemption process for holders to exchange for USDC', and on 2026-03-02 deployed exit liquidity on Manifest DEX priced at the prior Friday's market close, reachable through the Jupiter and Titan swap routers — i.e. open to any token holder via a DEX rather than a contractual redemption right.
redemption.rails: USDC on Solana (mint and redeem); post-wind-down, a DEX exit-liquidity pool on Manifest routed via Jupiter/Titan

issuers.corporateActions: unknown. The mints carry the Token-2022 scaledUiAmountConfig extension — the same mechanism xStocks uses for rebasing dividends and splits — but the multiplier is 1 with no scheduled change on every mint inspected (TSLAr, NVDAr, GLDr), so no rebasing had ever been applied. No dividend, split or delisting policy was ever published.

pricing.notes: Minting was priced at 'the current price on traditional exchanges' per the platform's own How It Works page — a platform mark, with no named oracle. Arbitrage depended entirely on the platform's mint/redeem window being open to the arbitrageur, which required an account; that window is now closed. The wind-down exit liquidity was priced off the prior Friday's market close, i.e. a stale mark. CoinGecko's 'Remora Markets Tokenized rStocks' category reports a $138.9M aggregate market cap against RWA.xyz's $1.99M distributed asset value for the same platform on the same date — treat all third-party valuation figures for these tokens as unreliable.

venues: Jupiter (aggregator; note the rTokens no longer carry Jupiter's 'stocks'/'rwa'/'equities' tags as of 2026-09-16 — only 'community-assist'/'token-2022'/'unknown')

incidents.summary: Parent Step Finance was compromised: attacker access to executive-team devices allowed stake authority on treasury wallets to be transferred, and 261,854 SOL (~$28.9M at the time; ~$40M including fee wallets) was unstaked and moved out of the project's control. STEP fell roughly 96% over the following weeks. This was a parent-treasury compromise, not a compromise of the rToken mints or of customer collateral as far as reported.

Step Finance announced it would wind down all operations immediately after failing to secure financing or an acquisition — the Step dashboard, SolanaFloor and Remora Markets all shut down. Remora stated all rTokens remained fully backed 1:1 and that it was developing a USDC redemption process for holders.
Remora deployed exit liquidity for rToken holders on Manifest DEX, priced at the prior Friday's market close and accessible through the Jupiter and Titan swap routers.

The remora.markets TLS certificate (Sectigo, CN=remora.markets, issued 2025-03-07) expired and was never renewed. As of 2026-09-16 the apex domain serves a cPanel default placeholder page (/cgi-sys/defaultwebpage.cgi), www.remora.markets has no A record, api./docs. do not resolve, app.remora.markets is a CNAME to an AWS me-central-1 load balancer that no longer resolves, and the alternate domain remoramarkets.xyz does not resolve at all. The Wayback record shows the site had become a bare directory autoindex by 2026-02-25.

Residual but non-zero outstanding supply and holders persist: RWA.xyz shows $1.99M distributed asset value across 6 RWAs, 3,635 holders, $5,267 monthly transfer volume and 85 monthly active addresses. On-chain supplies remain (e.g. TSLAr 1,238.996656657; NVDAr 1,190.998328212; GLDr 138.513547187), so a material number of holders have not exited.

openQuestions: What is the actual issuing legal entity and its jurisdiction? Nothing primary names it. Candidate lead: the former 'Moose Capital' entity, with UAE infrastructure (app.remora.markets CNAME to an AWS me-central-1 load balancer named 'mooseprodapialb') and secondary reporting of Canadian and UAE registration — none of which is a filing.

Is the collateral still actually there? The 1:1 backing claim of 2026-02 has never been evidenced, and ~$2M of rTokens across ~3,600 holders is still outstanding as of 2026-09-16. Who now holds the underlying shares and metals, and under what mandate?
Is the exit-liquidity pool on Manifest still funded and quoting, and at what price relative to the underlying? If it is drained, residual holders have no exit at all.

Who controls the key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb after the wind-down, and was it ever in scope of the January 2026 device compromise? It can still freeze, pause, mint and seize every rToken.

Why does CoinGecko's 'Remora Markets Tokenized rStocks' category report a ~$138.9M aggregate market cap with R-prefixed tickers (RTSLA, RCRCL, RGOOGL, RMU, RINTC) when the on-chain mints use r-suffixed tickers (TSLAr, CRCLr) and RWA.xyz reports $1.99M for the same platform on the same date? At least one aggregator is describing something other than these mints, or using stale/unreliable prices.

The brief's premise that Remora is 'listed on Jupiter's stocks tag' no longer holds: as of 2026-09-16 Jupiter's stocks/rwa/equities tags contain xStocks and Ondo tokens, while the rTokens carry only 'community-assist'/'token-2022'/'unknown'. When were they de-tagged, and by whom?
Did Remora ever publish a single proof-of-reserve report? None was found; if one exists it would materially change thirdPartyAttestations.

Direct DNS and TLS checks on remora.markets, www./app./api./docs.remora.markets and remoramarkets.xyz, 2026-09-16

keyGovernance.evidence: Every rToken mint names the single key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb as mint, freeze, pause, permanent-delegate and metadata authority (RPC getAccountInfo on FJug3z58gssSTDhVNkTse5fP8GRZzuidf9SRtfB2RhDe and the other mints, 2026-09-16). stocks/findings.md characterises no key type for Remora and no multisig evidence was gathered, so all three are recorded unknown rather than asserted to be hot keys.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: No legal documentation was ever published — the Terms & Conditions and Whitepaper pages were empty — so nothing establishes whether the chain or the operator's internal books was the authoritative record of entitlement. Evidence cuts both ways: minting and redemption ran through the platform's account system (suggesting an off-chain book), but the wind-down remedy was open DEX exit liquidity honouring whoever held the token (suggesting ledger state governed). Recorded as unknown rather than guessed.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Verified on Solana mainnet 2026-09-16 for TSLAr, NVDAr and GLDr: defaultAccountState = initialized (accounts are not frozen on creation, so no allowlist) and no transferHook extension at all. The platform itself advertised withdrawing rTokens to your own non-custodial wallet and using them across Solana DeFi. No gatekeeper approval was required for a transfer.

bearerRedemption.reason: Minting and redemption both ran through a Remora platform account subject to KYC (KYB for businesses); holding the token alone never entitled the bearer to the underlying. After the wind-down the only route out is a discretionary exit-liquidity pool on a DEX, priced off a stale mark — a courtesy, not a redemption right, and with no published terms there is nothing to enforce.

forcedTransfers.reason: Verified on-chain: every rToken mint carries a permanentDelegate, a freezeAuthority and a pausableConfig, all set to the single key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb (which is also mint authority, metadata update authority and scaledUiAmount authority). Whoever holds that key can move or burn any holder's tokens without consent. Concentration in one key is itself a risk given the parent's January 2026 device compromise.

titleDeed.reason: The token was marketed as economic exposure to a stock or metal held by a third-party custodian, not as the security itself. No shareholder rights, no register entry, no published instrument conveying ownership.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: The platform's How It Works page instructed users to 'Withdraw your RWAs to your own non-custodial wallet on Solana', and on-chain state confirms ordinary unfrozen Token-2022 accounts. Self-custody works and still works today.

issuerIndependent.reason: Demonstrated empirically, not merely inferred: the issuer wound down in February 2026 and the token's meaning collapsed with it. The web presence is gone (apex domain serves a cPanel placeholder, TLS expired 2026-03-06, alternate domain does not resolve), no proof of reserves is published, no redemption counterparty is contactable, and residual holders are left with a token whose backing rests on an undocumented assertion. The tokens still transfer, but they no longer reliably mean anything.

presetJurisdiction.reason: No governing law, forum or issuing entity was ever disclosed. The strongest published statement was 'Asset management license in premium offshore jurisdictions' with no jurisdiction, regulator or licence named, and the Terms & Conditions page was blank. A holder cannot determine which law governs the claim or where to bring it.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: 'Monthly Proof of Reserve audits' were claimed on the About page but no auditor was ever named, no report was ever published, and no feed or oracle existed. No independent attestation was attached to the token in any form. (The earlier rwa-sonar record asserting BitGo custody, sourced to remoramarkets.xyz/proof-of-reserves, is unsupported — that domain does not resolve.)

aiReady.reason: Per the vocabulary formula: unconditionalTransfers = yes and tokenSelfCustody = yes, so no KYC sits in the transfer loop and an agent could hold and trade rTokens. Largely academic now — with the issuer gone, there is nothing worth holding.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The on-chain mechanism exists (permanent delegate, freeze, pause) but there is no published governing law, no named entity, no forum and no operator still answering — so there is no route by which a court decision could be directed at anyone with the power to act on the ledger. Capability without an accountable holder of that capability is not enforceability.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Secondary transfers settled on the parties' agreement alone, with no issuer or platform sign-off, as verified by the absence of any transfer hook or allowlist on the mints.

attestations.attestor: Remora Markets (How It Works page, archived 2025-03-25)
attestations.statement: The platform described minting against a USDC deposit and withdrawal to a non-custodial wallet, and the TSLAr/NVDAr/GLDr mints carry defaultAccountState=initialized with no transferHook extension, so transfers are permissionless with no allowlist. Marked expired: the site and the operator are gone.

findings.statement: Step Finance wound down Step, SolanaFloor and Remora Markets with immediate effect on 2026-02-23/24 after a 2026-01-31 treasury compromise (261,854 SOL, ~$28.9M). Remora asserted rTokens remained 1:1 backed and offered a USDC exit; the domains no longer resolve while ~$2M across ~3,600 holders remains outstanding on-chain.

Exit liquidity was deployed on Manifest DEX from 2026-03-02 priced at the prior Friday's market close and routable via Jupiter and Titan: an open-market exit at a stale mark rather than a contractual redemption at live value.

No primary source identifies the issuing legal entity, its jurisdiction, its licence or its governing law. The strongest disclosure was an 'asset management license in premium offshore jurisdictions'; holders cannot identify their counterparty.

The Terms & Conditions, Whitepaper and KYC Info pages all existed in the site navigation but contained no content when archived on 2025-05-16. No terms were ever public and the site is now offline entirely.
Marketing claimed 'Monthly Proof of Reserve audits to ensure transparency' but named no auditor and published no report; no PoR page, feed or oracle was located.

The custodian was never named, only 'Wealth Management providers regulated in UAE'. The prior rwa-sonar record naming BitGo custody via remoramarkets.xyz/proof-of-reserves could not be corroborated from any reachable source and the domain is dead.

Every rToken mint names DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb as permanent delegate, freeze authority, pause authority, mint authority and metadata authority. The key is a single unattributed keypair: no named role, entity or governance process was ever published, and the operator has wound down.

keyGovernance.evidence: Every rToken mint names the single key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb as mint, freeze, pause, permanent-delegate and metadata authority (RPC getAccountInfo on FJug3z58gssSTDhVNkTse5fP8GRZzuidf9SRtfB2RhDe and the other mints, 2026-09-16). stocks/findings.md characterises no key type for Remora and no multisig evidence was gathered, so all three are recorded unknown rather than asserted to be hot keys.

(the Republic group parent), sole named director Jeffrey Vier. RepublicX is described by Republic as 'the innovation arm of Republic primarily in the business of providing asset tokenization services'. SpaceX has not reviewed, endorsed, or participated in this offering in any capacity.' This is categorically different from the Bullish/Securitize/Superstate cases — there is no issuer-sponsored tokenization of anything here, and no transfer agent, because there is no share register.

rSpaceX / rSPAX — the first and flagship offering, announced 2025-06-25, referencing SpaceX; minimum $50, maximum initial purchase $5,000, payable by Apple Pay or stablecoin

Announced or listed follow-ons referencing other private companies: OpenAI, Anthropic, Figma, xAI, Cursor, Ramp, Perplexity (a 'Reserve rPerplexity' page exists on republic.com), with Republic stating an intent to cover 20+ companies
