issuers.issuingEntity: RepublicX LLC, Delaware limited liability company, year of incorporation 2025, principal place of business New York, NY. Manager: OpenDeal Inc. (149 5th Ave Floor 10, New York, NY 10010). Director/signatory: Jeffrey Vier. Related group entities on EDGAR: Republic Core LLC (CIK 0001794805, SIC 6199, Reg CF issuer of the Republic Note, files Form C-AR annual reports — its 2026 C-AR and C-AR/A are the only EDGAR documents whose full text mentions 'Mirror Token'). There is NO transfer agent, NO registrar and NO custodian named for the Mirror Notes anywhere in the sources located.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Delaware LLC, operations New York, USA. UK/EU distribution runs through Republic Europe under its own regime.
issuers.governingLaw: US federal securities law for the exempt offerings (Securities Act exemptions — see regulatoryStatus) plus, presumably, Delaware LLC law and New York law for the note instrument. NOT VERIFIED: no note purchase agreement, indenture, subscription agreement, series note agreement or terms of service for the Mirror Notes could be retrieved. republic.com and europe.republic.com returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to every access method attempted from this host, including a headed Chrome over CDP, most likely a geographic block; the Internet Archive was offline on 2026-09-16. So the governing-law clause, the events of default, the valuation methodology and the subordination terms are all unread.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: MIXED AND PARTLY UNRECONCILED — the single most important finding in this dossier. (1) WHAT REPUBLIC SAYS: the June 2025 rSpaceX launch was announced as a Regulation Crowdfunding offering — Republic's own press release cites 'rule 206 of Regulation CF', open globally to non-accredited investors from $50 with a $5,000 initial cap, and secondary press consistently reports Reg CF plus Reg D and Reg S as the framework. (2) WHAT EDGAR SHOWS: RepublicX LLC's ENTIRE SEC filing history is two documents — a Form D filed 2025-12-04 and a Form D/A filed 2025-12-11 (file no. 021-565769), claiming federal exemption item '06c' i.e. Rule 506(c) of Regulation D, security type DEBT, date of first sale 2025-11-28, total offering amount $3,500,000, total sold $585,205, remaining $2,914,795 with the note 'The offering is closed. We do not intend to sell the remaining', minimum investment accepted $50, 199 investors already invested, and hasNonAccreditedInvestors = FALSE. NO FORM C, C/A, C-U or C-AR was filed by RepublicX LLC, and an EDGAR full-text search for 'rSpaceX' across all forms returns ZERO hits. Regulation Crowdfunding requires a Form C filed before any offer is made, so either (a) the Reg CF offerings were made by a different filer not identified here, (b) the Reg CF plan was abandoned and the notes were actually sold under Rule 506(c) to accredited investors only, or (c) there is a filing failure. The Form D's own data — accredited-only, 199 investors, $585k raised — is consistent with (b) and inconsistent with the 'open to all, everyday investors worldwide' framing. This contradiction must be resolved before grading, and it is resolvable only from Republic's own offering pages, which were unreachable. (3) NOT A REGISTERED SECURITY on any view: there is no registration statement, no exchange listing and no transfer agent.
issuers.holderClaim: An UNSECURED DEBT CLAIM ON REPUBLICX LLC, and nothing more. Republic's own description: 'Mirror Notes are an unsecured debt instrument issued by RepublicX LLC (RepublicX) that are designed to mirror the economic outcome of investing in SpaceX, giving you the chance to participate in the potential economic upside (or downside).' The holder owns no share, no equity, no fund unit and no interest in any SPV that holds shares: the token 'offers economic exposure to SpaceX through blockchain without giving equity or ownership rights' and 'does not represent actual ownership or equity in SpaceX'. The referenced company is not a party. Practically this is a synthetic long exposure documented as a note, whose value depends on (i) RepublicX's solvency and willingness to pay, (ii) RepublicX's own determination of 'fair value' at settlement, and (iii) a liquidity event occurring at all. The Form D confirms the instrument type as debt. WHETHER REPUBLICX HOLDS ANY HEDGE is the central unknown: no document located states that RepublicX owns SpaceX shares, SPV interests, forwards or any other backing asset, and 'unsecured' affirmatively indicates the holder has no claim over any such asset even if it exists.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: unknown — and possibly none. No custodian, trustee, collateral agent or SPV is named in any source located. Because the notes are expressly unsecured, any assets RepublicX may hold to hedge its exposure are not pledged to holders and would sit alongside general creditors in an insolvency.

custodyVerification.notes: THERE IS NO VERIFICATION SURFACE AT ALL, ON-CHAIN OR OFF. No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release or accessible page; no transfer agent exists; no reserve, collateral or hedge is disclosed; no auditor attestation, proof-of-reserve or NAV publication was located; and the token's on-chain state could therefore not be read. This is the opposite end of the spectrum from the Bullish and Securitize dossiers, where the mint could be verified even where documentation was thin. NO SOLANA MINT ADDRESS WAS FOUND — searches of the Jupiter token registry for rSPAX, rSpaceX, rOpenAI, rANTHROPIC and 'Mirror' on 2026-09-16 returned only impersonation memecoins, chiefly on the legacy SPL Token program with 1,000,000,000 supplies and pump.fun launchpad tags. The most dangerous of these is 79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x, symbol 'rSpaceX', created 2025-06-25T13:12:44Z — the same day as Republic's announcement — legacy Tokenkeg program, supply 997,884,479.34, 768 holders, launchpad-tagged. It is NOT the security, and its 768 holders are ~4x the 199 investors in RepublicX's actual closed Form D offering. Also present: GgWZbw7ZkcZQj3Jy6kX1m8HRx7D5YYqcoyGcmnjspump ('SPCX'/'rSpaceX', 2025-06-25), Dc3AjVi3At8YBebo3HPhLXcjR4nc9qRdPJCph9fbRPHp ('rSpaceX', 2025-07-08), AfdbLoS6F6Xa6gbrETZ7Jz6hx3aFjjqrJDjmFrr8UuG7 ('rOpenAI', 2025-06-25), plus a cluster of 'preSPAX'/'PreSPAX' Token-2022 mints from April 2026. A genuine restricted Mirror Note mint would plausibly be absent from a DEX aggregator's index precisely because it cannot trade — a 12-month transfer lock and a whitelist would keep it out of every pool — so absence from Jupiter is weak evidence of non-existence, but it also means an outside party has no way to find or audit it. Until RepublicX publishes a canonical address, ANY on-chain token bearing a Mirror Token ticker should be treated as an impersonation.

redemption.eligibility: There is no redemption at the holder's option and no put right located. Payment is contingent on a QUALIFYING LIQUIDITY EVENT of the referenced private company — an IPO, acquisition or similar. Republic: 'When a qualifying liquidity event occurs, RepublicX will distribute the fair value of common shares of the company.' And: 'There is no guarantee of returns, and the timing or likelihood of a liquidity event is not guaranteed.' Republic's own press release warns 'There is no guarantee that the company will ever conduct an IPO.' So the instrument can sit indefinitely with no payment and no exit other than secondary sale.
redemption.rails: At a qualifying liquidity event, 'investors receive payout in USD or USDC'. The amount is 'the fair value of common shares of the company' — determined by RepublicX, with no independent valuation agent, methodology, calculation-agent provision or dispute mechanism disclosed in anything located. Before any liquidity event, the only route out is secondary sale: tokens are 'locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance', after which 'Republic intends to allow trading of tokens on the Republic Secondary Market with other investors'. Republic's June 2025 release framed post-lockup trading as occurring on 'a regulated secondary market' following its then-pending acquisition of INX — i.e. the venue was contingent on a corporate transaction, and whether it is live was not verified.
redemption.minimum: $50 minimum investment (stated in Republic's press release and confirmed independently by the Form D field minimumInvestmentAccepted = 50); maximum initial purchase stated as $5,000 in the June 2025 release

transferRestrictions.mechanism: UNVERIFIED ON-CHAIN — no mint address was found, so none of the following could be confirmed against Solana mainnet, unlike the Bullish and Securitize dossiers. What is stated: (1) a hard 12-month lock — 'Mirror Tokens are locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance' — consistent with the Securities Act resale restrictions that attach to both Reg CF (1-year) and Rule 506(c) securities, and the binding constraint regardless of which exemption actually applied; (2) after unlock, transfers only to other investors on the Republic Secondary Market, a permissioned venue, not open transfer; (3) access control at the token level: Republic describes its Solana security-token standard as including 'access-control functions, meaning only pre-approved wallets can receive or send tokens, with freeze, clawback, and mint and burn functions to ensure legally compliant trading'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THAT LAST POINT: that description was given for Republic's own $NOTE asset (the Republic Note), not specifically for the Mirror Notes. It is a reasonable inference that the same 'Republic-created security token asset standard' governs the Mirror Tokens, and Republic says the Mirror Tokens use that standard — but it is an inference, and the specific extensions, authorities and hook programs are unread.

issuers.corporateActions: None flow to the holder, by design — this is a note referencing a company that is not a party to it. No dividend, distribution, voting, proxy, information or inspection right in the referenced company attaches: the instrument 'offers economic exposure ... without giving equity or ownership rights'. The referenced company's corporate actions matter only as inputs to the eventual 'fair value of common shares' calculation, and nothing located explains how a stock split, recapitalisation, down-round, secondary tender, partial acquisition, SPAC merger, direct listing or dissolution of the referenced company would be treated, nor what happens if a 'liquidity event' is partial or is for a different class of shares than the one referenced. On the RepublicX side the disclosed token-level capabilities (freeze, clawback, mint, burn) are administrative rather than corporate-action mechanisms. This is the largest documentation gap in the instrument after collateral: for a structured note, the calculation-agent and adjustment provisions are the product, and none were readable.

pricing.notes: There is no reference market. The referenced companies are private, so there is no exchange price, no NBBO and no continuous mark — the very feature that creates demand for the product removes any pricing anchor. Value is whatever RepublicX determines the 'fair value of common shares' to be at a liquidity event, with no disclosed valuation methodology, no independent calculation agent, no NAV publication and no oracle. Arbitrage is structurally impossible: there is no underlying an arbitrageur can buy or short (private-company stock is not freely obtainable), no redemption mechanism to trade against, and no transfers at all for the first 12 months. Any post-lockup secondary price on the Republic Secondary Market would be a supply-and-demand print inside a single permissioned venue, not a price disciplined against anything. Note the practical consequence for grading: the 'mirror' in Mirror Token describes an intention, not an enforced tracking mechanism, and no document located obliges RepublicX to hedge, to mark, or to track within any tolerance.

venues: None for the first 12 months after issuance — 'Mirror Tokens are locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance'.

Republic Secondary Market, post-lockup, permissioned — 'After the unlock, Republic intends to allow trading of tokens on the Republic Secondary Market with other investors.' Note 'intends to'. Republic's June 2025 release tied post-lockup trading to 'a regulated secondary market' following its then-pending acquisition of INX; whether that venue is live for Mirror Notes was not verified.
No DEX, AMM, lending market or DeFi integration was found, and none would be expected while transfers are restricted to pre-approved wallets.
NOT a venue: the pump.fun impersonation mints trading under Mirror Token tickers on Solana DEXs (see custodyVerification). Those are unrelated memecoins.

incidents.summary: REGULATORY-PATH CONTRADICTION found by rwa-sonar. Republic announced and marketed the Mirror Tokens as a Regulation Crowdfunding product open to everyday investors worldwide from $50 (its own press release cites 'rule 206 of Regulation CF'), but RepublicX LLC's complete SEC filing history consists of a Form D and Form D/A claiming Rule 506(c) of Regulation D, security type debt, with hasNonAccreditedInvestors = FALSE, 199 investors, $585,205 sold of a $3,500,000 offering, first sale 2025-11-28, and the offering marked closed. No Form C, C/A, C-U or C-AR exists for RepublicX LLC, and EDGAR full-text search for 'rSpaceX' across all forms returns zero results. Reg CF cannot lawfully proceed without a Form C on file. Either the Reg CF distribution was made by an unidentified filer, or it was abandoned in favour of an accredited-only 506(c) private placement, or a filing obligation was missed. Nothing located resolves it, and the primary pages that would are geo-blocked from this host. This is the finding that most affects how the product should be graded and described.

SAME-DAY IMPERSONATION. Within hours of Republic's rSpaceX announcement, at least three Solana memecoins appeared using Mirror Token tickers — 'rSpaceX' (79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x, 13:12 UTC, now 768 holders), 'SPCX'/'rSpaceX' (GgWZbw7ZkcZQj3Jy6kX1m8HRx7D5YYqcoyGcmnjspump, 13:32 UTC) and 'rOpenAI' (AfdbLoS6F6Xa6gbrETZ7Jz6hx3aFjjqrJDjmFrr8UuG7, 15:58 UTC) — each a 1-billion-supply launchpad token on the legacy SPL Token program. The impersonation mint has roughly four times as many holders as RepublicX's actual closed offering had investors (199). Not an incident at Republic, but a direct consequence of never publishing a canonical mint address, and the reason a retail investor searching for 'rSpaceX' on Solana will find a memecoin first. Bullish, by contrast, publishes its address and states that 'tokens claiming to represent BLSH from any other contract address are fraudulent'.

No exploit, default, missed payment, enforcement action, SEC comment letter, freeze event or clawback was found for the Mirror Notes as of 2026-09-16. Note this is weak evidence in both directions: the product has no on-chain surface an outsider can monitor, no transfer agent, no published reserve and no liquidity event has occurred, so the ordinary failure modes have not yet been reachable. Absence of a found incident is not proof there was none.

openQuestions: IS THERE A MIRROR NOTE TOKEN LIVE ON SOLANA MAINNET AT ALL, AND AT WHAT ADDRESS? This dossier could not verify a single on-chain fact. Republic states the tokens are 'minted on the Solana blockchain using a Republic-created security token asset standard', but no address is published, the Jupiter registry contains only impersonators, and republic.com is geo-blocked from this host. A restricted, non-tradable security token would legitimately be absent from a DEX aggregator, so this is not evidence of non-existence — but it does mean the tokenization is, from outside, entirely unaudited. NEXT STEP: retrieve republic.com/mirror and republic.com/rspax from a US IP (or ask Republic directly), then read the mint with getAccountInfo to establish token program, extensions, authorities, supply and holder count. Until then treat the on-chain layer as unverified rather than as present.

REG CF OR REG D? Marketing says Regulation Crowdfunding, open to non-accredited investors worldwide from $50. EDGAR shows only Form D / Form D/A under Rule 506(c) with hasNonAccreditedInvestors FALSE, 199 investors and $585,205 raised, and NO Form C for RepublicX LLC (CIK 0002080279) — while Reg CF requires a Form C before any offer. Three candidate explanations: the Reg CF offerings were filed by an unidentified affiliate; the Reg CF plan was abandoned for an accredited-only private placement; or a filing obligation was missed. This determines who could lawfully buy, what resale restrictions apply, and whether ongoing Form C-AR reporting is owed. Check for Form C filings by other OpenDeal Inc. entities and confirm with Republic.

DOES REPUBLICX HOLD ANYTHING? No source states whether RepublicX owns SpaceX shares, SPV interests, forwards, options or any hedge against the exposure it has sold. The notes are expressly unsecured, so holders have no claim on such assets even if they exist — but the difference between a hedged note and a naked short position in a private company's equity is the difference between a funded obligation and an unfunded one. A Delaware LLC formed in 2025 that raised $585,205 has written notes whose payout could be a large multiple of that if the referenced company appreciates. How is the obligation funded?

HOW IS 'FAIR VALUE' CALCULATED, AND BY WHOM? 'RepublicX will distribute the fair value of common shares of the company' is the entire payout term located. No methodology, no independent calculation agent, no adjustment provisions, no dispute mechanism. For a note referencing an illiquid private security this is the product. Obtain the note purchase agreement or series note agreement.

WHAT IS A 'QUALIFYING LIQUIDITY EVENT', AND WHAT IF NONE OCCURS? IPO and acquisition are mentioned. Is a direct listing, SPAC merger, tender offer, secondary sale round, partial acquisition, recapitalisation or change of control included? Is there a maturity date, a long-stop date, or does the note simply persist indefinitely? Republic warns 'There is no guarantee that the company will ever conduct an IPO' without saying what then happens to the note.

IS THE POST-LOCKUP SECONDARY MARKET ACTUALLY LIVE? Republic 'intends to allow' trading on the Republic Secondary Market after 12 months, and the June 2025 release tied a 'regulated secondary market' to Republic's then-pending acquisition of INX. rSpaceX notes issued in June 2025 unlocked around June 2026; those in the Form D offering (first sale 2025-11-28) unlock around November 2026. Whether any Mirror Note has ever actually traded, where, at what price and under whose regulatory permission is unverified — and it is the test of whether this is a tokenized security or a database entry.

WHICH ENTITY AND WHICH REGIME APPLIES TO EUROPEAN HOLDERS? Republic Europe (formerly Seedrs) offers 'RepublicX Mirror Notes' through a separate channel. Is the issuer still RepublicX LLC, or a European entity? Is the instrument the same note? Is the same Solana token used? Are the lock-up and payout terms identical? Conflating the two channels would produce a wrong grade.

HOW MANY MIRROR NOTE SERIES EXIST AND WHAT IS OUTSTANDING? Republic has announced or listed references to SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Figma, xAI, Cursor, Ramp and Perplexity with an intent to cover 20+ companies. Only ONE offering appears on EDGAR ($3.5M offered, $585,205 sold, closed). Are the other series unfiled, filed elsewhere, offered only outside the US, or not yet launched? Is each series a separate token, and does each have its own claim on RepublicX or do they share one balance sheet?

WHO ARE THE 768 HOLDERS OF THE IMPERSONATION MINT, AND DOES REPUBLIC KNOW? 79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x ('rSpaceX', created within hours of the announcement) has roughly four times as many holders as RepublicX's actual offering had investors. No Republic warning about impersonation mints was located. Publishing canonical addresses would cost nothing and would be the single highest-value disclosure improvement available to this issuer.

DOES THE TOKEN STANDARD REALLY CARRY FREEZE AND CLAWBACK FOR THE MIRROR NOTES? The 'access-control ... freeze, clawback, and mint and burn' description is Republic's own, but was published for the $NOTE asset. Whether the Mirror Note mints implement it — and via which Token-2022 extensions or hook program — is unread, which is why forcedTransfers and reflectLegalDecisions are scored 'unknown' rather than 'yes' here while their equivalents are 'yes' for Bullish and Securitize.

METHODOLOGICAL NOTE FOR THE MAINTAINER: this dossier is graded 'low' confidence because the issuer's own primary pages were unreachable from this host (HTTP 403, Cloudflare, consistent with a geographic block, reproduced across WebFetch, curl with a browser UA, and a headed Chrome over CDP) and the Internet Archive was offline on 2026-09-16. Everything sourced from republic.com or europe.republic.com below is quoted via search-engine indexing of those pages rather than direct retrieval, and should be re-verified. The SEC Form D data and the Solana registry reads are first-hand and reliable.

Solana mainnet / registry reads by rwa-sonar on 2026-09-16: Jupiter token-registry searches for rSPAX, rSpaceX, rOPENAI, rANTHROPIC and 'Mirror' returned no genuine RepublicX instrument, only legacy-SPL and Token-2022 launchpad memecoins. NO Solana JSON-RPC read of any Mirror Note mint was possible because no address was found.

keyGovernance.evidence: No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release or accessible page, and none was located in the token registries, so no authority key could be read from the chain (stocks/findings.md, Republic Mirror entry). Republic describes its own standard as carrying freeze, clawback, mint and burn functions, but nothing ties those powers to an identified key.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Nothing states or implies that the chain is the legal record, and the structure argues against it. This is an unsecured note of a private Delaware LLC: the obligation exists under the note agreement and the holder's entitlement is recorded on RepublicX's own books. There is no transfer agent, no registrar and no register of any kind disclosed; transfers are locked for 12 months and then permitted only inside Republic's own permissioned secondary market; and the token standard is described as giving RepublicX freeze, clawback, mint and burn powers over holders' balances. A ledger the issuer can rewrite at will, gating a claim documented off-chain, is a convenience layer. Note also the asymmetry with the equity cases: for a registered share there is at least a contest between a transfer agent's register and the chain. Here there is no competing register to point to — which means the on-chain balance is not authoritative and nothing else is published either.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: The most restricted of the three issuers examined, on three independent grounds. (1) An absolute 12-month prohibition: 'Mirror Tokens are locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance' — this follows from the Securities Act resale restrictions attaching to both Reg CF and Rule 506(c) securities, so it holds whichever exemption actually applied. (2) After unlock, transfer is not free but confined to Republic's own permissioned venue: 'Republic intends to allow trading of tokens on the Republic Secondary Market with other investors' — note 'intends to', and note that whether the venue is live for Mirror Notes is unverified. (3) Token-level access control: Republic's Solana security-token standard is described as having 'access-control functions, meaning only pre-approved wallets can receive or send tokens'. Caveat on the evidence: none of this could be verified on-chain because no mint address was found, and the access-control description was given for Republic's $NOTE asset and inferred to the Mirror Tokens.

bearerRedemption.reason: There is no redemption at all, let alone bearer redemption. No put right and no holder-initiated exit exists. Payment happens only if and when a qualifying liquidity event occurs at the referenced private company — 'When a qualifying liquidity event occurs, RepublicX will distribute the fair value of common shares of the company' — and Republic itself warns 'There is no guarantee that the company will ever conduct an IPO' and that 'the timing or likelihood of a liquidity event is not guaranteed'. Presenting the token to any third party gets nothing: no third party has any obligation under it, least of all the referenced company, which 'has not reviewed, endorsed, or participated in this offering in any capacity'.

forcedTransfers.reason: Claimed but not verifiable. Republic describes its Solana security-token standard as including 'freeze, clawback, and mint and burn functions to ensure legally compliant trading', which would supply the mechanism for court-ordered seizure, theft recovery, loss recovery and inheritance. Two problems prevent scoring it 'yes'. First, that description was published for Republic's own $NOTE asset rather than specifically for the Mirror Notes, so its application here is inference. Second and decisively, no mint address was located, so nothing could be checked against Solana mainnet — unlike Bullish and Securitize, where the permanent delegate and freeze authority were read directly off the mint. Recorded as unknown rather than yes on the principle that an unverified capability is not a capability. Note that even if present, the powers would be exercised by a single private LLC with no named role, no disclosed policy and no regulated registrar, which is a materially weaker governance posture than an SEC-registered transfer agent holding the same keys.

titleDeed.reason: Emphatically not, and the issuer says so. The token conveys no ownership of the referenced company: it 'offers economic exposure to SpaceX through blockchain without giving equity or ownership rights' and 'does not represent actual ownership or equity in SpaceX'. What the holder has is a derived, contingent, unsecured contractual claim against RepublicX LLC — a debt note whose payout references a third party's share value. Nor is it a title to anything RepublicX holds, since the note is unsecured and no backing asset is even disclosed. This is the cleanest 'no' in the set and the structural difference from the Bullish and Securitize dossiers, where the token IS the registered share.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Not established. Republic's press release says investments can be made 'with investments as small as $50 using Apple Pay or stablecoin', which is a consumer-platform onboarding flow and is at least consistent with the position being held in a Republic-hosted wallet; on the other hand the token is described as living on Solana under a standard with pre-approved-wallet access control, which is consistent with self-custody in a whitelisted address. No document located states which, no wallet instructions were readable, and with no mint address the distribution of holdings across accounts could not be inspected. Left unknown rather than guessed.

issuerIndependent.reason: Total dependence on a single counterparty, and more so than in any other structure examined. RepublicX LLC is a Delaware LLC formed in 2025 with no disclosed capital, no transfer agent, no trustee, no collateral and no independent calculation agent. If it disappears the token means nothing: the payout is its unsecured promise, the 'fair value' determination is its own, the secondary market is its affiliate's, and the token's transferability depends on its access-control keys. The Form D shows an entity that raised $585,205 and closed the offering early ('We do not intend to sell the remaining'), against notes whose eventual payout could be many multiples of subscription value if the referenced company appreciates — with nothing located to indicate how that obligation would be funded. Compare the equity cases: there, the SHARE survives the platform's failure even when the TOKEN does not. Here, nothing survives.

presetJurisdiction.reason: The applicable legal framework is identifiable even though the instrument's own terms were not readable: a Delaware LLC with New York offices, a US federal securities exemption claimed on the public record (Form D, Rule 506(c), file no. 021-565769), a named manager (OpenDeal Inc.) and a named signatory (Jeffrey Vier), with a separate and clearly demarcated UK/EU channel through Republic Europe. A US holder would know which courts and which regulator to approach. Marked 'yes' on that basis, but with two real qualifications: the governing-law clause of the note itself is unread because the offering pages are geo-blocked; and the regulatory characterisation is internally contradicted — marketed as Reg CF, filed as Reg D 506(c) — so which exemption governs the securities-law treatment of any given holder's notes is genuinely unclear.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent exists anywhere in the structure, and this is the most complete absence in the set. No transfer agent, no trustee, no custodian, no auditor report on the notes, no proof-of-reserve, no NAV or valuation publication, no independent calculation agent, no smart-contract audit, no published mint address and no on-chain metadata to attach anything to. Every fact about the instrument — its backing, its value, its outstanding amount, its holder list — is RepublicX's unverified assertion. The referenced companies explicitly disclaim involvement, which removes the one party who could authenticate the economic reference.

aiReady.reason: Fails on every limb. Transfers are prohibited outright for 12 months, then restricted to a permissioned affiliate venue among vetted investors; the token standard is described as permitting only pre-approved wallets to send or receive; and subscription runs through a retail investment platform's KYC/AML onboarding with per-investor purchase caps ($5,000 initial), which is exactly the kind of identity and suitability gate an autonomous agent cannot pass. Fails on unconditionalTransfers regardless.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: Cannot be established. The mechanism may exist — Republic's token standard is described as including freeze and clawback — but it is unverified on-chain and only inferred to apply to the Mirror Notes, and no contractual undertaking to honour judicial or regulatory orders was readable, because the note agreement and offering pages could not be retrieved. There is also no regulated intermediary in the structure carrying such obligations by operation of law: no transfer agent means no Exchange Act §17A duties, no Rule 17Ad-17 lost-holder obligations and no escheat process. Note the countervailing point that keeps this from being a 'no': a plain unsecured note of a Delaware LLC is an ordinary contractual claim that US courts can adjudicate and garnish by conventional means — the legal system can reach the CLAIM even if nobody can demonstrate it can reach the TOKEN.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Buyer-and-seller agreement is worth nothing here for a full year, and little after. For 12 months no transfer is permitted on any terms. Afterwards, Republic 'intends to allow' trading on its own secondary market among vetted investors, with pre-approved wallets on the token side — so the counterparty set, the venue and the permission all sit with the issuer's group, not with the parties. Two willing counterparties cannot effect a valid transfer of a Mirror Note by agreeing to one.

attestations.statement: The issuer states plainly that holders get no equity and no ownership: the token 'offers economic exposure to SpaceX through blockchain without giving equity or ownership rights' and 'does not represent actual ownership or equity in SpaceX'. Reinforced by the affiliation disclaimer: 'rSPAX Mirror Notes are not issued by, sponsored by, or affiliated with SpaceX. SpaceX has not reviewed, endorsed, or participated in this offering in any capacity.'

attestations.attestor: RepublicX LLC (SEC Form D and product description)
attestations.statement: The priority is disclosed at the level of a label - 'Mirror Notes are an unsecured debt instrument issued by RepublicX LLC' - and the Form D independently confirms the security type as debt (isDebtType true). Recorded unknown because no legal opinion, indenture or note agreement setting out subordination, ranking against other RepublicX creditors, events of default or remedies could be retrieved.

The core claims are published by the issuer - unsecured debt instrument of RepublicX LLC, no equity or ownership rights, no affiliation with the referenced company, Solana, a proprietary security-token standard, $50 minimum and $5,000 initial cap, 12-month lock, payout of 'fair value of common shares' in USD or USDC at a qualifying liquidity event - and the affiliation disclaimer is unusually prominent and correct. The two claims that matter most for grading are not published anywhere located: the canonical mint address, and whether any asset backs the note.

findings.statement: RepublicX publishes no mint address in any SEC filing, press release or retrievable page, so no outside party can audit the token's supply, extensions, authorities or holder distribution, and the ticker namespace has been captured by impersonators. The top Solana result for 'rSpaceX' is 79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x, a legacy-SPL one-billion-supply pump.fun token created on the announcement day with 768 holders - roughly four times the 199 investors in the actual closed offering.

Marketed as Regulation Crowdfunding, 'open to all', 'everyday investors worldwide', $50 minimum (citing 'rule 206 of Regulation CF'); filed as Rule 506(c) of Regulation D with hasNonAccreditedInvestors false, 199 investors, $585,205 of $3,500,000 sold, offering closed, and no Form C anywhere in EDGAR for the filer. Reg CF requires a Form C before any offer.

RepublicX LLC has filed no offering circular (Form 1-A), no Form C offering statement, no registration statement and no periodic report. Its entire filing history is two Form D notices, which are 15-question notices of sale carrying no risk factors, no financial statements and no description of the instrument.

The holder's claim is an unsecured obligation of RepublicX LLC itself, a Delaware LLC formed in 2025 whose manager is the Republic group parent. There is no SPV, trust, segregation or ring-fence; any assets RepublicX may hold to hedge are neither disclosed nor pledged, so on insolvency holders would rank with general creditors over a pool whose contents are unknown.

No reserve is disclosed, so none is verified: no proof-of-reserve, auditor attestation, NAV publication or reserve-composition statement for the Mirror Notes was located, and no source states that RepublicX holds any shares, SPV interests or forwards at all.

No custodian, trustee or collateral agent is named anywhere located, and because the notes are expressly unsecured holders would have no claim over such assets even if they exist. Whether "mirror" is backed, hedged or wholly synthetic is the single largest unknown in the instrument.

The sole determinant of what a holder receives is RepublicX's own determination of 'the fair value of common shares of the company' at a qualifying liquidity event, in USD or USDC. No independent calculation agent, no valuation methodology, no adjustment provisions for splits or multi-class events, no fallback if no event occurs, no maturity date and no dispute mechanism. The party that owes the money decides how much is owed.
No NAV, mark, indicative value or valuation methodology is published at any cadence. For a structured note this is the product, and it is unreadable.

The referenced companies are private, so there is no market price to feed and no oracle was located. This is the structural reason the "mirror" is an intention rather than an enforced tracking mechanism.

Investors subscribe through the Republic platform with per-investor caps, which entails identity verification, and the filed Rule 506(c) exemption requires reasonable steps to verify accredited status. But no KYC policy, provider, sanctions-screening commitment or accreditation-verification method was published, and the accredited-verification requirement sits oddly with marketing aimed at everyday investors.

Republic describes its Solana security-token standard as carrying 'freeze, clawback, and mint and burn functions to ensure legally compliant trading', but no mint address was located, so the authority public keys are unknown and no role, officer, escalation path or key-management arrangement is disclosed. If present, the powers sit with a single unregulated private LLC.

Republic maintains public product and offering pages that search indexing shows contain substantive terms (the unsecured-note characterisation, the 12-month lock, the liquidity-event payout, USD/USDC settlement). Every one returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) from this host to WebFetch, to curl with a browser user agent and to a headed Chrome over CDP on 2026-09-16, and the Internet Archive was offline the same day. A limitation of this review, not a finding against Republic; re-attempt from a US IP before grading.

keyGovernance.evidence: No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release or accessible page, and none was located in the token registries, so no authority key could be read from the chain (stocks/findings.md, Republic Mirror entry). Republic describes its own standard as carrying freeze, clawback, mint and burn functions, but nothing ties those powers to an identified key.

issuers.name: Securitize SECZ
issuers.issuerText: Securitize Corp. (NYSE: SECZ) — the securities issuer is the listed company itself (Delaware corporation, SEC CIK 0002094496), which is also its own tokenization platform, its own SEC-registered transfer agent (Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC) and the operator of the broker-dealer/ATS that gates access. This vertical integration is the defining feature of the structure: there is no independent transfer agent anywhere in the stack, unlike Superstate (where an independent Recordkeeping Transfer Agent holds the master file) or Bullish (where Equiniti is still a third party until Q1 2027).
chains: Avalanche (larger deployment per the S-1; contract not verified here)

Securitize states native integration with 21 chains — Ethereum, Avalanche, Polygon, Optimism, Arbitrum, XDC, Base, InkChain, ZkSync, Mantle, Hedera, BNB, Linea, Sei, Tron, Aptos, Solana, XRP Ledger, Cronos, Injective and SUI — with 'Tokenization on other blockchains ... being explored' for SECZ specifically
products: Tokenized SECZ — 'a natively tokenized version of our common stock', enabled on the Closing Date of the business combination (2026-07-01) and live from the NYSE listing (2026-07-02), issued on Solana and Avalanche. 'Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class.'

Solana deployment — Token-2022 mint 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED, created 2026-06-29, supply 148,998 tokens across 117 token accounts on 2026-09-16. 'Trading of Tokenized SECZ on Solana is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners.'

Avalanche deployment — the larger of the two; 'certain shares of Tokenized SECZ on Avalanche are held by persons who have executed lock-up agreements pursuant to terms of the Business Combination Agreement'. Contract address not verified by rwa-sonar (out of Solana scope).
Announced follow-on (2026-08-20 press reporting, unverified): SECZ used as collateral in Solana on-chain credit markets.
issuers.issuingEntity: Securitize Corp., a Delaware corporation (EDGAR CIK 0002094496, SIC 6199 Finance Services), formed via the business combination of Cantor Equity Partners II, Inc. ('CEPT'), Securitize, Inc. ('Old Securitize') and Securitize Holdings, Inc. under a Business Combination Agreement dated 2025-10-27, consummated 2026-07-01 after stockholder approval on 2026-06-29. NYSE listing certified 2026-07-01 (Form CERT), 8-A12B filed 2026-06-30, first trade 2026-07-02. Register maintained by Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC — SEC Transfer Agent File No. 084-06638, CIK 0001782266, with a live filing history (TA-1 through TA-1/A and annual TA-2s). Access gated by the group's SEC-registered, FINRA-member broker-dealer and ATS.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Delaware corporation, principal operations United States. All regulated entities in the stack are SEC-registered/FINRA-member US entities.
issuers.governingLaw: Delaware General Corporation Law governs the common stock and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing, the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21) and the broker-dealer/ATS gating access. No separate token terms of service or holder agreement for Tokenized SECZ was located; the operative public instrument is the Form S-1 prospectus risk factor plus the Securitize platform's general investor terms (not located in tokenized-SECZ-specific form).
issuers.regulatoryStatus: The most heavily regulated of the three Solana-native issuers examined, and the only one where the tokenization vendor is itself the registrant. The underlying security is registered common stock of a Delaware SEC-reporting company listed on the NYSE (S-4 registration statement effective 2026-06-05; S-1 filed 2026-07-31, EFFECT 2026-08-07; 424B3 prospectuses 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-13). Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638). The S-1 describes the group as 'the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration'. Access to the tokenized form is intermediated by a regulated broker-dealer: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer' (note: the S-1 renders the entity name as 'Securities Markets, LLC'; Securitize's broker-dealer is publicly known as Securitize Markets, LLC, so this is most likely a typographical error in the filing — flagged, not resolved). No exemptive relief or no-action letter for the tokenized form was located; the S-1 warns that 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations'.
issuers.holderClaim: The holder owns the actual registered common share. The S-1 risk factor is unambiguous on two points at once: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class' and 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'. The issuer's own press release adds that this is an 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE' and that 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Holders may move between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. There is no SPV, receipt or nominee layer in the legal structure — but access runs through a broker-dealer's onboarding, so whether the holder is a registered holder of record in their own name or a customer of the broker-dealer is NOT established by any document located, and this is the central unresolved question for this issuer.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: No custodian is interposed for the security itself — the token is the share and the register is Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC's master securityholder file. For its own corporate digital assets Securitize discloses self-custody via Fireblocks MPC ('enables us to retain exclusive control over the authorization of transactions without ever generating or storing a traditional private key'), and states that 'In the case of Securitize-issued tokenized securities held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure, Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Investor-side custody may be self-custody (see transferRestrictions) or broker/custodian-held; the split is not disclosed.

custodyVerification.agent: Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC (SEC-registered transfer agent, File No. 084-06638, CIK 0001782266) — an affiliate of the issuer, not an independent party
custodyVerification.frequency: continuous, claimed — 'every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time'; multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file to ensure that total outstanding units remain consistent and singular across chains'
custodyVerification.notes: NO PUBLIC VERIFICATION FEED. Securitize publishes no instruments API, no per-token supply endpoint, no allowlist enumeration and no reconciliation report for SECZ. The token's TokenMetadata URI (https://metadata.securitize.io/secz.json) resolves but contains only name, symbol, description and image — no CUSIP/ISIN, no register link, no supply, no attestation. The Securitize Connect API (https://sec-connect-api-docs.securitize.io/wallets) documents the whitelisting mechanism but is an authenticated partner API, not a public verification surface. VERIFIED ON SOLANA MAINNET BY RWA-SONAR, 2026-09-16 (slot ~447535518): mint 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED is a Token-2022 mint, decimals 6, supply 148,998.000000, name 'Securitize Corp.', symbol 'SECZ'; 117 Token-2022 accounts exist for the mint (getProgramAccounts with mint filter); extensions MetadataPointer, PausableConfig, DefaultAccountState=Frozen, PermanentDelegate, ScaledUiAmount, TokenMetadata; NO TransferHook. Authority topology, and this is the notable finding: mintAuthority == freezeAuthority == 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs, and getAccountInfo on that address returns null — a zero-lamport, never-initialized account, which is the signature of a program-derived address used as a CPI signer rather than a funded wallet. That is a MEANINGFULLY BETTER key posture than Bullish, whose mint/freeze authority is a plain funded wallet: it implies a Securitize program mediates minting and thawing. It is not proof — the owning program was not identified, and the separate authority on the extensions (D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS, which holds permanentDelegate, pausable, scaledUiAmount, metadataPointer and tokenMetadata update authority) was not resolved either. MEASURED CONTRADICTION: press coverage (CoinDesk, PRNewswire, RWA.xyz-sourced) reports '$295 million in tokenized shares'. The Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens, worth roughly $1.24M at the ~$8.35 price Jupiter reported on 2026-09-16 — about 0.4% of $295M. Either essentially all of the $295M sits on Avalanche (consistent with the S-1, which puts the locked-up business-combination shares there) or the $295M figure is not comparable to on-chain supply. Any grading that attributes the $295M headline to Solana is wrong by more than two orders of magnitude.

redemption.eligibility: Holders who have completed the broker-dealer onboarding: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The issuer's press release adds that the tokenized form is for 'eligible U.S. investors' subject to 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. Certain Avalanche holdings are additionally subject to business-combination lock-up agreements.
redemption.rails: Bidirectional switching between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. No burn address, no processing time, no fee schedule and no step-by-step process was located in any public document. Because the transfer agent and the platform are the same group, the switch is an internal book movement rather than a coordination between two agents — mechanically simpler than the Superstate peer's DRS route, but also entirely un-auditable from outside.

transferRestrictions.mechanism: program-mediated, per-token whitelist. On-chain: Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so every new SECZ token account is frozen at birth and only the freeze authority (8Twerer..., an apparent program PDA) can thaw it; plus PausableConfig for a global halt. Off-chain: the Securitize Connect API documents wallet whitelisting scoped to a specific token ('adds a wallet address to the whitelist of an specific token', requiring a tokenId, since 'in a given domain there may be multiple tokens'), with wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and a 'not-authorised' response state. Notably the whitelist is NOT tied to a platform-hosted wallet: 'This is not required, as the whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' — a self-custodied address can be whitelisted directly. Contractually: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche holdings carry business-combination lock-ups. US persons are the TARGET market here ('eligible U.S. investors'), which inverts the usual tokenized-equity geofence.

issuers.corporateActions: Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. Emergency halt: PausableConfig on the mint, with no published policy for its use.

pricing.notes: The same class trades on NYSE under SECZ, so a continuous reference price exists, and the token has on-chain liquidity: 'Trading of Tokenized SECZ on Solana is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners', and Jupiter priced the mint at ~$8.35 on 2026-09-16 with a reported holder count of 44 and roughly $1.24M market value. The issuer is candid about the basis risk in its own prospectus: 'the simultaneous existence of both could potentially fragment liquidity across platforms, affect bid-ask spreads (particularly outside NYSE trading hours), and result in price discrepancies between Tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ—especially if arbitrage is limited by operational or regulatory constraints', and 'Blockchain-based trading mechanisms may have significantly less liquidity and volume compared to national securities exchanges, such as NYSE'. Arbitrage is real but constrained twice over: the switch between forms has no published latency, and only broker-dealer-onboarded persons can hold the tokenized side at all, so the arbitrageur set is permissioned. Jupiter reported a -100% 24h volume change on 2026-09-16, i.e. no trades that day — the on-chain market exists but is thin. No oracle price feed for the Solana mint was located.

venues: On-chain liquidity on Solana via unnamed 'on-chain liquidity provision partners' (S-1). Jupiter indexes and prices the mint (isVerified true, tags token-2022/verified), so DEX routing exists — a materially more open venue posture than Bullish, where 'AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled'.
Securitize's own SEC-registered broker-dealer and alternative trading system, 'approved for digital asset securities primary and secondary market trading'.
NYSE — for the non-tokenized common stock.
Avalanche — the larger tokenized deployment; venue arrangements there not examined.
Reported 2026-08-20 but unverified by rwa-sonar: SECZ linked to Solana on-chain credit markets (collateral use).

incidents.summary: Observation by rwa-sonar, not an announced incident: the widely-cited '$295 million of tokenized SECZ' does not correspond to the Solana deployment. The Solana Token-2022 mint held 148,998 tokens on 2026-09-16 (~$1.24M at ~$8.35), i.e. roughly 0.4% of the headline figure, across 117 token accounts. The S-1 places the locked-up business-combination shares on Avalanche, which is the likely home of the balance. The headline figure appears to be a cross-chain (or Avalanche-dominated) total that press coverage attached to the Solana launch; nothing published by the issuer breaks it down per chain. A grader reading '$295M on Solana' would be off by more than two orders of magnitude.
incidents.source: Solana mainnet getTokenSupply and getProgramAccounts on 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED vs https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/07/02/securitize-tokenizes-usd295-million-of-its-own-stock-on-solana-and-avalanche-amid-nyse-debut

incidents.summary: Discrepancy inside the issuer's own prospectus, worth recording as the marketing-versus-instrument split this project exists to arbitrate. The S-1 business section says Securitize 'issues, manages, and records securities natively on-chain — meaning that instead of relying on disconnected systems across brokers, custodians, and clearinghouses, every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time'. The same document's risk factors say multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file', that in a fork 'Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record', and that Securitize keeps 'manual safeguards ... which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent'. The risk factors describe an off-chain control book with the chain as its projection; the business section describes the chain as the ledger. The risk factors are the operative description.

No exploit, freeze event, pause event, forced burn, trading halt, depeg, fork event or reconciliation failure was found for Tokenized SECZ as of 2026-09-16. Note the product is only ~2.5 months old (enabled 2026-07-01). Absence of a found incident is not proof there was none.

documents.title: Securitize Corp. Form S-1, filed 2026-07-31 — THE definitive primary document. Contains the 'tokenization of our common stock' risk factor ('Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class'; broker-dealer onboarding gate; Solana trading via liquidity partners; Avalanche lock-ups; price-discrepancy warning), the blockchain-fork risk factor (control book, master securityholder file, Securitize determines the authoritative chain), the Fireblocks/manual-safeguards disclosure, and the 21-chain integration list.
Securitize Corp. Form 424B3 prospectus, filed 2026-08-07 (registration effective per EFFECT 2026-08-07)
Securitize Corp. Form 8-K filed 2026-07-08 — the business-combination 'super 8-K' (Items 1.01, 2.01, 3.01, 3.02, 3.03, 4.01, 5.01, 5.02, 5.03, 5.05, 9.01) for the Closing on 2026-07-01
Securitize Corp. Form 8-K filed 2026-08-12 with Exhibit 99.1, Q2 2026 earnings release (mentions Solana)
Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC SEC transfer-agent registration filings, SEC File No. 084-06638, CIK 0001782266 (TA-1 plus multiple TA-1/A amendments and annual TA-2 reports)

Securitize press release, 2026-07-02 — 'Tokenizing SECZ: Securitize Brings Its Own Public Stock Onchain at Listing Day'. Names Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC; 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE'; 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.'

Securitize Connect API documentation — Wallets. Documents per-token whitelisting (tokenId required), wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and 'not-authorised', and that 'whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' (i.e. self-custodied addresses can be whitelisted).

SECZ token metadata document referenced by the mint's TokenMetadata extension — resolves, on an issuer-controlled domain, but carries only name, symbol, description and image; no CUSIP/ISIN, no register link, no supply, no attestation

NOT FOUND: no token terms of service or holder agreement specific to Tokenized SECZ; no published Solana or Avalanche contract addresses in any issuer filing or release; no smart-contract audit for the Solana deployment; no reconciliation report or proof-of-register; no public supply/holder API.

openQuestions: MINT ATTRIBUTION IS INFERRED, NOT PUBLISHED. Securitize has published no Solana contract address anywhere located. 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED is attributed on the strength of its TokenMetadata URI pointing at metadata.securitize.io, matching name/symbol, the Token-2022 compliance extension set, a 2026-06-29 creation date (three days before listing) and a registry verified flag. That is strong circumstantial evidence, not issuer confirmation. Given four SECZ-branded impersonation mints on Solana, the single highest-value next step is asking Securitize IR to publish canonical addresses. Treat the address as high-confidence-but-unconfirmed until then.

Where is the $295M? Press reports $295M of tokenized SECZ; the Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens (~$1.24M). The S-1 puts locked-up business-combination shares on Avalanche, so the balance is presumably there — but Securitize publishes no per-chain supply figures and nothing reconciles the headline to the chains. The Avalanche contract address should be identified and its supply read to close this.

Is a tokenized holder a holder of record in their own name, or a customer position behind the group's broker-dealer? This is the most consequential unanswered question for grading, and it determines whether titleDeed really behaves like the Superstate peer's (where the holder's name, address and TIN sit on the register). Access runs through 'the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer', which is the shape of a customer relationship — yet the whitelisting API explicitly supports addresses with no Securitize iD profile, which is the shape of direct registration. Both cannot be the general case.

What is the correct name of the gatekeeping broker-dealer? The S-1 says 'Securities Markets, LLC'; Securitize's broker-dealer is publicly known as Securitize Markets, LLC. Most likely a typo in a registration statement, but it is the entity that controls who may hold the security, and it should be confirmed against the FINRA/SEC BD registration rather than assumed.

Which entity holds the on-chain authorities, and under what program? 8Twerer... (mint + freeze) is an apparent PDA whose owning program was not identified; D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA... (permanent delegate, pause, split, metadata) was not resolved at all. Whether these sit with Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC (the regulated registrar) or with an operating affiliate matters legally, and whether the program has a timelock or multisig gate matters for grading. Fireblocks MPC is disclosed for corporate treasury only.

What are the 117 token accounts? 148,998 tokens across 117 accounts, with Jupiter reporting 44 holders and a top-holders concentration of ~11.7%. How many are investor self-custody wallets versus platform/custodian/liquidity-pool accounts is unknown. getTokenLargestAccounts on the public RPC returned HTTP 429 on 2026-09-16 and should be retried against a paid endpoint.

Who are the 'on-chain liquidity provision partners' on Solana? The S-1 says Solana trading 'is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners' without naming them. Since holding SECZ requires whitelisting, a liquidity pool must itself be whitelisted — so the pool addresses, and whether pool LPs must be onboarded, are open. Jupiter reported zero volume in the 24h to 2026-09-16.

Is SECZ actually live as DeFi collateral? Press of 2026-08-20 reports SECZ linked to Solana on-chain credit markets. Unverified by rwa-sonar. If true it would need an oracle feed (none located) and would raise the same jurisdiction-of-use question the Superstate/Kamino integration raises.

Has the fork policy ever been applied, and who bears the loss? The S-1's fork provisions are the most developed chain-exception policy in this universe, but they allocate authority without allocating loss: nothing states what happens to a holder whose tokens end up on the chain Securitize does not recognise, or who compensates them. Also note the dependency it creates — the tie-break heuristic is whichever fork 'principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' recognise.

How do dividends, proxy voting and splits work for a tokenized holder? Securitize sells 'distributions, dividend issuances' as transfer-agent services and runs them for third-party issuers, but Securitize Corp. pays no dividend, the ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, and no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented. Untested on its own stock. Note the earnout structure (VWAP thresholds of $15/$20/$25 triggering Securitize Earnout Shares over five years from Closing) will cause share issuance that must propagate to the mint — a live, dated test of the control-book-to-chain path.
What is the token-to-nontokenized switch latency and fee? Unpublished, and it is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies.

Has the Solana token program been independently audited? Nothing public ties an audit to this deployment, despite Securitize's scale (BUIDL alone was >60% of its tokenized AUM at 2025-09-30) and its 21-chain integration.
