blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Securitize's own prospectus decides this three times over, against its own marketing. (1) The control book: multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file to ensure that total outstanding units remain consistent and singular across chains' — a master securityholder file that reconciles the chains is by definition above them. (2) The fork policy: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities.' If the issuer picks which ledger is authoritative, the ledger is not authoritative. (3) The manual fallback: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Against this, the business section claims 'every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time', and third-party commentary claims 'a transfer of a SECZ token on Solana or Avalanche constitutes a transfer of the underlying security in the official company records'. The latter may well describe the operational reality — the transfer agent and the chain operator are the same firm, so the propagation is immediate and there is no inter-party reconciliation gap, which is the strongest version of this architecture anyone is running. It is still a control book with an on-chain projection.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Gated at both layers. On-chain: the mint carries DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so any account opened by a non-whitelisted wallet is frozen at birth and cannot receive; only the freeze authority (8Twerer...) can thaw it; and PausableConfig allows a global halt. Off-chain: whitelisting is per-token through the Securitize Connect API, and 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The press release: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Specific Avalanche positions carry business-combination lock-ups on top. The one point in Securitize's favour: there IS on-chain liquidity ('trading ... enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners', Jupiter-routable), so whitelisted-to-whitelisted trading including via pools actually works — better than Bullish, where AMM/DEX trading is disabled outright.

bearerRedemption.reason: Presenting the token to a third party gets you nothing. Switching between tokenized and nontokenized SECZ runs entirely through Securitize's own platform and requires broker-dealer onboarding: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ', but only holders who 'meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC'. No burn address, no process, no timeframe and no fee is published. A holder outside the whitelist holds a token that is frozen at any new address and convertible nowhere.

forcedTransfers.reason: Verified on-chain 2026-09-16 and corroborated in the filing. The mint carries a PermanentDelegate (D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS) able to transfer or burn from any token account without the holder's signature, a freeze authority able to freeze any account, and PausableConfig able to halt every transfer at once. The S-1 describes the institutional counterpart: Securitize keeps 'manual safeguards ... which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent', and reserves the right in a fork to decide the authoritative record and even to migrate assets. So lost keys, theft, inheritance and court-ordered seizure are all addressable — the property that makes a registered-share tokenization legally usable and that no SPV tracker has.

titleDeed.reason: Stated in a registration statement, which is the strongest form this claim takes anywhere in the universe: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class.' And: 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'; 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. The press release: 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE'; 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share.' No SPV, receipt, derivative or tracker layer. Residual gap: no CUSIP/ISIN is published for the tokenized form and the token metadata carries none, so there is no identifier-level cross-check of the kind the Superstate peer provides.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Self-custody is supported at the mechanism level and this is documented rather than inferred: the Securitize Connect API states that whitelisting a wallet to a token 'does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD', so an arbitrary self-controlled address can be whitelisted directly to hold SECZ, and Securitize's own corporate holdings of Securitize-issued tokenized securities are described as 'held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure'. Caveats: (1) conditional — accounts are frozen at birth and only Securitize's whitelisting makes them usable, and it can re-freeze or pause; (2) the press release describes access as being 'through Securitize's regulated platform' and does not mention self-custody, so how many of the 117 token accounts are genuinely investor-controlled versus platform- or custodian-held is unknown.

issuerIndependent.reason: This is the weakest point in the structure and it is structural, not incidental. Securitize Corp. is simultaneously the securities issuer, the transfer agent, the tokenization platform, the broker-dealer and ATS that gate access, and the holder of the on-chain freeze, claw-back and pause authorities. There is no independent party anywhere — no independent recordkeeping transfer agent as in the Superstate peer, no third-party registrar as at Bullish today. If Securitize stops operating, no address can be thawed, no share can be tokenized or de-tokenized, the control book has no other keeper, and the 'manual safeguards' that back up the chain are its own. The SHARE would survive (Delaware common stock of a reporting company, and a successor transfer agent could be appointed); the TOKEN would not. Note the mitigant on key topology: the mint/freeze authority appears to be a program PDA rather than a plain wallet, which is better than Bullish's funded single key — but a program Securitize controls is still Securitize.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unambiguous and documented in a registration statement: a Delaware corporation, US federal securities law, an SEC-registered transfer agent with a public file number (084-06638), an SEC-registered FINRA-member broker-dealer and ATS gating access, and an NYSE listing. The tokenized form is described in the issuer's own S-1 risk factors rather than only in press releases, which means the legal characterisation is made under Securities Act liability. This is the clearest 'yes' of the three issuers examined and the sharpest contrast with Bullish, which publishes no token instrument at all. The one soft spot is forward-looking rather than present: the S-1 itself notes 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations' for tokenized securities.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent is attached to the token and nothing independent is published about it. The mint's TokenMetadata additionalMetadata array is empty and its update authority is a Securitize-side address; the metadata URI carries name/symbol/description/image only. There is no attestation hook, no proof-of-reserve, no published reconciliation between mint supply and the master securityholder file, no smart-contract audit for the Solana deployment, and no public supply or holder API. The structural problem is worse here than elsewhere: with issuer, transfer agent, platform and broker-dealer all in one group, EVERY assertion about the register is first-party. Securitize's financial statements are audited and it is a reporting company, which is real but is not an attestation about the token.

aiReady.reason: KYC sits directly in the transfer loop, and here it is a broker-dealer's onboarding rather than a platform's: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer', with 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. An autonomous agent cannot complete FINRA-member broker-dealer onboarding. Partial mitigation of the same kind the peer has: whitelisting is per-token and does not require a Securitize iD profile, and on-chain liquidity pools are live, so protocol addresses can evidently be whitelisted — but an agent still cannot get itself whitelisted. Fails on unconditionalTransfers regardless.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: Mechanism, obligation and institutional standing all present. Mechanically: PermanentDelegate, freeze authority and PausableConfig allow seizure, reversal, freezing and a market-wide halt without holder consent. Institutionally: the register is kept by an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638) subject to Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21, and the issuer is a reporting company, so lost-securityholder, escheat and regulatory-request obligations attach. Documented policy: the S-1's fork provisions commit the transfer agent to determine the authoritative record 'for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions', and the manual safeguards exist precisely so that ownership records survive on-chain failure. This is the most explicitly articulated chain-exception posture of the three issuers.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Buyer-and-seller agreement is not sufficient: both sides must be whitelisted to the specific token, and a counterparty must first pass a FINRA-member broker-dealer's onboarding. The press release is explicit that tokenization 'does not ... override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche positions are subject to lock-ups that bind regardless of any agreement between the parties. A trade between two already-whitelisted wallets does settle without per-trade sign-off — and on Solana it can even settle through a liquidity pool, which is more than the Bullish peer allows — but the eligible counterparty set is determined by the issuer's own broker-dealer, and because there is no public allowlist a would-be buyer cannot verify their eligibility in advance.

attestations.attestor: US Securities and Exchange Commission (registration record), asserted by Securitize Corp.
attestations.statement: Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC (CIK 0001782266) is a registered transfer agent, SEC File No. 084-06638, with a long live filing history. Critical qualifier for grading: the transfer agent is an affiliate of the issuer, not an independent third party. Satisfied on its face and not to be read as independence.

'On Closing Date, we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class.' Made in a Form S-1 under Securities Act liability, which is a stronger evidentiary posture than a press release.

'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE'; 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' S-1: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. Unresolved: whether the tokenized holder is a holder of record in their own name or a customer position behind the group's broker-dealer.

'While tokenized securities may exist across multiple blockchains through authorized multichain issuance, such deployments are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file to ensure that total outstanding units remain consistent and singular across chains.' Reinforced twice: 'Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record'; and Securitize retains manual safeguards over the records in its capacity as transfer agent.

attestations.attestor: Securitize Corp. (S-1 and Connect API docs)
attestations.statement: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer', implemented as a per-token wallet whitelist. Verified on-chain: the mint carries defaultAccountState=Frozen, freeze authority 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs (an address returning null from getAccountInfo, i.e. an apparent program PDA) and a pausable extension; there is no transfer hook. The whitelist itself is not publicly enumerable.

The gate is a FINRA-member broker-dealer's customer onboarding, a higher bar than platform KYC: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer'. The press release adds onboarding, KYC/AML verification and jurisdictional eligibility checks, and restricts the tokenized form to eligible U.S. investors.

The mint carries a permanent delegate (D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS) able to transfer or burn from any token account without the holder's signature, a freeze authority able to freeze any account, and a pausable extension able to halt all transfers. Corroborated institutionally by the S-1's manual safeguards over ownership records and by the fork provisions under which Securitize may decline to recognise tokens or migrate assets.

The role is named: Securitize acting 'in its capacity as transfer agent', an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638), is the party that controls the records and the safeguards and that would determine which chain is authoritative. Which on-chain key belongs to which entity is not stated, and is recorded separately as a finding.

attestations.attestor: US Securities and Exchange Commission / NYSE / Securitize Corp.
attestations.statement: The underlying security is registered common stock of a Delaware SEC-reporting company listed on the NYSE: S-4 effective 2026-06-05, 8-A12B filed 2026-06-30, NYSE CERT 2026-07-01, S-1 filed 2026-07-31 with EFFECT 2026-08-07 and 424B3 prospectuses filed 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-13. Since the tokenized form is the same class and not a separate security the registration covers it, and uniquely here the tokenized form is described inside the registration statement.

There is no token terms of service or holder agreement specific to Tokenized SECZ. The key rights and restrictions are publicly stated in an SEC registration statement under Securities Act liability - same class, broker-dealer onboarding gate, switchability between forms, Avalanche lock-ups, control book and master securityholder file, fork policy, manual safeguards - and the Connect API docs make the whitelisting mechanism public. Recorded unknown because a disclosure document is not a contract with holders.

Securitize Corp. is an Exchange Act reporting company with audited financial statements in its registration statements and a 10-Q filed 2026-08-13 for the period ended 2026-06-30. Included because, uniquely here, the tokenization platform and the audited registrant are the same entity, so the platform's going concern and control environment are subject to public audit. This attests to the issuer's financials, not to the token register.

Core claims published by the issuer: issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same NYSE-listed common stock; Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC as the SEC-registered transfer agent; Avalanche and Solana; eligible US investors subject to onboarding and KYC/AML; and 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share'. The contract addresses are not published anywhere by the issuer.

The mint and freeze authority 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs returns null from getAccountInfo - zero lamports, never initialized, the signature of a PDA used as a CPI signer - so minting and thawing run through a program rather than a person with a private key. Contrast Bullish's funded system-owned wallet. This establishes program mediation, not constrained governance: the owning program was not identified and its upgrade authority is unknown.

findings.statement: The issuer of the security, the SEC-registered transfer agent that keeps the register, the platform that mints the token, the broker-dealer and ATS that gate access, and the holder of the on-chain freeze, claw-back and pause authorities are all one corporate group: 'the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration'. Positive: no inter-party reconciliation gap. Negative: every assertion about the register is first-party and the entity holding claw-back power is the company whose shares they are.

'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights... Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities.' The tie-break heuristic is the fork recognised by the principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows, and Securitize reserves the right to migrate assets to another fork. Having a policy at all is rarer and better than not having one; the content allocates authority rather than loss, and is decisive evidence against the chain being the main ledger.

Token-2022 pausableConfig is present and active (authority D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS, paused false): a single instruction halts every transfer of the security at once, exercisable without a court, a regulator or a notice period.

Securitize publishes no Solana or Avalanche contract address in any SEC filing or press release located, so attribution of mint 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED rests on its TokenMetadata URI pointing at metadata.securitize.io plus a registry verified flag. The gap is not theoretical: at least four pump.fun memecoins use the SECZ ticker and Securitize branding.

The obligation is stated more explicitly than by either peer - multichain deployments are reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file - but no output is published: no reconciliation report, no attestation, no per-chain supply disclosure and no public API. The one comparison available goes the wrong way: the widely reported $295M of tokenized SECZ cannot be reconciled with a Solana mint holding 148,998 tokens.

No N-of-M threshold, quorum or timelock is disclosed or observable. The apparent PDA shape of the mint/freeze authority is more favourable than a funded hot wallet, but the owning program was not identified, the extension authority was not resolved, and the disclosed Fireblocks MPC arrangement covers corporate treasury rather than these authorities.

The permanent-delegate, pause, split and metadata authority is unattributed: no owning program was identified, no entity or role is tied to the key in any filing, and no key-management arrangement is disclosed for it.

The mint is a stock Token-2022 mint configured by extensions, so no upgradeable program account is visible from the mint - but the authority controlling the extensions can flip the pause flag or change the split multiplier with immediate effect, and the apparent PDA mint/freeze authority implies an upgradeable Securitize program behind it whose upgrade authority was not identified. ScaledUiAmount's newMultiplierEffectiveTimestamp (currently 0) is the only delay primitive present.

No audit report for the Solana SECZ deployment was located. Securitize has issued tokenized securities since 2018 across 21 chains and for BlackRock, Apollo, BNY, Hamilton Lane and KKR, so audit work almost certainly exists, but nothing public ties an audit to the Solana token program behind this mint.

No oracle publisher (Pyth, Chainlink or other) for the Solana SECZ mint was located. Jupiter reported about $8.35 on 2026-09-16 derived from pool liquidity with a -100% 24h volume change, so an on-chain price exists but is thin and aggregator-derived, not an attested feed.

The Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens (about $1.24M, roughly 0.4% of the reported $295M tokenized) and recorded no trades on 2026-09-16. The on-chain market is not usable for price discovery or redemption arbitrage.

The gap is acknowledged and its consequence named but never quantified: the S-1 describes 24/7/365 trading with instant atomic settlement as the aspiration and liquidity fragmentation, wider spreads outside NYSE hours and persistent price discrepancies as the symptom, but never states how long the token-to-nontokenized switch takes.

'While holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ ...' is the whole of the stated right: no process, no burn address, no latency or SLA, no fee and no statement of what happens if the request is refused. The S-1 flags the consequence itself - price discrepancies persist 'especially if arbitrage is limited by operational or regulatory constraints'.

keyGovernance.evidence: RPC getAccountInfo, 2026-09-16 (stocks/findings.md, Securitize entry): the mint and freeze authority 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs returns null - zero lamports, never initialized - which is the shape of a PDA used as a CPI signer, so minting and thawing are program-mediated. The owning program was not identified and its upgrade authority is unknown. The permanent-delegate/pause/split/metadata authority D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS was not resolved, hence unknown.

issuers.issuingEntity: SHIFT DAO LLC, a for-profit series DAO limited liability company. Each product is a separate designated Series of that LLC (Series 12-18 observed) with its own executed Series Operating Agreement; the Company enters each agreement "solely in its limited and non-discretionary capacity as the administrative agent" and is "not a manager, managing member, fiduciary, or controlling person" of the Series. The initial nominee member of each Series is MINS LLC, Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road, Ajeltake Island, Majuro, MH 96960, which "holds its membership interest solely for purposes of facilitating the formation and annual renewal" and "has no economic entitlement or discretionary authority". The Series 17 agreement is digitally signed 2026-04-19 by Robin Van Niekerk on behalf of MINS LLC. No director, officer or operating-company entity is named; the team page lists twelve individuals with no roles and cites backgrounds at the Israel Securities Authority, Tel-Aviv Stock Exchange, Deloitte, Kraken, Flow Traders, Securitize, CheckPoint, Utila and Emurgo, and names SNZ Holding as seed-round lead investor. The entity that actually holds the backing ETFs is not named: the Solution Overview says only that "SHIFT engages with a private entity that holds the backing assets".
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Republic of the Marshall Islands. Formed under the Decentralized Autonomous Organization Act 2022 and governed under the Limited Liability Company Act 1996, with the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act also cited in the Series agreements. Series segregation is asserted under LLC Act s.79. The Principal Office "need not be in the Marshall Islands" and the "Official Online Venue" for member participation is www.Shiftrwa.xyz.
issuers.governingLaw: Laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, stated in both the Terms of Use (s.12) and each Series Operating Agreement (Art. XII.2). Recourse is narrow: after a 30-day notice period a dispute "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution", seated in the RMI, sole arbitrator, English, final and without appeal, and "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction". The Terms of Use separately submit website disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI". Members owe and are owed no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3, DAO Act s.109), and under Art. VI.2 (DAO Act s.111) "no one shall have the right under the LLC Act to demand to separately inspect or copy records" of the Series.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: Unregistered and self-disclaiming, on top of a real company-law registration. The site-wide legal notice states the tokens "have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933 ... or under the securities or financial-instrument laws of any other jurisdiction", that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State", and that the tokens are "not offered, sold, or distributed in the United States or the United Kingdom, nor to any U.S. or U.K. persons or entities; in applicable jurisdictions they are offered only to 'qualified investors,' 'professional clients,' or their equivalent legal analogues". The Terms of Use add that the membership interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law, but purchasers are responsible for assessing their legal status in their jurisdiction". No licence, prospectus, offering document or exemption filing was located in any jurisdiction.
issuers.holderClaim: On paper: a membership interest in a designated Series of SHIFT DAO LLC whose sole purpose is to "acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to" one named index or stock. The Series 17 agreement says "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 says "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", with no voting, management or fiduciary rights. In practice three things break that chain. (1) The issuer's own site-wide legal notice says the opposite: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." (2) The executed Series agreements do not identify the token they govern - membership is obtained by holding a token "created from and constricted by the parameters defined in the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined" - so no published document links the SPL mint that trades on Jupiter to the Series whose treasury holds the asset; the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement compounds this by requiring "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". (3) What the Series is documented to hold is not the referenced equity but a daily-reset leveraged ETF share (Series 17: SPXL, Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3x, ISIN US25459W8626; Series 12: Direxion Daily TSLA X2, ISIN US25460G2865), so exposure to Tesla or the S&P 500 is delivered through a third party's derivative fund. Graded as derivative for that reason; if the Series agreements' "owners in the Series Assets" language controlled and were bound to these mints, the record would move to spv-claim-redeemable.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: Two custodians are named, in the Risk Disclosure only: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets." The Collateral & Custody page adds that backing is held "with FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners" in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" and "off-balance-sheet". Marketing and press name Alpaca Markets as the brokerage rail. The holding entity itself is not named ("a private entity that holds the backing assets"), nor is the market maker that operates the B2B mint/burn endpoints, and no account, statement, holdings report or balance for any Series has been published.

custodyVerification.agent: Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves is claimed as the verification agent; no feed, contract or report was located
custodyVerification.frequency: claimed continuous - "The feed publishes the verified reserve state on-chain, every block" - but nothing observed at any cadence
custodyVerification.notes: Claimed, not evidenced. The docs assert Chainlink PoR "runs continuously, verifying that every Series Token in circulation is backed 1:1" and that "the SHIFT smart contract cannot issue tokens in excess of verified reserves; mint operations are gated by PoR feed". Verified 2026-09-16: the PoR dashboard link on that same page reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", the third-party attestation section reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", the app dashboard the page points to resolves to https://app.shiftrwa.xyz/coming-soon, and no Chainlink PoR feed naming SHIFT could be found. The earlier marketing site states PoR is "coming with mainnet". The on-chain record contradicts the gating claim outright: every observed issuance is a bare SPL Token-2022 mintTo signed by the mint's own authority keypair plus a fee payer, with no SHIFT program, oracle account or PoR account in the transaction at all.

securityInterest.holder: none - no charge, pledge, lien or security agent is created; the Series is documented as owning its treasury outright under LLC Act s.79 segregation

redemption.eligibility: Contradicted between primary documents. Each Series Operating Agreement grants a member a redemption right: "If a Member wishes to transfer their token back to the Series in exchange for funds, this is an internal membership-interest repurchase ... This transaction is available only to Members processed by smart contract where the transaction is settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet, not using any third-party assets." The Technical Overview says the opposite: "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly. Mint and burn are B2B endpoints used by professional market makers to maintain inventory. Users acquire Series Tokens by swapping on Jupiter against market-maker liquidity." U.S. and U.K. persons are excluded from membership entirely.
redemption.rails: Documented retail path: internal membership-interest repurchase settled from the Series treasury by smart contract. Documented operational path: market makers mint and burn against the underlying ETF through B2B endpoints, 24/5 in line with U.S. trading hours, while user-facing trading is 24/7 RFQ on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. No burn address, latency, SLA or minimum is published for either path, and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to implement the smart-contract repurchase.
redemption.fees: Primary market: "The per-token purchase price shall equal the executed market price paid in a bona fide transaction to acquire one (1) share of [the named ETF], plus a transaction fee equal to 0.1% of such executed price." Ongoing: "The Master DAO is allowed to charge operational fees to the Series using a percentage-of-treasury formula" - the percentage is never stated in the master or any Series agreement. Secondary market: "User-facing trading costs are reflected in the RFQ spread quoted by market makers", tightest in U.S. hours and widest at weekends; the two docs pages give different weekend ceilings ("up to ~3%" in Solution Overview, "up to ~5%" in Risk Management). No transfer fee is charged on-chain: none of the eight mints carries a transferFeeConfig extension.

issuers.corporateActions: Nothing is passed through and nothing is applied by Shift. "Membership interests represent a limited economic interest in the Assets of the Series 17 treasury and do not provide any expectation of profit, income, or dividends." Leverage resets are the ETF issuer's: "SHIFT does not perform rebalancing. The leverage is delivered by the underlying ETF (e.g., Direxion TSLL), which manages its own daily reset internally. SHIFT simply tokenizes the ETF position 1:1. Nothing happens at 4 PM ET inside the SHIFT protocol." Wind-down is issuer-decided: on a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone determines, in its administrative capacity, whether each Series "(i) continue[s] as an independent DAO LLC" or "(ii) be dissolved and wound up", and "all applicable fees, costs, and third-party expenses associated with such continuation shall be borne by the applicable Series or its members". Membership can also end involuntarily - "the person's involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal of their status as a Member, if the person is deemed a Restricted Person" - and Art. VII.2 provides that voluntary or involuntary cessation "does not give rise to any right of a Member to a distribution of any property or economic resources". Separately, the scaledUiAmountConfig authority on every mint lets the issuer restate all displayed balances; SOX3S already sits at multiplier 0.1.

pricing.notes: The issuer publishes no NAV, mark or indicative value for any Series Token at any cadence, and no oracle carries a price for them (rwa-sonar's own reference-price probe returns refSource null for all 8: "leveraged; no 1:1 reference"; the Shift symbols also truncate their underlyings, TSL2L to TSL and SOX3L to SOX, so no ticker join is possible). The user-facing price is a market maker's RFQ quote "based on the underlying ETF's NAV, plus a spread", and the spread is neither published nor bounded in any document. The primary-market price is anchored to a real exchange print - the executed price of one share of the named Direxion ETF plus 0.1% - so arbitrage against a public NAV is structurally possible, but only for the authorized market makers who can reach the mint/burn endpoints, and only 24/5. Observed secondary market on 2026-09-16: Jupiter reports null DEX liquidity on all eight mints, USD 117.91 of total 24h volume across all of them, organicScore 0 on every one, and a first pool for only 3 of 8 (all created 2026-07-31).

incidents.summary: The executed Series 17 (S&P 500 X3 SHIFT) Operating Agreement, signed this date by Robin Van Niekerk for MINS LLC, defines membership by holding "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token" - the wrong product - and locates the governing token in "the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined". The binding document for the largest Shift Series therefore names neither the right token nor any mint address.

395.71858898 SPCX2S ("Shift SpaceX 2x Short") were minted by the mint's own authority keypair, although Shift's markets page still carried SPCX2S as not yet tradable and a June 2026 report of the SpaceX launch said the SPCX2S launch date "remains to be determined ... subject to the availability of the underlying market instrument". No Series Operating Agreement for any SpaceX Series has ever been published, so what the Series is permitted to hold against those tokens is undocumented.

All eight mints were topped up in a single ten-second batch (08:48:20Z to 08:48:30Z), each a bare SPL Token-2022 createIdempotent + mintTo signed by that mint's own authority keypair with one shared fee payer (2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz). No SHIFT program, oracle or proof-of-reserve account appears in any of the transactions, which is the opposite of the documented architecture ("the SHIFT Solana program ... mints, burns, and tracks Series Token supply", "mint operations are gated by PoR feed").

The only audit Shift publishes is another company's. The Audits page asserts "All SHIFT smart contracts are audited by independent third-party security firms. Audit reports are published in full" and links one file: ARTokens_GmbH_Zokyo_audit_report_June19_2025.pdf, a Zokyo review dated 19 June 2025 of ARTokens GmbH, scope "aRtoken.sol", source repo github.com/artokens-fi/art-erc20 at commit 93e33c9a45fec14c2b611c4c49b8a504fd96cf77, assessed against "the Ethereum network's fast-paced and rapidly changing environment". It names no SHIFT entity, no Solana program and no Token-2022 mint, and predates the Shift mints (created 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-11) by about eleven months. Whether ARTokens GmbH is affiliated with SHIFT DAO LLC is not stated anywhere.

Documentation and hosting are split and partly broken. www.shiftrwa.xyz now leads with a different product - covered-call vaults on SPY and COPX plus a USD Yield+ credit vault, "Extra yield on real-world assets" - while the leveraged tokens live on /trade; /faq, /markets, /blog and /status 404 on that domain and are served only from a Vercel preview host (shift-rwa.vercel.app); the Operating Agreement PDFs 404 at www.shiftrwa.xyz/legal/*.pdf and resolve only from GitBook and that preview host. The vault marketing pages carry their own in-page warning label, "Unverified figure - drafted, not yet sourced from a published document", and the docs contain live [TO BE UPDATED] / [LINK] placeholders for the PoR dashboard, the third-party attestation, $SHFT utility and the operating-agreement link.

openQuestions: Which document controls? The executed Series agreements say "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and grant "treasury ownership only", while the site-wide legal notice says holding the tokens gives no "legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets". The whole claim-depth grade turns on this and the issuer publishes both.

Which mint does each Series Operating Agreement actually govern? Every agreement locates the token in "the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined", and the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement requires "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". Nothing published links the mints that trade to the Series that hold the assets.

What backs SPCX2L and SPCX2S, and under what Series? Both mints are live and trading, neither appears in the docs' Series or contract-address tables, and no Operating Agreement exists. Direxion's 2x SpaceX bull ETF (LOFF) listed on NYSE Arca on 15 June per Structured Retail Products, and a bear counterpart (LOFD) was announced later - was either instrument held when 250 SPCX2L were minted on 2026-06-16 and 395.72 SPCX2S on 2026-06-24?

Does the Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves integration exist at all? The docs describe it as gating every mint and publishing every block; the dashboard link is "[TO BE UPDATED]", no feed naming SHIFT was found, and no observed mint transaction touches an oracle account.

Is there any SHIFT Solana program? The docs describe "the SHIFT Solana program" that "mints, burns, and tracks Series Token supply" and audited "open-source" contracts, but every observed issuance is a raw Token-2022 mintTo signed by a bare keypair.
What is ARTokens GmbH to SHIFT DAO LLC, and why is its June 2025 Ethereum ERC-20 audit the only file on Shift's Audits page?
Why is SOX3S on a scaled-UI multiplier of 0.1 when the other seven mints are on 1? No document mentions the multiplier.
What is the Master DAO's percentage-of-treasury fee? Both the master and the Series agreements authorise it and neither states a number.

Which restriction list binds? The Series agreements define Restricted Persons as UN-listed persons plus residents of Iran, Syria, Cuba, North Korea and Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk, and do not exclude U.S. or U.K. persons - while the Terms of Use, Risk Disclosure and site notice exclude them explicitly and threaten "immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation". The binding agreement and the marketed policy differ.

Where did "over $40M in liquidity" go? Press reporting from the June 2026 Jupiter listing cites that figure; on 2026-09-16 Jupiter reports no DEX liquidity on any Shift mint, USD 3.26M of combined market cap and USD 117.91 of 24h volume.

Is the leveraged programme still being invested in, or is it being succeeded? www.shiftrwa.xyz now leads with covered-call vaults on SPY and COPX while /faq, /markets, /blog, /status and the Operating Agreement PDFs 404 on that domain and survive only on a Vercel preview host.
Who is the market maker with mint and burn access, and who is the "private entity that holds the backing assets"? Neither is named, and both sit between the holder and the ETF.

keyGovernance.evidence: Verified 2026-09-16 by RPC. Each mint has its own single authority address that simultaneously holds mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate, metadataUpdateAuthority, pause and scaled-UI authority (SPX3L CoghvrToe8SZTta5Q6cb2BnVki6WXXGMogeSiea5vNte; SPX3S 2CeU1GEWbhXXZvypMfAPa2AzyvF3yhrG7AqUyFoDqxZf; TSL2L 21bymdv3CB8QFa5taouuTcrgTVLjH9vKVEScEKqKGRZd; TSL1S 9eo5QkvdxsAU6kdAbAABWpbq1TGvsxPkLoroPwgxY4o1; SOX3L 2g5JvVx2C6si9XoLoMjr1CEyK8Mt597qptsrNN1RZ4WB; SOX3S 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA; SPCX2L ELt7GJcL4jxVoF1snNjxjegPKjuELxi13ut5f8R7vgH; SPCX2S 4mU3jH1iEA78LJ9YPfFYnN4ABty6xMBxndajFg3iToaK). getMultipleAccounts returns null for all eight, i.e. they are unfunded, dataless addresses, and each one nevertheless appears as a true transaction signer on raw Token-2022 mintTo instructions with a separate funded fee payer (2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz) - so they are plain off-chain Ed25519 keypairs, not program-derived addresses (a PDA cannot sign at the transaction level) and not Squads or any other multisig (no multisig program appears in any of the transactions). Recorded as hot-key with that nuance: single-key control, fees sponsored by another wallet. The mints themselves were created on 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-11 by HJfhNwwaDqcUc7k5J8N5y3y1xHZ7qDYMsC7YFpp9fCdp with a plain createAccount + initialize* + setAuthority script. No threshold, timelock or governance process is disclosed for any of these keys, and none of the eight addresses appears in any Shift document.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Membership is defined by token holding: "A person becomes a Member by obtaining at least one (1) [Series] SHFT Token", and each holder "shall be deemed to have agreed to and be bound by this Agreement upon such person's acquiring" it. The Series records required by Art. VI.1 are "the name of each current and former Member or the unique Distributed Ledger identifier(s) attributable to each Member", and where the activity is on a distributed ledger with public human-readable explanations "there shall be no separate requirement to keep books of accounts". No transfer agent, share register or off-chain holder list exists anywhere in the documents. The caveat that keeps this from being clean: the agreements never name the mint, locating the token smart contract at "an address and a blockchain to be determined", so the chain is the register of a Series whose own agreement does not identify which chain or which mint.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Nothing gates a transfer today, on any of the eight mints: defaultAccountState is initialized (new accounts are not frozen), the transferHook slot is initialized with a null programId, there is no allowlist, and there is no transferFeeConfig at all. Any wallet can send to any wallet, and the tokens are marketed as "24/7 permissionless" and composable on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. Control is entirely reactive: the permanentDelegate, freeze and pause powers are exercised after the fact, and the Risk Disclosure says a U.S. or U.K. person who bypasses the restrictions "may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse".

bearerRedemption.reason: Presenting the token compels delivery from nobody. The Series Operating Agreement's repurchase right is to be "processed by smart contract", and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to process it - every observed issuance is a raw Token-2022 mintTo by a keypair. The Technical Overview states plainly that "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly" and that mint and burn are "B2B endpoints used by professional market makers", the app that would front a redemption resolves to /coming-soon, backing operations run only 24/5, and U.S. and U.K. persons are barred from membership entirely. Observed burns are negligible: on SOX3L the sum of all mintTo amounts (3,967.41007219) exceeds current supply (3,967.37399156) by 0.03608063 tokens, i.e. about 0.0009% of supply has ever been retired.

forcedTransfers.reason: Confirmed in both law and code. All eight mints carry a live permanentDelegate plus freezeAuthority and pausableConfig, all three held by the same single key per mint. The Risk Disclosure authorises the use: any attempt by a U.S. or U.K. person to bypass the restrictions "including the use of VPNs or proxy entities - is a material breach of the Operational Agreement and may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse", and Art. VII of each Series agreement makes Restricted-Person status trigger "involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal" of membership with no right to a distribution.

titleDeed.reason: The site-wide legal notice is explicit: holding the tokens "does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets", and each Series "is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by" the trademark owners it references. Even on the Series agreements' more generous reading ("treasury ownership only"), the treasury asset is a Direxion daily-reset leveraged ETF share, not the referenced equity, so the token is at best a derived interest two layers away from Tesla or the S&P 500.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Ordinary Token-2022 mints, held in any Solana wallet: "Holders custody the token in any Solana wallet. There is no liquidation engine and no forced close", and "SPL tokens held in any Solana wallet. No exchange custody." No KYC or allowlist gates holding, and Phantom, OKX Wallet and other wallets are listed integrations.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token cannot outlive its administrator on its own terms. On a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone decides whether each Series continues as an independent DAO LLC or is wound up, and the members pay for continuation. The documented value chain runs entirely through parties the holder cannot reach: an unnamed "private entity that holds the backing assets", unnamed market makers who alone can mint and burn, and an administrator that owes no fiduciary duty and is subject to no court action in any jurisdiction. Nothing independent of Shift attests the reserve, and no NAV or PoR feed exists to price the token if Shift stopped publishing.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unusually well pinned down for this cohort. A named issuer (SHIFT DAO LLC), a named jurisdiction (Republic of the Marshall Islands, DAO Act 2022 and LLC Act 1996), a stated governing law (RMI, in both the Terms of Use and every Series agreement), a named nominee member with a Majuro address (MINS LLC, Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road) and a fixed forum (ICDR arbitration seated in the RMI). The flag asks whether the jurisdiction is preset, and it is; what the jurisdiction is worth is another matter, since the agreements bar any court action anywhere and remove both fiduciary duties and inspection rights.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Every third-party verification Shift claims is either absent or somebody else's. Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves is described as running "continuously" and publishing "every block" and as gating mints, yet the PoR dashboard link reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", no Chainlink PoR feed naming SHIFT could be located, and the observed mints carry no oracle account at all. The "Third-party attestation" heading in the Collateral & Custody page is an empty "[TO BE UPDATED]". The sole file on the Audits page is a Zokyo review of ARTokens GmbH's Ethereum ERC-20 contract dated 19 June 2025. No custodian confirmation, holdings statement or reconciliation output has ever been published by DekaBank, ALPACADB LTD or anyone else.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers is yes and tokenSelfCustody is yes, so an agent can hold and trade these tokens with no KYC and no allowlist. Three caveats that the flag does not capture: an agent cannot truthfully make the non-U.S./non-U.K.-person representation membership requires, it holds an asset subject to clawback, freeze and global pause by a single key, and there is effectively no market to trade into - USD 117.91 of 24h volume across all eight mints and no reported DEX liquidity on any of them.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The mechanism exists but no document binds it to a legal process. The clawback, freeze and pause powers are triggered by the issuer's own determination - Restricted-Person status or "a material breach of the Operational Agreement" such as VPN use - not by a court or regulator, and no procedure, notice period or appeal is published. The Restricted-Person definition does track external legal instruments (the UN Security Council Consolidated List and OFAC-embargoed regions), which is the one point in Shift's favour, but the same agreements bar any court action "in any court of any jurisdiction" and remove inspection rights, so there is no ordinary forum in which a holder-facing order could be obtained and then reflected on-chain.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A DEX or peer-to-peer transfer settles on the agreement of buyer and seller alone: no issuer signature, allowlist check, transfer hook or KYC step sits in the transfer path on any of the eight mints. Validity can be undone afterwards by clawback or freeze, but the transfer itself needs no third party.

attestations.statement: A full legal set is published and was retrieved on 2026-09-16: Terms of Use, Risk Disclosure, FAQ, Privacy Policy, the Master Operating Agreement and executed Series Operating Agreements for Series 12, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 18. The GitBook legal hub is described as the "Single source of truth for SHIFT DAO LLC's policies, disclosures, and the Operating Agreements governing each Series of membership-interest tokens" and was last updated 7 days before this review.

Site-wide legal notice: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." The Series agreements add "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only. Members shall have no voting rights, management rights, or authority to participate in the control or operation of the Series", and the FAQ: "A Series membership grants you an exclusive economic interest in the assets held by the Series treasury, but it does not include voting or management rights."

Risk Disclosure: any attempt by a U.S. or U.K. person to bypass the eligibility restrictions "including the use of VPNs or proxy entities - is a material breach of the Operational Agreement and may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse". On-chain on 2026-09-16 every one of the eight mints carries permanentDelegate, freezeAuthority, mintAuthority and pausableConfig, all held by one key per mint.

Risk Disclosure: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets", held in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" with "FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners". Recorded unknown: neither named firm has published any confirmation, account statement or holdings report tied to these Series, the entity that actually holds the ETFs is described only as "a private entity", and no Series is identified in any custodian document.

Series 17 Operating Agreement: "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", each Series "acting functionally as its own LLC with distinct assets, liabilities, and objectives" under LLC Act s.79. Recorded unknown because the issuer's own site-wide notice denies exactly this ("does not grant ... legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets") and because the agreement does not identify the mint it governs ("an address and a blockchain to be determined"), so the traded SPL token cannot be shown to be the membership interest described.

The docs publish a Contract addresses table with the Solana SPL address for six of the eight live mints (TSL2L, TSL1S, SOX3L, SOX3S, SPX3L, SPX3S), all of which match the mints observed on-chain, with the instruction "Always verify the address before any swap or wallet addition." The two SpaceX mints that exist and trade (SPCX2L, SPCX2S) are absent from this table and from the Product Overview Series table.

Solution Overview: "For every Series Token in circulation, this entity holds the corresponding leveraged or inverse ETF on a 1:1 basis ... There are no fractional reserves. Tokens cannot be issued in excess of verified backing." Recorded unknown: no proof-of-reserve feed, attestation, custodian confirmation or holdings report exists, the claimed Chainlink PoR gating is absent from every observed mint transaction, and the SPCX2S mint was issued while the issuer's own pages said the underlying instrument was not yet available.

findings.statement: 1:1 backing is the central product claim and nothing verifies it. Chainlink PoR is said to run "continuously" and publish "the verified reserve state on-chain, every block" while gating mints, but the PoR dashboard link on that page is "[TO BE UPDATED]", the "Third-party attestation" section is "[TO BE UPDATED]", the app dashboard it points to resolves to /coming-soon, no Chainlink feed naming SHIFT could be located, and no custodian statement or holdings report has ever been published.

The Audits page claims "All SHIFT smart contracts are audited by independent third-party security firms" and links a single file: ARTokens_GmbH_Zokyo_audit_report_June19_2025.pdf, a Zokyo review of ARTokens GmbH scoped to "aRtoken.sol" from repo github.com/artokens-fi/art-erc20 at commit 93e33c9a45fec14c2b611c4c49b8a504fd96cf77, written against "the Ethereum network's" environment and dated 19 June 2025. It names no SHIFT entity, no Solana program and no Token-2022 mint, and there is no SHIFT program on Solana for it to have audited.

Each mint's mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate, metadata, pause and scaled-UI authority is one and the same address, and that address signs raw SPL Token-2022 mintTo instructions directly with no multisig program anywhere in the transaction. The eight authority addresses hold no lamports and no data, so they are plain off-chain keypairs with fees sponsored by 2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz. No threshold, quorum or timelock is disclosed in any Shift document. Verified by getMultipleAccounts over all eight authority addresses and getTransaction on their mintTo signatures.

None of the eight keys that can claw back, freeze or pause a Shift mint appears in any published Shift document, and no role, entity or governance process is attached to them. The docs publish mint addresses but never the authorities that control them.

All eight mints carry pausableConfig with a live authority (paused=false on 2026-09-16), so one key per product can halt every transfer of that token at once, with no court, regulator or notice period involved. The product is marketed as "24/7 permissionless".

Every Shift mint carries scaledUiAmountConfig under the same single authority, so all displayed balances can be restated by changing one multiplier. This is not hypothetical: SOX3S already sits at multiplier 0.1 while the other seven are at 1, and no Shift document mentions the multiplier, explains the SOX3S value or commits to a notice period for changing it.

Issuance is unconditioned. 395.71858898 SPCX2S were minted on 2026-06-24 while the issuer's own markets page carried SPCX2S as not yet tradable and a June 2026 report said its launch was "subject to the availability of the underlying market instrument"; no Series Operating Agreement for a SpaceX Series has ever been published. Every observed mintTo is a bare Token-2022 instruction signed by a keypair, with no program, oracle or reserve account in the transaction, so the claim that "tokens cannot be issued in excess of verified backing" has no on-chain enforcement.

Two of the eight live mints have no terms at all. The operating-agreements page publishes the master agreement plus Series 12, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 18; SPCX2L and SPCX2S are covered by no agreement, appear in neither the Product Overview Series table nor the Contract addresses table, and therefore have no documented Series, no defined permitted Assets, no price formula and no redemption right - while trading on Jupiter under the Shift name and tag.

The Series agreements define the treasury contents openly: Series 17 is "designated solely to acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to the S&P 500 index (the 'Assets'), as established and approved by the Master DAO", and "The Master DAO shall define via its own governance process, which asset the Series acquires and holds". A specific ETF (SPXL, ISIN US25459W8626) is named only in the pricing formula, not as a binding holdings constraint, so the Series is not contractually confined to the instrument the marketing names.

The Series agreements grant a member redemption "processed by smart contract ... settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet", while the Technical Overview says "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly" and mint/burn are "B2B endpoints used by professional market makers". No SHIFT program exists on-chain to process a member repurchase, the app front-end is at /coming-soon, and observed net burns are negligible (SOX3L: total minted 3,967.41007219 versus supply 3,967.37399156, a net 0.03608063 tokens retired).

The docs acknowledge the gap - "Backing operations (ETF purchases) run 24/5, in line with U.S. trading hours. User-facing trading on Jupiter remains 24/7" - but state no latency, SLA or bound for mint, burn or redemption, and the two pages disagree on the resulting cost: weekend spreads "Widest (up to ~3%)" in Solution Overview against "up to ~5%" in Risk Management.

Shift publishes no NAV, indicative value or valuation output for any Series Token at any cadence. The markets page shows "Loading live price..." and "On-chain TVL feed wires up next, with the indexer", the app dashboard is /coming-soon, and the only price a holder can see is a market maker's RFQ quote whose spread is neither published nor bounded.

No oracle publisher carries a price for any Shift mint. The Shift symbols truncate their underlyings (TSL2L to TSL, SOX3L to SOX, SPX3L to SPX), so no Pyth equity feed matches, and the repo's own probe resolves all eight to refSource null with the note "leveraged; no 1:1 reference" (stocks/data/reference-prices.json). On-chain consumers such as the lending venues the docs name have no attested feed to read.

Jupiter reports null DEX liquidity for all eight mints against USD 3,260,945 of combined market cap, with a first pool for only three of them (all created 2026-07-31) and USD 117.91 of total 24h volume across the whole issuer - against press reporting of "over $40M in liquidity" assembled by Shift RWA. SPX3L alone accounts for USD 81.79 of that volume; four of the eight traded nothing. Aggregated from stocks/data/universe.json (Jupiter lite-api tokens/v2/search, fetched 2026-09-16T14:02:53Z).

Jupiter reports organicScore 0 and organicScoreLabel "low" on all eight mints, with buyOrganicVolume and sellOrganicVolume null throughout, so no part of the reported 24h volume is measured as organic end-holder flow. Median top-10 holder share is 99.79% across the eight mints (99.86% SPX3L, 99.93% SPX3S, 99.20% TSL2L, 99.95% SOX3S, 99.72% SOX3L, 99.92% TSL1S, and the lower 81.39% SPCX2L and 95.78% SPCX2S), so the 1,810 reported holder accounts do not measure distribution - essentially all supply sits in issuer or market-maker inventory wallets.

Inter-Series segregation is asserted "To the maximum extent permitted by the LLC Act" and the FAQ says "The debts of one Series cannot legally affect another", but no insolvency or trust-recognition opinion is published for the RMI series structure or for the off-chain holding arrangement, and the Risk Disclosure concedes that on custodian insolvency "In extreme cases, some or all of the Series Assets may become unrecoverable."

On the issuer's own site-wide notice the holder has no proprietary claim: holding the tokens "does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets". The Series agreements reinforce the downside - dissolution distributes only "after settling all debts", and cessation of member status, including involuntary withdrawal, "does not give rise to any right of a Member to a distribution of any property or economic resources". No security interest, trustee or collateral agent exists.

SHIFT DAO LLC is the issuer of every Series, its sole administrator, the party that "shall define which asset the Series acquires and holds", the recipient of an undisclosed percentage-of-treasury fee, and the holder of every on-chain authority. The only other parties in the agreements are a nominee member with "no economic entitlement or discretionary authority" and an unnamed "private entity that holds the backing assets"; the docs also state the Master DAO "does not serve as a manager, investment adviser, or fiduciary", so no independent party assures anything about the reserve or the register.

The Risk Disclosure commits each Series to the obligation - "This requires timely and accurate reconciliation between on-chain token activity and off-chain activity, including acquisitions and disposals of off-chain assets linked to new issuances or redemptions" - and warns that failure "may result in imbalances". No reconciliation report, supply endpoint or per-Series holdings figure has ever been published, so the claim cannot be tested from outside.

A real company-law registration is presented alongside express denials of regulated status. The Terms of Use lean on the RMI DAO LLC registration for "legal clarity" while stating the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law", and the site notice adds that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State". A series vehicle that holds an ETF against redeemable interests is fund-shaped; no fund authorisation exists anywhere.

issuers.name: Opening Bell by Superstate
issuers.issuerText: Superstate (Superstate Inc. / Superstate Services LLC) — Opening Bell platform. NOTE: the securities issuer is the public company itself (Forward Industries, Galaxy Digital, Solana Company, Exodus, SharpLink); Superstate is the SEC-registered digital transfer agent, not the securities issuer.
products: Opening Bell — tokenized SEC-registered common stock, issued natively on Solana (and Ethereum/Linea) to allowlisted wallets
Direct Issuance Program (DIP) — primary issuance of new registered shares at oracle-derived prices settled in USDC (documented on Ethereum; EquityToken + DIP contracts)

Live equities (2026-09-16): FWDI (Forward Industries, Solana), GLXY (Galaxy Digital Class A, Solana), EXOD (Exodus Movement Class A, Solana), HSDT (Solana Company, Solana, supply 0), SBET (SharpLink, Ethereum + Linea)
issuers.issuingEntity: Superstate Services LLC (Delaware LLC, 205 W 28th Street Floor 8, New York, NY 10001) acting as 'Digital Transfer Agent'; SEC Transfer Agent File No. 84-06972, registered under Section 17A(c)(2) of the Exchange Act. Shares are issued by the public company; Superstate mints the token representing its book-entry shares.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Delaware LLC, principal offices New York, NY, USA. Issuers are US-incorporated SEC reporting companies (Forward Industries, Inc. — Delaware/NY; Solana Company (HSDT) — Delaware; Exodus Movement, Inc. — Delaware; Galaxy Digital Inc. — Delaware).
issuers.governingLaw: New York law (Superstate Transfer Agent & Terms of Service Agreement §12; Digital Transfer Agency Agreement §16.2). US federal securities law: Securities Act 1933 registration, Exchange Act 1934 §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21, Rule 17Ad-17 lost-shareholder rule. Disputes: mandatory arbitration in New York (JAMS for investor terms; AAA for the issuer agreement), class-action waiver.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: Fully regulated US path. The underlying security is registered common stock of an SEC-reporting, exchange-listed company (Nasdaq/NYSE American). Superstate Services LLC is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 84-06972; TA-1 filed 2025-02-03, amended 2025-05-05 and 2026-03-25; EFFECT 2025-03-05; TA-2 filed 2026-03-26) operating as a co-/digital transfer agent alongside the issuer's Recordkeeping Transfer Agent (for FWDI: Equity Stock Transfer). Superstate Advisers LLC is a separate SEC-registered investment adviser (funds business, not Opening Bell). No exemptive relief or no-action letter located; issuers' own filings say the application of securities laws to trading tokenized shares 'remains uncertain'.
issuers.holderClaim: The holder owns the actual registered common share of the listed company — not a derivative, receipt or SPV claim. The Digital Transfer Agency Agreement defines 'Tokenized Shares' as 'Issuer's Book-Entry Shares represented by digital tokens recorded on the Solana blockchain', and the holder is a holder of record in their own name (Superstate maintains name, physical address and taxpayer ID per Schedule A §3.1) — there is no Superstate nominee, street-name or custodian layer. Forward Industries' 10-K: 'All issued shares, regardless of form, represent identical rights.' Schedule B of the Exodus agreement lists the in-scope security as the same class with the same CUSIP (30209R106, NYSE American) as the listed stock; Superstate's own instrument API publishes the ordinary CUSIP for each tokenized equity.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: None interposed. The token is the share itself, held in the investor's own name and in the investor's own wallet; the Recordkeeping Transfer Agent (Equity Stock Transfer for FWDI) maintains the issuer's Master Securityholder File and an 'On chain Eligible Shares Record' that Superstate debits/credits. Superstate maintains the 'Subsidiary Securityholder Records'. Superstate's own private-key management (for its admin keys) is via Turnkey.

custodyVerification.agent: Superstate Services LLC (SEC-registered digital transfer agent, File No. 84-06972) in coordination with the issuer's Recordkeeping Transfer Agent (Equity Stock Transfer for FWDI)
custodyVerification.frequency: continuous / real-time (the on-chain mint supply is the tokenized portion of the register; the public instruments API is refreshed continuously)
custodyVerification.notes: SYSTEMATIC RECONCILIATION BREAK FOUND (2026-09-16, all four Solana equities compared): Superstate's public API circulating-supply exceeds the on-chain Token-2022 mint supply by exactly 0.1 shares on FWDI (api 7,280,819.200000 vs chain 7,280,819.100000) and on GLXY (api 13,399.282876 vs chain 13,399.182876), and matches exactly on EXOD (60.000000) and HSDT (0). The +0.1 appears on precisely the two tickers with a DeFi integration, and the FWDI asset page exposes an 'AdminSeed-Kamino-SolMainnet-900' position worth 0.607498 notional = 0.1 share at $6.07 — so the most likely reading is an admin seed counted in the register figure but absent from the mint supply, not random drift. Superstate's own rendered FWDI asset page shows 7,280,819.10 on Solana, agreeing with the chain and disagreeing with its own API. Economically trivial (~$0.61) but structurally the point: the chain is a mirror of the register, the mirror is measurably and repeatably off, two Superstate surfaces disagree with each other, and no published reconciliation would have caught it. There are FOUR machine-readable verification surfaces, all public and unauthenticated: (1) https://api.superstate.com/v2/instruments returns, per ticker, the CUSIP, the per-chain mint address, total_supply, circulating_supply, the equity burn address and the split multiplier — verified 2026-09-16: FWDI total_supply 8,732,937.10, circulating (tokenized) 7,280,819.20; (2) per-ticker scalar endpoints https://api.superstate.com/v1/instruments/FWDI/total-supply and /circulating-supply (plain numbers, no auth); (3) the Token-2022 mint itself via getTokenSupply — FWDI 7,280,819.100000 at slot 447531447; (4) the Allowlist program HFkKyweJDUuGer5KaCst5qZSYD5aapKaD7xzdNaoRtfA is publicly enumerable — getProgramAccounts returned 827 accounts (698 of 32 bytes, 129 of 64 bytes) on 2026-09-16, and Superstate publishes a Rust SDK (crates.io superstate-allowlist-interface) and TS SDK (@superstateinc/allowlist) to read its state. 481 Token-2022 accounts exist for the FWDI mint. What is NOT public: the register itself (holder identities, name/address/TIN), which sits in Superstate's Subsidiary Securityholder Records and the RTA's Master Securityholder File. Superstate's /v1/balances and /v2/transactions APIs require an API key scoped to your own entity; the issuer sees a private 'Issuance dashboard'. No auditor attestation, no Chainlink Proof-of-Reserve and no reconciliation report on the equities is published. Reserve-style verification is structurally unnecessary — the token is the share, not a claim on a reserve.

redemption.eligibility: Any allowlisted holder with an approved Superstate account. 'Burn to book-entry' converts tokens back to book-entry shares; those can then be DRS-transferred to a traditional brokerage and sold on Nasdaq. Available to eligible investors globally ('Global*', excluding jurisdictions subject to US sanctions); accredited-investor status is NOT required.
redemption.rails: Send tokens to the published equity burn address on Solana (2u8YwJTykTreziHBN5QwE7Bi2SyN8M2MicCscthtph9E — the same burn address for all Solana equities), then the book-entry balance updates in the Superstate portal; a transfer authorization form plus a DRS transfer moves the shares to a broker. Note: burning equity tokens does NOT trigger a cash payout (unlike the funds) — you must sell on a DEX or move the shares to a broker to realise value.
redemption.fees: Superstate charges no processing fee for burn/transfer; the holder pays Solana network fees and any fees charged by the Recordkeeping Transfer Agent or the receiving broker-dealer (Terms §4.2, §4.3).

issuers.corporateActions: Dividends: on Board declaration the issuer instructs the RTA with declaration/ex/record/payment dates and amount per share; payment is 'in cash or additional Shares (or other agreed to form, such as stablecoins, in the future), at the election of each shareholder' and Superstate coordinates with the RTA to process dividends, payments and tax forms (Digital Transfer Agency Agreement Schedule A §4). Note that FWDI, GLXY, EXOD and HSDT do not currently pay dividends, so the pathway is untested in practice. Voting/proxy: the tokenized holder is a holder of record, and Superstate 'will coordinate with the RTA to enable shareholder communication and proxy material distribution' (Schedule A §3.3); there is no on-chain voting. Splits: applied at the mint via the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount multiplier, and exposed publicly as equity_info.current_split_multiplier in the instruments API. Lost shareholders: Superstate performs Rule 17Ad-17 services; escheat stays with the issuer/RTA (Schedule A §5).

pricing.notes: The underlying class trades on Nasdaq, so an exchange price exists, but the TOKEN has no exchange venue. Forward Industries' own 10-K warns that 'there are no current trading venues for the tokenized shares' and holders 'may face potential illiquidity, trading volatility and/or pricing discrepancies when compared to shares of common stock which trade on Nasdaq. These discrepancies may be substantial.' Arbitrage exists but is slow and one-way-ish: conversion of tokens back to Nasdaq-tradeable book-entry shares 'could take up to multiple weeks' (10-K), which is far too slow to hold the peg intraday. Solana Company's 10-K makes the same point: 'prolonged price discrepancies between Tokenized and Traditional HSDT — especially where arbitrage is limited by operational or regulatory constraints.' Superstate publishes two Pyth feeds per equity: a Nasdaq feed (Equity.US.FWDI/USD) and a Superstate index feed used by DeFi protocols (Crypto.Index.FWDI/USD); the Direct Issuance Program prices new shares off a Pyth oracle at or below the Nasdaq/NYSE price with a configured discount, circuit breakers and slippage bounds.

venues: No centralised exchange listing for the tokens. Peer-to-peer transfers between allowlisted wallets.

Kamino Finance (Solana) — borrowing/lending; FWDI usable as collateral. Verified on the public FWDI asset page 2026-09-16: 3,156,493.10 FWDI ($19.18M) held in Kamino, i.e. ~43% of tokenized supply. Restricted to EX-US holders per the launch release.
Superstate allowlists DeFi protocol addresses at its discretion; the Allowlist program exposes a permissionless Thaw instruction so protocols can onboard allowlisted users inside their own flows.
Superstate itself is not a trading venue: 'Investors cannot trade directly on Superstate.'

incidents.summary: Reconciliation discrepancy observed by rwa-sonar (not an announced incident): Superstate's public API circulating-supply runs exactly 0.1 shares above the on-chain Token-2022 mint supply on FWDI (7,280,819.200000 vs 7,280,819.100000) and GLXY (13,399.282876 vs 13,399.182876), while matching exactly on EXOD and HSDT. The affected pair is exactly the pair with a DeFi integration, and the FWDI asset page shows an 'AdminSeed-Kamino' position of 0.1 share — consistent with an admin seed counted off-chain but not minted. Superstate's own rendered asset page agrees with the chain and therefore disagrees with its own API. Immaterial in value (~$0.61); material as evidence that the off-chain register and the chain are not bit-identical and that no published reconciliation exists to surface it.

No exploit, freeze event, trading halt, forced-burn event or depeg found for Opening Bell equities as of 2026-09-16. Searches of press and of the issuers' SEC filings returned nothing. Absence of a found incident is not proof there was none.
