openQuestions: Is the FWDI/HSDT Solana equity token program the same code as the audited Superstate token programs, and has the EQUITY-specific program (and the EVM EquityToken/DIP contracts) had an independent security audit? The published 0xMacro/ChainSecurity audits cover USTB/USCC and the Allowlist; no equity-token audit was located.

Governance of the admin keys. The Solana Allowlist upgrade authority (2ccHdavxJ3eZ4aUy39sHmykFhiKkuvtomyRLRULrwkMA) and each mint authority are on-curve, system-owned addresses with no multisig program account. Turnkey may enforce an off-chain N-of-M policy, but no threshold, quorum or timelock is disclosed anywhere. Single-key compromise would reach mint, freeze, forced-burn and allowlist writes.

Which register wins in a dispute? The DTAA makes the RTA's off-chain Master Securityholder File authoritative and Superstate's record 'subsidiary', while the SEC-filed Galaxy 8-K says Superstate 'records legal ownership onchain in real time' and 'the registered shareholder list of Galaxy updates in real-time'. If the chain and the RTA's file disagree, no document located says which controls, or who bears the loss.

RESOLVED for FWDI and EXOD, open for the rest: FWDI's published CUSIP 349862409 is the ordinary Nasdaq-listed common-stock CUSIP, assigned by Nasdaq when the 1-for-10 reverse split took effect 2024-06-18 (nasdaqtrader.com Equity Corporate Actions Alert #2024-287) — so no separate tokenized tranche. EXOD's 30209R106 is confirmed by Schedule B of the signed agreement. GLXY (36317J209), HSDT (42328V876) and SBET (820014405) were taken from Superstate's own API and not cross-checked against an independent CUSIP source.

Is there a dividend precedent? DTAA Schedule A §4 sets out a full cash/shares/(future stablecoin) dividend path, but FWDI, GLXY, EXOD and HSDT do not pay dividends, so the path has never been exercised. Likewise no split has occurred (multiplier still 1), so the ScaledUiAmount corporate-action mechanism is untested in production.

Has proxy voting actually been exercised by a tokenized holder? Schedule A §3.3 only commits Superstate to 'coordinate with the RTA to enable shareholder communication and proxy material distribution' — no record of a tokenized holder voting at a meeting was found.

Why is HSDT (Solana Company) still at zero supply? The token was deployed 2025-11-14 and the Digital Transfer Agency Agreement is dated 2025-10-17, but the mint supply was 0 on 2026-09-16. Announced but effectively not live; treat HSDT as non-operational for grading.

What is the real ownership dispersion? 481 Token-2022 accounts exist for the FWDI mint, but ~43% of tokenized supply (3,156,493 FWDI, $19.2M) sits in Kamino, and the public asset page shows an 'AdminSeed-Kamino' label — so the holder count overstates independent economic holders.

Why is the public API's circulating-supply exactly 0.1 shares above the on-chain mint supply on FWDI and GLXY but exact on EXOD and HSDT? The 0.1 'AdminSeed-Kamino' position on the FWDI asset page is the likely cause, but nothing states whether that 0.1 is a real share in the register with no token, a display artefact, or an unminted placeholder — and no published reconciliation would reveal which.

RESOLVED: the freeze-authority/permanent-delegate address 2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x is controlled by the Allowlist program, proven on-chain rather than taken from the docs. Transaction 2hYLRFwbxU7DcMxGudfJopFdCT1txbsi4eLa8zAPo47Enp8hyPhLKK6XDbdUFtuHnWFxTuBxYoN1Z3si2dSZFbDy (blockTime 1789052737, i.e. live activity on 2026-09-16) invokes the Allowlist program HFkKyweJDUuGer5KaCst5qZSYD5aapKaD7xzdNaoRtfA, whose inner instructions are Token-2022 getAccountDataSize, System createAccount, initializeImmutableOwner, initializeAccount3 and thawAccount — i.e. the program creates the associated token account with the ImmutableOwner extension and thaws it in one shot, signing as freeze authority via that PDA. Confirms the documented design and confirms ImmutableOwner is applied at the token-account level. What remains open is only the seed derivation (common single seeds did not reproduce the address) and, separately, who controls the program's upgrade authority.

Superstate's fee to the issuer is $1 per year (DTAA §3.1). Is the commercial arrangement documented elsewhere (equity, warrants, platform fees), and does it create an incentive misalignment for a party that also holds forced-burn authority?

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Superstate on-chain profile, 2026-09-16): per-mint mint authorities and the one shared freeze/permanent-delegate authority 2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x are single system-owned addresses with no multisig or timelock visible; Superstate states only that key management is facilitated by Turnkey. Tension worth noting: the account that actually thaws holder accounts is the upgradeable Allowlist BPF program HFkKyweJDUuGer5KaCst5qZSYD5aapKaD7xzdNaoRtfA (CPI into Token-2022), so the thaw path is program-mediated even though the authority key is not a PDA of a constrained program.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: The Digital Transfer Agency Agreement is explicit: §1.10 'Master Security holder File means the database shareholder record of ownership maintained by the RTA', and §1.8 Superstate keeps only 'Subsidiary Security holder Records'. §1.9 defines Tokenized Shares as book-entry shares 'represented by' tokens. So the authoritative register is the Recordkeeping Transfer Agent's off-chain master file, into which Superstate transmits on-chain activity (Schedule A §2.1). The chain is a near-real-time mirror of a subsidiary record, not the register. Superstate's and Galaxy's marketing says the opposite ('records legal ownership onchain in real time', 'the registered shareholder list of Galaxy updates in real-time'); the executed contract controls. Corroborating: on termination Superstate must 'deliver to Issuer all Subsidiary Security holder Records' and freeze token transfers (§7.5) — the shares survive off-chain.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Both sender and receiver must be on Superstate's Allowlist. Mechanically: the Token-2022 mints carry DefaultAccountState=Frozen, so every newly created token account is frozen and unusable until the Allowlist program (which holds freezeAuthority) thaws it; a transfer to a non-allowlisted wallet therefore cannot settle. Contractually: DTAA Schedule A §3.4 obliges Superstate to program the contracts 'such that Tokenized Shares may only be transferred to or held by digital wallet addresses of persons or decentralized exchange pools on the Allowlist', and §3.5.5.2 reserves the right to refuse transfers to non-allowlisted addresses. Superstate may also 'block or disable access to any Third-Party Services ... which includes our Allowlist at any time' (Terms §7.3).

bearerRedemption.reason: You cannot present the token to a third party and receive the share. Burn-to-book-entry runs entirely through Superstate: you must have an approved, KYC'd Superstate account, send tokens to Superstate's published burn address, and the book-entry balance then appears in your Superstate portfolio; moving to a broker requires a Superstate transfer-authorization form and a DRS transfer coordinated with the RTA. Burning also produces no payout ('Unlike funds, burning equity tokens does not trigger a payout'). A holder without a Superstate account holds a frozen, unusable token.

forcedTransfers.reason: The mints carry a PermanentDelegate (2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x, verified on-chain 2026-09-16), which can move or burn tokens from any account without the holder's signature, and the Allowlist program holds freezeAuthority so any account can be re-frozen. Superstate documents the intent: admin functions include 'forcibly burning an investor's tokens (if required by exogenous legal circumstances, for example)'; 'In the unusual event in which an investor's Allowlist address is compromised, there are procedures in place capable of restoring your investment'; and the Terms note 'Allowlist restrictions and recovery mechanisms in place' for lost or stolen tokenized shares (§6.2). This is the point on which Opening Bell scores where most tokenized-stock wrappers do not.

titleDeed.reason: The token is the registered common share, not a derived or partial right. Galaxy's SEC-filed 8-K: 'These are not derivatives or representations; they are Galaxy Digital Class A Common Stock, with all the rights that confers.' Forward Industries' 10-K: 'All issued shares, regardless of form, represent identical rights.' The Exodus agreement's Schedule B lists the in-scope security as the same class and the same CUSIP (30209R106) as the NYSE American-listed stock, and Superstate publishes the ordinary CUSIP for every tokenized equity. The holder is a holder of record in their own name (name, address, TIN held by Superstate), not a beneficiary behind a nominee.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Tokens are held in the investor's own Solana wallet once that address is allowlisted; the Terms put the private-key risk squarely on the holder ('by using self custody you take on this full responsibility', §6.4–6.5) and warn that self-custodied holders get no SIPC protection. Galaxy's 8-K: available to 'approved KYC'd investors who can hold and transfer them within their own crypto wallets'. Caveat: self-custody is conditional — the account is frozen by default and only Superstate's allowlist makes it usable, and Superstate can re-freeze it.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token's usability depends continuously on Superstate. The Allowlist program is upgradeable (upgrade authority 2ccHdavxJ3eZ4aUy39sHmykFhiKkuvtomyRLRULrwkMA, a single on-curve system-owned address as of 2026-09-16) and is the only thing that can thaw a token account; mint authority is a separate single on-curve Superstate address per instrument. If Superstate stops operating, no new account can be thawed and no new share can be tokenized or burned. The DTAA anticipates exactly this: on termination Superstate will 'freeze the continued ability to transfer Tokenized Shares and coordinate with the RTA to allow holders of Tokenized Shares to redeem them for Certificated Shares or Book-Entry Shares' (§7.5). The SHARE survives Superstate's disappearance; the TOKEN does not.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unambiguous and stated in writing: New York law and exclusive New York jurisdiction (Terms §12; DTAA §16.2), US federal securities law (Securities Act registration statement effective; Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21; Rule 17Ad-17), an SEC-registered transfer agent with a public file number (84-06972), and named arbitration fora (JAMS for investors, AAA for issuers, both seated in New York).

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent is attached to the token. The mint's TokenMetadata additionalMetadata array is empty and its update authority is Superstate's own admin key; there is no attestation hook, no Chainlink Proof-of-Reserve on the equities, no auditor report and no published reconciliation between the on-chain supply and the RTA's master file. What verification exists is contractual and non-public: the issuer, the RTA and regulators have inspection and audit rights over Superstate's Subsidiary Securityholder Records (DTAA §6.2), and the SEC transfer-agent rules apply. The independent RTA is a real second pair of eyes, but its confirmation is not published or attachable on-chain.

aiReady.reason: KYC is directly in the transfer loop. An address can only hold or receive the token after Superstate verifies the Shareholder Information of the person or entity controlling it and clears AML/sanctions screening (DTAA Schedule A §3.4); the Onboarding API exists precisely to submit KYC-verified identity data plus a wallet address. Onboarding also requires a government ID with a real-time image capture and, for individuals, an SSN and date of birth. Note the partial exception: decentralised exchange POOLS can themselves be allowlisted and the Allowlist program exposes a permissionless Thaw instruction, so protocols can integrate — but an autonomous agent still cannot get its own wallet allowlisted. Fails on unconditionalTransfers regardless.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The mechanism and the obligation both exist. Mechanically the PermanentDelegate and the Allowlist program's freeze authority let Superstate move, burn or freeze tokens without the holder. Contractually Superstate documents forced burns 'if required by exogenous legal circumstances'; will not issue where it has 'official notice from any appropriate authority of competent jurisdiction' that issuance is suspended (DTAA §3.5.2); must cooperate with 'regulatory, judicial or other similar requests for shareholder and share information' (§2.3); and the Terms preserve court relief to 'compel compliance with regulatory requirements or valid court orders' (§13.3) and expressly preserve SEC remedies (§13.6). Escheat and lost-holder obligations (Rule 17Ad-17) are handled.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A trade between two already-allowlisted wallets settles without per-trade sign-off, which is a genuine improvement — but the counterparties cannot be chosen freely: both must have been pre-approved by Superstate, and Superstate 'reserves the right to refuse to transfer On chain Eligible Shares to investors or blockchain addresses that are not on the Allowlist' and, separately, 'until it is satisfied that the requested transfer ... is legally authorized' (DTAA §3.5.5.2–3.5.5.3). Buyer-and-seller agreement alone is not sufficient for a valid transfer.

attestations.attestor: US Securities and Exchange Commission (registration record), asserted by Superstate Services LLC
attestations.statement: Superstate Services LLC is registered as a transfer agent under Exchange Act s.17A(c)(2), SEC File No. 84-06972 (TA-1 filed 2025-02-03, effective per EFFECT 2025-03-05, TA-1/A 2025-05-05 and 2026-03-25, TA-2 annual report 2026-03-26). It acts as Digital Transfer Agent alongside the issuer's Recordkeeping Transfer Agent.

attestations.attestor: Forward Industries, Inc. and Galaxy Digital Inc. (SEC filings), with Superstate Services LLC
attestations.statement: 'Tokenized Shares: Digital representations of our common stock recorded on the Solana blockchain, maintained by our digital transfer agent. All issued shares, regardless of form, represent identical rights.' Galaxy's 8-K: 'These are not derivatives or representations; they are Galaxy Digital Class A Common Stock.' Same class and same CUSIP as the listed security: FWDI 349862409, GLXY 36317J209, EXOD 30209R106, HSDT 42328V876, SBET 820014405 - FWDI's confirmed as the Nasdaq common-stock CUSIP assigned at the 2024-06-18 reverse split.

attestations.attestor: Superstate Services LLC and Exodus Movement, Inc. (Digital Transfer Agency Agreement s.1.9, Schedule B)
attestations.statement: 'Tokenized Shares means Issuer's Book-Entry Shares represented by digital tokens recorded on the Solana blockchain'; Schedule B names the in-scope security as the same class and CUSIP (30209R106) as the NYSE American-listed Exodus Class A common stock. The holder is a holder of record in their own name, with name, physical address and TIN held by the digital transfer agent.

attestations.attestor: Superstate Services LLC and Exodus Movement, Inc. (Digital Transfer Agency Agreement ss.1.7, 1.8, 1.10, Schedule A s.2.1)
attestations.statement: The Master Securityholder File is maintained by the Recordkeeping Transfer Agent (Equity Stock Transfer for FWDI); Superstate, as a second SEC-registered digital transfer agent, maintains only Subsidiary Securityholder Records for on-chain eligible shares and transmits purchases, exchanges, conversions, transfers and redemptions to the RTA. The subsidiary register feeds, and is subordinate to, the master file - which contradicts the marketing claim that the blockchain is the register.

attestations.attestor: Superstate Services LLC (DTAA Schedule A s.3.4)
attestations.statement: 'Superstate shall create, update, and maintain an Allowlist, and ensure that the smart contract(s) underlying the Tokenized Shares is/are programmed such that Tokenized Shares may only be transferred to or held by digital wallet addresses of persons or decentralized exchange pools on the Allowlist.' Verified on-chain: all four Solana equity mints carry defaultAccountState=Frozen and share one freeze authority and permanent delegate (2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x), and a live transaction shows the Allowlist program CPI-ing into Token-2022 to createAccount, initializeImmutableOwner, initializeAccount3 and thawAccount. There is no transfer hook: every account is born frozen and only this program can thaw it.

attestations.attestor: Superstate Services LLC (DTAA Schedule A s.3.4; Terms s.3, s.5.2)
attestations.statement: Before allowlisting a wallet Superstate must obtain and verify the Shareholder Information of the person owning or controlling it and confirm that the owner (or the DEX pool) 'has passed all anti-money laundering and sanctions screening'. Investor onboarding requires government ID with real-time image capture, SSN and date of birth; accepted KYC providers are enumerated in the Direct Issuance Program docs.

'Our smart contracts are upgradable and various functions are gated behind the Superstate Admin Address calling them. This includes all minting, adding or removing users from the allowlist, and forcibly burning an investor's tokens (if required by exogenous legal circumstances, for example).' Verified on-chain: the equity mints carry a permanent delegate and the Allowlist program holds the freeze authority. Positive for legal integration in this vocabulary and a governance risk at the same time.

The reversal, freeze and burn authority is the named 'Superstate Admin Address' held by Superstate Services LLC, the SEC-registered digital transfer agent; key management is facilitated by Turnkey. On Solana the freeze authority and permanent delegate resolve to the single shared address 2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x.

attestations.attestor: Exodus Movement, Inc. and Superstate Services LLC (DTAA s.4.1.3; Terms s.14.1)
attestations.statement: DTAA s.4.1.3: 'A registration statement under the Securities Act of 1933 on behalf of the Issuer with respect to shares subject to this Agreement is, or will be effective, upon the commencement date of services.' Terms s.14.1: 'These shares are registered pursuant to an effective registration statement.' The issuers are Exchange Act reporting companies listed on Nasdaq or NYSE American.

attestations.attestor: Superstate Services LLC (docs; Terms s.14.5; DTAA Schedule A s.3.5.6)
attestations.statement: Tokens can be burned back to book-entry shares and then DRS-transferred to a traditional brokerage, but only through a KYC'd Superstate account and with no cash payout on burn. Forward Industries' 10-K warns the conversion 'could take up to multiple weeks'.

The full Transfer Agent and Terms of Service Agreement (effective September 2025) is published at superstate.com/terms, including the SEC transfer-agent file number, governing law, Direct Issuance Program terms and risk disclosures. The issuer-side Digital Transfer Agency Agreement is public too, as an exhibit to Exodus Movement's 10-K.

Superstate publishes 12 0xMacro audits plus a ChainSecurity audit and two Allowlist audit files, covering USTB/USCC and the Allowlist program that gates the equity mints. Whether the equity token program itself has an independent audit is not stated and no equity-specific report was located; dates and scope unverified.

The set of addresses permitted to hold the token is readable on-chain by anyone: getProgramAccounts on the Allowlist program returned 827 accounts (698 of 32 bytes, 129 of 64 bytes) on 2026-09-16, and Superstate ships a Rust SDK (superstate-allowlist-interface) and a TypeScript SDK (@superstateinc/allowlist) to read the program state. The compliance perimeter is auditable even though the identities behind it are not.

Stock splits and reverse splits are applied at the mint via the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension rather than by reissuing tokens, and the multiplier is published both on-chain (scaledUiAmountConfig, 1 on FWDI and HSDT) and off-chain (equity_info.current_split_multiplier), so corporate actions do not break holder balances or DeFi positions.

findings.statement: Superstate's public API circulating supply exceeded the on-chain Token-2022 mint supply by exactly 0.1 shares on FWDI (7,280,819.200000 vs 7,280,819.100000, slot 447531447) and on GLXY (13,399.282876 vs 13,399.182876) on 2026-09-16, while matching on EXOD and HSDT. Superstate's own rendered asset page shows 7,280,819.10, so two of its surfaces disagree; the break is labelled 'AdminSeed-Kamino'.

No reconciliation report or third-party attestation exists for the equities. The DTAA obliges Superstate to coordinate with the RTA to 'ensure consistent and accurate shareholder records' and gives the issuer, RTA and regulators audit rights, but no output is published, and the Terms expressly contemplate discrepancies: 'there may be a delay in processing that may result in a discrepancy. To the extent there is a discrepancy, you are responsible for notifying us'.

Per-instrument mint authorities (FWDI CWdsNnEuCYzxBjjd9dxvhYuatVHY2cGsMNNJcKsGFSqq; HSDT 7cowcPXxq3dfEKwg2MHmxkneKSNkzKuma8WZTaaZbwh6), the shared freeze/delegate authority and the Allowlist upgrade authority (2ccHdavxJ3eZ4aUy39sHmykFhiKkuvtomyRLRULrwkMA) are all single system addresses with no Squads or other multisig program account. Superstate states only that key management is facilitated by Turnkey; no N-of-M threshold is disclosed.

The single shared freeze and permanent-delegate authority for all four Solana equity mints is a system-owned key, as are the per-mint mint authorities. Mitigating: the account that thaws holder accounts in practice is the upgradeable Allowlist BPF program, so the thaw path is program-mediated even though the key itself is not a PDA of a constrained program.

'Our Allowlist program is upgradeable' and 'our smart contracts are upgradable'. The Allowlist program's upgrade authority resolved on 2026-09-16 to 2ccHdavxJ3eZ4aUy39sHmykFhiKkuvtomyRLRULrwkMA, an on-curve system-owned address with no multisig program account, so there is no on-chain timelock and no evidence of N-of-M control over the program that gates every transfer.

HSDT (Solana Company) is documented, has a CUSIP and a deployed mint (8UBqBGXM4NF22y5TZs8PhNVwVNqsHw2jBstfcxsSZaQ4), but its total supply is 0 and both is_token_enabled_any_chain and is_trade_enabled_any_chain are false: the instrument is non-operational.

The token may be held by US persons but a specific DeFi utility is geofenced: 'Ex-US holders of Forward's tokenized FWDI shares can now post their equity as collateral on Kamino.' About 43% of tokenized FWDI (~$19.2M) sits in Kamino. One token therefore carries different permitted uses per holder jurisdiction, which a per-token boolean cannot express.

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Superstate on-chain profile, 2026-09-16): per-mint mint authorities and the one shared freeze/permanent-delegate authority 2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x are single system-owned addresses with no multisig or timelock visible; Superstate states only that key management is facilitated by Turnkey. Tension worth noting: the account that actually thaws holder accounts is the upgradeable Allowlist BPF program HFkKyweJDUuGer5KaCst5qZSYD5aapKaD7xzdNaoRtfA (CPI into Token-2022), so the thaw path is program-mediated even though the authority key is not a PDA of a constrained program.

products: T-OpenAI (tOpenAI)
T-Kalshi (tKalshi)
T-SpaceX (tSpaceX)
issuers.issuingEntity: Tessera Works Foundation ("TWF"), a Panama foundation, registered office Ricardo Arias Street, Advanced Tower Building, First Floor, Panama City. Each token is issued by its own wholly owned Panama subsidiary: SPX Tessera Issuer Inc. (T-SpaceX), KLSH Tessera Issuer Inc. (T-Kalshi), OPAI Tessera Issuer Inc. (T-OpenAI). The underlying exposure sits one layer further out, in per-company segregated portfolios of a Cayman Islands segregated portfolio company (SPC).
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Panama (foundation and per-token issuer entities); Cayman Islands (SPC segregated portfolios holding the exposure)
issuers.governingLaw: Singapore law, "without giving effect to its principles or rules of conflict of laws". Disputes: SIAC arbitration, sole arbitrator, seat Singapore, English language; Singapore International Commercial Court for related court proceedings.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: Unlicensed and structured to sit outside securities regulation. Docs: "The product carries a non-security legal opinion under Singapore law, confirming it is structured as a loan product, not a capital markets product" and "T-Tokens represent loan participation rights, not securities, though regulatory treatment may vary by jurisdiction." The opinion itself is not published. No Regulation S or other exemption is cited anywhere in the terms.
issuers.holderClaim: An unsecured stablecoin-loan participation right against one named Panama issuer entity, repayable only out of Liquidity Event Proceeds that issuer actually receives, pro rata to the holder's share of the loan series. The terms are explicit that this is purely contractual: the obligation "does not confer on any User any legal, beneficial or other proprietary interest in those Liquidity Event Proceeds, in any PE Investment or in any asset of that Issuer". No equity, voting or dividend rights and no place on the underlying company's cap table.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: No external share custodian is named. Exposure is held in per-company segregated portfolios inside a Cayman Islands SPC, acquired as "direct shares, contracts for shares, or similar instruments tracking company value". Fireblocks provides MPC key management for the token mint/transfer/burn authorities - that is operational key custody of the tokens, not custody of the underlying shares. The independent auditors who attest the portfolio holdings are not named.

custodyVerification.agent: Chainlink SmartData (DataLink) decentralised oracle network, fed by unnamed independent auditors of the Cayman SPC portfolios
custodyVerification.frequency: Chainlink feeds readable on-chain in real time (published on Solana); the underlying audited asset count behind them is "refreshed approximately monthly", so a feed reflects the most recent attested holdings rather than intra-month portfolio changes
custodyVerification.notes: Materially stronger than peers, with two real caveats. (1) The feeds publish ASSET COUNTS, not dollar values - docs: "The values these feeds publish are asset counts - Proof of Reserve - not dollar valuations of the underlying holdings", so a feed at ratio 1.00 says nothing about what the exposure is worth. (2) The attesting auditors are not named and the attestation reports themselves are not published; docs say only that "All auditors involved in signing off on the attestations ... will be shown on this page" (future tense). Crucially, 1:1 here means supply matches verified units - it is NOT a security interest, because the loan is expressly unsecured.

securityInterest.holder: none - no charge, pledge or lien over the underlying shares is granted to holders

redemption.eligibility: Any holder during the Redemption Period, whether the original lender or a subsequent acquirer of the token - the right runs with the token. Excluded Persons (including all US persons) and persons in Excluded Jurisdictions are barred, and the issuer "may require a User to provide such information as that Issuer may require" for identity verification, AML/CFT and sanctions screening. Redemption is contingent, not on demand: it requires a Liquidity Event (IPO or change of control >50%), expiry of any lock-up, actual receipt of proceeds by the issuer, and a formally announced Redemption Start Date.
redemption.rails: Holder burns the T-Tokens to the Tessera smart contracts to claim the Redemption Amount. Proceeds are paid in stablecoin, but "the specific stablecoin is determined by Tessera at its discretion and may not necessarily be the same stablecoin you originally used".
redemption.fees: 0% on acquisition; 0.2% (20 bps) on sells and transfers, enforced on-chain by the Token-2022 transferFeeConfig extension. Fees can be changed by the transfer-fee config authority.

issuers.corporateActions: Everything hinges on a Liquidity Event, defined as an IPO on a recognised exchange or a Change of Control (>50% of voting control acquired, or sale/merger). Sequence: any lock-up expires, the segregated portfolio liquidates its position, proceeds flow to the issuer entity and are converted to a stablecoin of Tessera's choosing, Tessera announces a Redemption Start Date, and holders burn tokens for a pro-rata share during the Redemption Period. Per the terms, that period runs from 10am Panama time on the Redemption Start Date to 10pm Panama time on the 90th day thereafter, and the Start Date must fall within 90 days of the issuer receiving proceeds in full. Unclaimed amounts "cease to be claimable", Tessera "reserves the right to forfeit unclaimed proceeds", and the issuer is "deemed released from all obligations" - redemption is not automatic. Tokens may keep trading on secondary markets until redemption, and if the company never exits there is no maturity date at all. Depending on structure, tokens may be fully extinguished on redemption or retain residual rights where the portfolio holds other positions.

pricing.notes: The API publishes a markPrice and a markValuation per token (T-OpenAI 812.79 / $950B, T-Kalshi 413.80 / $14B, T-SpaceX 423.00 / $800B on 2026-09-16), with no disclosed methodology and no external reference market for a private company. Secondary price discovery happens on Solana DEXs (Meteora, Jupiter). There is no continuous mint/redeem arbitrage loop: primary issuance runs through Alpha Vault pro-rata auctions and direct acquisition on the platform, while redemption is unavailable until a Liquidity Event occurs, so the Chainlink PoR feed constrains supply but nothing pins price to the mark.

venues: Tessera platform (direct acquisition with USDC/USDT, 0% fee)
Alpha Vault pro-rata auctions (fair-launch primary distribution)

incidents.summary: Governance concentration, disclosed by the issuer: the upgrade authority for both the Token Program and the Referral Program was transferred from a Squads multisig (HimRFy5qQHKribjfnqSDYLhZ6hujsmJgYoGRKir1NMrA) to a single Fireblocks wallet (EXvTtxurWBUNNCtLojaN8ZBJFNJPZFSH3szoih9hh7YW). That one key now holds upgrade, mint, transfer-fee-config, referral config and default fee recipient authority across all programs and mints.

Sector-wide risk event affecting Tessera's largest product: Anthropic and OpenAI both declared unauthorised SPV and tokenized transfers of their stock void, OpenAI warning such transactions "could carry no economic value to buyers". Tessera's T-OpenAI acquires exposure via "direct shares, contracts for shares, or similar instruments", and neither the instrument type nor the counterparty is disclosed per portfolio, so it is not publicly determinable whether T-OpenAI's exposure is of a kind OpenAI would recognise. No reporting named Tessera and Tessera published no response found in this research.

Documentation/on-chain mismatch found in this research: the docs state all T-Tokens have "Transfer Fee, Transfer Hook, Metadata Pointer, and On-Chain Metadata" extensions enabled, but no transferHook extension exists on any of the three mints; and a live freezeAuthority (7n2PNcDXVDMK2m8dyV9cVPNY7p4jM4ZMHv7TzfibEt8o) is present on all three mints yet does not appear in the docs' Authorities & Security table. The docs also describe T-Tokens as "SPL tokens on Solana" in one place and Token-2022 elsewhere; on-chain they are Token-2022.

openQuestions: Who are the independent auditors behind the Chainlink PoR feeds, and will the attestation reports themselves ever be published? The docs promise the auditors "will be shown" on the transparency page in future tense.

For T-OpenAI specifically: is the exposure direct shares, a contract for shares, or a synthetic? This decides whether OpenAI's May 2026 position that unauthorised SPV/tokenized transfers are void touches Tessera's portfolio at all.

How does a holder rank on insolvency of the Panama issuer entity? The terms are silent, and the loan is unsecured, so the Cayman segregated portfolio protects the assets from the holder as much as from third parties.

Why does the on-chain reality diverge from the docs - no Transfer Hook despite the claim, and a freeze authority that the Authorities & Security table omits? Who controls 7n2PNcDXVDMK2m8dyV9cVPNY7p4jM4ZMHv7TzfibEt8o?

The docs advertise "no KYC" and permissionless global access while the terms exclude US persons plus 17 jurisdiction categories and reserve identity verification. Which governs in practice, and is any geoblocking enforced?
How is markPrice computed? The API publishes it with no methodology, and there is no external reference market.
Note the jurisdictional irony worth flagging on the site: PreStocks lists both Panama and Singapore as Prohibited Jurisdictions - precisely where Tessera is incorporated and whose law governs it.
What happens if a segregated portfolio's exposure is written down between monthly attestations? Supply is not reduced automatically and the feed lags.

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Multisig evidence, 2026-09-16): the freeze key 7n2PNcDXVDMK2m8dyV9cVPNY7p4jM4ZMHv7TzfibEt8o is a nonce-based hot key with no Squads program in its history and has exercised freeze/thaw four times. Program upgrade authority moved from the Squads multisig HimRFy5qQHKribjfnqSDYLhZ6hujsmJgYoGRKir1NMrA to the single Fireblocks wallet EXvTtxurWBUNNCtLojaN8ZBJFNJPZFSH3szoih9hh7YW on 2026-01-28, which now also holds mint, transfer-fee-config and referral-config authority. The mints carry no permanentDelegate at all, so there is no delegate authority to govern.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: The loan participation is embodied in the token and follows it. The terms give the redemption right to "a holder of those Stablecoin Loan Tokens (whether such holder is the Lender of that Stablecoin Loan or acquiror of those Stablecoin Loan Token)", and redemption is effected by burning the token to the smart contract. There is no separate register of lenders; the Solana mint is the record of who holds the claim.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Nothing sits in the transfer path. The mints carry no transfer hook (despite the docs claiming one), no allowlist, and no defaultAccountState forcing new accounts frozen; docs promise you can "transfer freely to anyone" and describe "permissionless, global participation". The 20 bps transfer fee is a fee, not a gate. The freeze authority is reactive, matching the reactiveCompliance model this flag implies.

bearerRedemption.reason: This is Tessera's strongest feature and what separates it from PreStocks. The terms expressly extend redemption to an "acquiror of those Stablecoin Loan Token", not just the original lender, and it is exercised by burning the token to a smart contract rather than by applying to the issuer for discretionary approval. Qualified: the right is contingent on a Liquidity Event and a 90-day window, US persons and 17 excluded jurisdictions are barred, and the issuer may demand AML information - so it is a bearer right with eligibility screening, not an unconditional one.

forcedTransfers.reason: The mints have a freezeAuthority, which can immobilise a token account, but no permanentDelegate and no clawback - so the issuer cannot move a token to a different owner without the holder's key. That means no token-theft recovery, no recovery of tokens sent to an unreachable address, and no mechanism to vest a deceased holder's tokens in their heirs. Freezing destroys value; it does not reassign it.

titleDeed.reason: Explicitly the opposite. The token is a loan participation, and the terms state the issuer's obligation "does not confer on any User any legal, beneficial or other proprietary interest in those Liquidity Event Proceeds, in any PE Investment or in any asset of that Issuer". Docs: "T-Tokens are not equity. Holders have no ownership, voting, or dividend rights ... and do not appear on its cap table."

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Ordinary Token-2022 mints held in any Solana wallet; no custodial account, and docs advertise use across Solana DeFi (DEX trading, lending, LPing) which presupposes self-custody.

issuerIndependent.reason: The claim is an unsecured obligation of a Panama SPV and is worthless without the operator. Tessera alone declares the Liquidity Event, decides when the Redemption Period opens, and chooses the payout stablecoin; if the window lapses the proceeds are forfeited and the issuer is "deemed released from all obligations". Because the loan is unsecured, holders have no claim on the Cayman portfolio's assets if the issuer fails, and if Tessera simply stopped operating no redemption would ever be declared.

presetJurisdiction.reason: The clearest legal framing of the three issuers. Named issuing entities with a registered address, Singapore substantive governing law with conflict-of-laws expressly disapplied, SIAC arbitration seated in Singapore with the Singapore International Commercial Court as the related court forum, and a disclosed Panama/Cayman two-tier structure. A holder knows exactly whom to sue, where, and under which law.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Independent attestations exist and are attached to the token in machine-readable form: audited asset counts for each Cayman segregated portfolio are refreshed roughly monthly, fed through Chainlink's oracle network, and published as live on-chain SmartData PoR feeds on Solana for all three tokens, so anyone can verify supply against attested units. Weakened by the auditors not being named and the underlying reports not being published, and by the feeds carrying counts rather than valuations.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers yes and tokenSelfCustody yes. Docs are explicit - "Anyone can verify that token supply matches actual asset holdings - no KYC, no intermediaries, no trust assumptions" and "no KYC required" for participation. An agent can acquire, hold and trade T-Tokens; it could not satisfy the terms' eligibility representations or any AML request at redemption.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: A court could order a T-Token transferred, and the operator could not execute it. With only a freeze authority and no permanent delegate or clawback, on-chain enforcement is limited to immobilising a balance - it cannot revert ownership, satisfy a seizure with delivery to a receiver, or effect an inheritance. The terms also nowhere address insolvency ranking or how a court order would be given effect on the ledger.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A DEX or wallet-to-wallet transfer settles on the agreement of buyer and seller alone - no issuer sign-off, allowlist check, or KYC step is in the transfer path, and the redemption right transfers with the token to the acquirer by operation of the terms.

attestations.attestor: Unnamed independent auditors of the Cayman SPC portfolios, delivered via Chainlink SmartData (DataLink)
attestations.statement: Audited asset counts per segregated portfolio are validated across Chainlink oracle nodes and published as live PoR feeds on Solana. Two caveats: the auditors are unnamed, and the audited count behind each feed is refreshed only about monthly.

"Tessera does not issue more tokens than there are verified units of underlying exposure" - reserve ratio 1.00, continuously validated. The feeds publish unit counts, not dollar values, so this attests supply discipline and not collateral value.

No ownership, voting or dividend rights; holders do not appear on the underlying company's cap table and have no "legal, beneficial or other proprietary interest" in any PE Investment or issuer asset.

The redemption right travels with the token: burn to the contract after a Liquidity Event, lock-up expiry, receipt of proceeds and an announced Redemption Start Date. Proceeds are stablecoin, not the underlying shares (recorded separately as a finding).

Both the Token Program (TESQvsR4TmYxiroPPQgZpVRoSFG8pru4fsYr67iv6kf) and the Referral Program (TESMgr3q4s1CK5nGz7bmkbMQBQeSt8N9wpZjTDWm2cY) were independently audited prior to mainnet deployment. The audit date is not stated in the docs corpus.

Full Terms and Conditions are published at terms.tessera.pe, naming the per-token Panama issuer entities, Singapore governing law, the SIAC arbitration forum, the excluded persons and the 17 excluded jurisdiction categories.

attestations.attestor: Unnamed Singapore counsel, asserted by Tessera Works Foundation
attestations.statement: Docs assert "a non-security legal opinion under Singapore law, confirming it is structured as a loan product, not a capital markets product". Neither the opinion nor the firm is published, and the docs concede "regulatory treatment may vary by jurisdiction".

findings.statement: Stated twice in the docs: "the loan to the issuer entity is unsecured and is not collateralised by the underlying shares". The holder makes a stablecoin loan to a per-token Panama issuer which lends on to a per-company Cayman SPC segregated portfolio, and ranks as an unsecured creditor of the Panama entity.

Redemption runs from 10am Panama time on the Redemption Start Date to 10pm on the 90th day after. Miss it and "any unclaimed redemption amounts cease to be claimable", Tessera "reserves the right to forfeit unclaimed proceeds", "you permanently lose your funds", and the issuer is "deemed released from all obligations".
Redemption is for stablecoin proceeds of a Liquidity Event, never for the underlying shares or contracts, and only after lock-up expiry and receipt of proceeds by the issuer.
All three mints carry freezeAuthority 7n2PNcDXVDMK2m8dyV9cVPNY7p4jM4ZMHv7TzfibEt8o, a key that appears neither in the docs' Authorities & Security table nor in the terms.

The docs claim a Transfer Hook extension enforcing eligibility; on-chain the hook slot is not even present on the Tessera mints, and no mint in the 441-token universe has a hook program set. The docs also describe the tokens as "SPL" when the chain says Token-2022.
Each mint carries transferFeeConfig at 20 bps with an unbounded maximum fee, so every secondary transfer is taxed at the token level.
The freeze key has 2 freezeAccount and 2 thawAccount transactions between 2026-06-01 and 2026-06-07: the power has been used on real holder accounts, not merely reserved.

The freeze authority is a nonce-based plain key with no multisig program in its transaction history, and the mint, transfer-fee-config and referral-config authorities sit on a single Fireblocks wallet.

Program upgrade authority was held by a Squads multisig (HimRFy5qQHKribjfnqSDYLhZ6hujsmJgYoGRKir1NMrA) until 2026-01-28, when it was moved to a single Fireblocks wallet (EXvTtxurWBUNNCtLojaN8ZBJFNJPZFSH3szoih9hh7YW) that now also holds mint, transfer-fee-config and referral config authority. No N-of-M threshold or timelock remains.

Composition is disclosed only at type level - "direct shares, contracts for shares, or similar instruments tracking company value" - with no per-portfolio breakdown, so the share-versus-derivative mix is not determinable.
The Cayman SPC is described generically and no share custodian, broker or counterparty is named. Fireblocks is named, but for MPC custody of the token authorities, not of the underlying shares.

Docs describe "two layers of isolation" (per-token Panama issuer plus per-company Cayman segregated portfolio) that "structurally prevent cross-contamination", but no legal opinion is published, and because the loan is unsecured the isolation also insulates the portfolio assets from the token holders.
Organic share of 24h DEX volume was 3% on 2026-09-16 (Jupiter stats24h), the lowest of the asset-backed issuers, on three tokens whose median top-10 holder share is 16.7%.

issuers.issuingEntity: unknown - no legal entity is named anywhere in the public documentation. Critically, Ventuals issued no instrument at all: it was a HIP-3 market deployer on Hyperliquid, so there is no issuer of a security or token to identify.
issuers.governingLaw: unknown - no terms of service, governing-law clause or dispute-resolution provision appears in the docs corpus or on the app
issuers.regulatoryStatus: unknown / unlicensed, and structurally different from its peers: because a Ventuals position was a cash-settled derivative referencing a valuation rather than a claim on shares, no SPV, share transfer or securities offering was involved. Press coverage framed this as the category's regulatory workaround - a shift "from tokenized stock structures using special purpose vehicles, which have faced legal challenges, to synthetic perpetuals that may avoid some restrictions but could still face future scrutiny from private companies". No CFTC, SEC or offshore registration, exemption or US-person exclusion was found in any primary source.
issuers.holderClaim: Nothing was owned. A position was a margin position in a Hyperliquid HIP-3 perpetual futures market, cash-settled in USDH. Docs are unambiguous: "Instead of share prices, on Ventuals you trade on whether you think the total valuation of the company is going to go up or down. When you have a position in a company on Ventuals, you do not have any underlying economic ownership in the company - you're merely speculating on its valuation change." Company valuations were divided by 1 billion and quoted as "Valuation Units".
issuers.underlyingCustodian: none - there were no shares, SPV, holding entity or custodian anywhere in the structure. The only asset involved was USDH margin collateral held in the trader's on-chain HyperCore account. USDH is "deployed through Stripe's stablecoin platform (Bridge), fully backed 1:1 by US Treasuries, cash, and cash equivalents managed by BlackRock".

custodyVerification.notes: Nothing to verify by construction - a fully synthetic derivative has no reserve. This is not a disclosure failure but a category difference: where PreStocks and Tessera invite proof-of-reserve questions, Ventuals had no reserve to prove. What was verifiable was the margin system itself: positions, oracle prices and USDH collateral all lived on Hyperliquid and were publicly inspectable on-chain, with oracle prices pushed roughly every 3 seconds.

securityInterest.holder: none - no asset existed to take security over

redemption.eligibility: n/a - positions were never redeemable for shares or any underlying. Exit was by closing the position on the order book, or by automatic cash settlement at wind-down.
redemption.rails: PnL cash-settled in USDH with no USDH/USD conversion. At wind-down all open positions were settled automatically at a frozen mark price with no action required from traders; users then bridged USDH to USDC via the HyperCore USDH/USDC order book or the 1:1 zero-fee HyperEVM bridge through Across Protocol.
redemption.fees: No deposit fees, no withdrawal fees and no cut of native HYPE staking yield on vHYPE - docs: "Ventuals has never earned any fees on vHYPE." Trading fees followed the Hyperliquid HIP-3 venue model.

issuers.corporateActions: n/a - no equity, so no dividends, splits, votes or cap-table events could flow through. The only lifecycle event was the venue's own wind-down, which functioned as a synthetic settlement: effective 9:30am ET 2026-06-15 the OPENAI and ANTHROPIC marks were frozen at their 24-hour TWAPs (mark samples every 5 minutes) and funding rates set to 0, "the fairest settlement mechanic considering that these markets do not have a realtime external reference price". OPENAI halted 10:30am ET 2026-06-15 and settled at $1,341.80; ANTHROPIC halted 11:30am ET 2026-06-15 and settled at $1,618.90. Commodity markets froze to CME prices at 2:20pm ET 2026-06-18 (SOY 2:30pm, WHEAT 3:30pm); index markets froze at 4:00pm ET 2026-06-18 and halted hourly from 4:30pm to 11:30pm ET. vHYPE withdrawals returned HYPE 1:1 plus accrued native staking yield, batch-processed from 10am ET 2026-06-19 and every 24-72 hours thereafter.

pricing.notes: Two-thirds self-referential, and the operator said so. Oracle price = (1/3) x Notice valuation estimate + (2/3) x 2-hour EMA of Ventuals' own mark price, pushed on-chain about every 3 seconds. The external third came from Notice (notice.co), polled at least once a minute, incorporating secondary transactions, secondary bids and offers, fundraising announcements, mutual fund marks, 409A valuations and a comparable public-company set. Mark price was itself an EMA of a liquidity-weighted impact price with a dynamic coefficient k that falls to 0 once the impact price deviates 2% or more from its 1-minute EMA, capping mark movement at 0.125-0.2% per update. The operator designed in room for price discovery deliberately, citing the "IPO pop" phenomenon - but the sunset guide concedes outright that these markets "do not have a realtime external reference price", so no arbitrage could anchor them and the settlement price had to be an internal TWAP. The one external validation point in the sector: a Hyperliquid pre-IPO perp priced Cerebras within 1.3% of its $350 Nasdaq opening price.

venues: Hyperliquid (as a HIP-3 perpetual-futures market deployer, using Hyperliquid's own order book)
app.ventuals.com frontend (Privy embedded wallets for email signups)

incidents.summary: Ventuals announced it was sunsetting and winding down its on-chain pre-IPO markets, with the team folding into an unnamed project in the Hyperliquid ecosystem. Over its run it traded more than $650 million in volume and raised over 500,000 HYPE in community support. This is the decisive fact for grading: the entire product was extinguished at an operator-chosen mark within hours of the announcement, and holders had no instrument that survived it.

Pre-IPO market settlement executed: marks frozen at 24-hour TWAPs and funding zeroed at 9:30am ET; OPENAI halted 10:30am ET and settled at $1,341.80; ANTHROPIC halted 11:30am ET and settled at $1,618.90. All open positions settled automatically. The operator warned traders against closing early because "liquidity may be thin and the orderbook price may deviate from the mark price TWAP" - an admission that the order book could not be relied on to exit at fair value.
Commodity and index markets entered settlement periods and were frozen to external exchange/CME prices, then halted on a staggered hourly schedule through 11:30pm ET.

vHYPE withdrawals began batch processing at 10am ET, returning deposited HYPE 1:1 plus accrued native staking yield, continuing every 24-72 hours. New vHYPE deposits were disabled immediately on announcement. Depositors were made whole in HYPE terms.

Stated end of sunset-page support: "We plan to maintain this page at least until September 15, 2026. Please withdraw any remaining vHYPE and export your Privy wallet before that date." That date passed the day before this dossier was compiled; app.ventuals.com now serves only "Ventuals is sunsetting", so email-signup users who did not export their Privy wallet may have lost their access path.

openQuestions: CORRECTION FOR THE EXISTING RECORD: the repo's "Ventuals Pre-IPO" entry is typed "Tokenized Pre-IPO Equity" with tokenStandard "HyperEVM". Ventuals never tokenized equity and issued no pre-IPO token - it deployed HIP-3 perpetual futures markets on Hyperliquid. The record's asset_image also points at a vHYPE logo, which is the HYPE staking vault token rather than any pre-IPO asset. The blockchain field (Hyperliquid) is correct.

CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH PREMISE: Ventuals has no Solana presence - no program, no mint, no Solana deployment at any point. The dossier was requested on the assumption of Solana pre-IPO exposure; the Solana pre-IPO issuers are PreStocks and Tessera.

The record should be marked defunct: all markets were settled and halted in June 2026 and app.ventuals.com now serves only a sunset notice. Consider whether rwa-sonar keeps defunct entries with a status flag or retires them, since a maturity grade on a dead product is misleading either way.
Which Hyperliquid-ecosystem project did the team join? Neither the announcement nor any coverage named it, and it matters for whether these markets return under a new operator.

Was there ever a terms of service, and were US persons excluded? Nothing was found - notable given that this synthetic structure was widely read as the way to sidestep the SPV transfer-restriction problem.
Did any email-signup users lose access by not exporting their Privy wallet before the 2026-09-15 sunset-page deadline?

Note for cross-referencing: Ventuals ran OPENAI and ANTHROPIC markets but not SPACEX in the final period - press attributes the SPACEX pre-IPO perp on Hyperliquid to Trade.xyz, while the Ventuals docs list SPACEX among its own markets. Deployer attribution over time is unresolved.

keyGovernance.evidence: Not applicable: Ventuals never issued a token and never deployed a Solana program. Positions were margin entries in a Hyperliquid HIP-3 perpetual market, so no mint, freeze or delegate authority exists to govern (stocks/findings.md, Ventuals entry).

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Consistent with the existing record. The Hyperliquid HIP-3 order book and margin engine were genuinely on-chain and authoritative for the POSITION, but there was no ownership of any real-world asset for a ledger to record. The referenced companies' cap tables were entirely untouched by anything happening on Ventuals, and the docs say so explicitly: no underlying economic ownership.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: A perpetual futures position is account state in a margin engine, not a bearer instrument. It could not be sent to another address at any price, and could only be entered or exited against the venue's order book. The operator could and did halt trading and force-settle every position.

bearerRedemption.reason: There was nothing to redeem and no custodian to present to. Exposure terminated either by closing on the order book or by the operator's automatic cash settlement in USDH.

forcedTransfers.reason: No token existed to move, so the loss-recovery, theft-recovery and heritability capabilities this flag is about were all structurally unavailable. The venue could liquidate under-margined positions and did force-settle all positions at wind-down, but forced settlement of a derivative is not the ability to reassign ownership of an asset to a rightful owner or heir.

titleDeed.reason: The clearest 'no' of the three issuers, and by design rather than by omission: "you do not have any underlying economic ownership in the company - you're merely speculating on its valuation change." The position referenced a valuation figure, not even a share price.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Consistent with the existing record. Non-custodial in the usual DEX sense - the trader held their own keys and the USDH margin sat in an on-chain HyperCore account they controlled, with permissionless withdrawal. Qualified twice: margin was posted into the venue's margin system rather than sitting free in a wallet, and email signups used Privy embedded wallets that had to be exported before the sunset page went dark.

issuerIndependent.reason: Demonstrated, not merely predicted - the strongest available evidence for this flag anywhere in the pre-IPO category. The operator announced a wind-down and within two hours had frozen the marks, halted the markets and extinguished every pre-IPO position at a price of its own construction. Nothing survived the operator's exit. To its credit the wind-down was orderly and vHYPE depositors were returned HYPE 1:1 plus yield, but orderliness is not independence.

presetJurisdiction.reason: No legal entity, no jurisdiction of incorporation, no governing law, no dispute-resolution clause and no terms of service were found in the docs corpus or on the app. A trader had no identifiable counterparty and no forum.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: No attestation mechanism existed and nothing could be attested, since there was no underlying asset or reserve to link a position to. The nearest third-party input was Notice (notice.co) supplying one-third of the oracle weight - a valuation data vendor, not an attestor of any asset's existence.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers is no, so aiReady is no regardless of KYC. Consistent with the existing record. Worth noting the failure mode was not KYC - no KYC was documented - but the non-transferability of margin positions.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: There was no ownership ledger for a court to correct. The operator could liquidate, halt and force-settle positions, but could not revert ownership, give effect to a seizure by delivering an asset, or vest anything in an heir - because no asset was ever held.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Positions could not be assigned between parties by agreement. Entry and exit ran exclusively through the venue's order book and margin engine, and the operator retained the power to halt trading and settle unilaterally - which it exercised on 2026-06-15.

attestations.statement: "When you have a position in a company on Ventuals, you do not have any underlying economic ownership in the company - you're merely speculating on its valuation change." Marked expired because the product itself was discontinued.

attestations.attestor: Ventuals (operator), with Notice (notice.co) as the external data source
attestations.statement: Oracle price published on-chain roughly every 3 seconds as (1/3) x Notice valuation estimate + (2/3) x 2-hour EMA of Ventuals' own mark price. Fully documented formula, but two-thirds self-referential.

The Sunset Guide published the settlement method (24h TWAP from 5-minute mark samples), the exact settlement prices ($1,341.80 OPENAI, $1,618.90 ANTHROPIC), a per-market halt schedule, the vHYPE 1:1-plus-yield redemption terms and batch cadence, and the USDH-to-USDC exit routes.

"100% of vHYPE holders will be able to withdraw their deposited HYPE ... back 1:1, plus any accrued native staking yield since their deposit", batch-processed from 10am ET on 2026-06-19. No deposit, withdrawal or yield-share fees were ever taken.

findings.statement: No SPV, share purchase, holding entity or custodian existed at any point. A position was a margin position in a Hyperliquid HIP-3 perpetual futures market cash-settled in USDH, quoted in "Valuation Units" of company valuation divided by one billion. Reserve and custody questions do not apply.

Operator-admitted at settlement: an internal 24-hour TWAP was used because "these markets do not have a realtime external reference price". The live oracle was itself two-thirds an EMA of the venue's own mark.

Exercised in full on 2026-06-15: marks frozen at 24-hour TWAPs, funding zeroed at 9:30am ET, markets halted on a published schedule (OPENAI 10:30am, ANTHROPIC 11:30am) and all open positions settled automatically with no action available to traders.
Product documentation was thorough but no terms of service, governing-law clause or dispute-resolution provision was published anywhere in the docs corpus or on the app.

No legal entity is named anywhere in the public documentation. Structurally there was no issuer at all: Ventuals was a HIP-3 market deployer on Hyperliquid, so no instrument and no counterparty entity was ever identified.

Ventuals announced on 2026-06-15 that it was sunsetting its on-chain pre-IPO markets, with the team folding into an unnamed Hyperliquid-ecosystem project. The whole product was extinguished at an operator-chosen mark within hours of the announcement and no instrument survived it.

keyGovernance.evidence: Not applicable: Ventuals never issued a token and never deployed a Solana program. Positions were margin entries in a Hyperliquid HIP-3 perpetual market, so no mint, freeze or delegate authority exists to govern (stocks/findings.md, Ventuals entry).

bearerRedemption.reason: Redemption requires successful KYC/AML with the Issuer before the Products are accepted, only whitelisted wallets may interact with the primary-market platform, and the Issuer may reject a request on negative findings. Physical delivery of the underlying is expressly excluded — settlement is cash only, T+5. Presenting the token is not sufficient.

forcedTransfers.reason: Verified on-chain: the Token-2022 mints carry a permanentDelegate (5aMNNLQJwAEeoemTEMkv5NVjqKwvvefRYCQ5Z67HFvEq) which can transfer or burn tokens from any holder account without the holder's consent, plus a freezeAuthority and a pausableConfig (JDq14BWvqCRFNu1krb12bcRpbGtJZ1FLEakMw6FdxJNs). The legal side also has a Realization Event mechanism under which the Security Agent liquidates collateral and forces maturity.

titleDeed.reason: The token is a bearer debt instrument / tracker certificate, not the share. The prospectus states investors' rights 'do not consist of any shareholders' rights', excluding attendance, dividend payments, participation and voting, and investors 'are not entitled to any rights or claims to the Underlying ... or the Collateral aside from those described in the Terms and Conditions'. A derived economic claim, not full ownership.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Base Prospectus s.3.17 names as an advantage 'the direct control of the ledger-based security by the Investor, as it may be held in an unhosted respectively non-custody wallet, which the Investor has exclusive access to'. Confirmed by on-chain state: ordinary Token-2022 accounts, not frozen by default.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token's value is a claim against the Issuer, an SPV that the prospectus says is 'currently not profitable', depends on parent financing, whose reserves 'remain limited, which may result in the inability of the Issuer to continue as a going concern', and whose obligations are not guaranteed by Payward/PEL. Rebasing and redemption both require issuer action; the scaledUiAmount multiplier authority is issuer-controlled. Mitigated but not cured by the product-specific pledge to the Security Agent, who on a Realization Event liquidates and distributes cash — the token then ceases to track anything.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Base Prospectus clause XXVIII: the Products and the rights and obligations of the Issuer and each holder 'shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of Jersey', with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Jersey; the Registration Agreement is governed by Swiss law (Art. 973d CO). Unambiguous and published.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Chainlink Proof of Reserve publishes reserve figures on-chain, sourced from an attestation API operated by The Network Firm, which holds read-only access to Backed's custody bank accounts; updated daily or on a >10% reserve change. Independent of the issuer. Weakness: no signed periodic examination/AUP report was found published, and no public smart-contract audit exists.

aiReady.reason: Per the vocabulary formula: unconditionalTransfers = yes and tokenSelfCustody = yes. No KYC is in the secondary transfer or holding loop; an agent can acquire and hold xStocks on a DEX. KYC only gates the primary market (mint/redeem).

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The permanentDelegate plus freeze and pause authorities give the issuer on-chain means to implement a court order (seizure, reversal, recovery), and the legal layer provides a Security Agent with account control to enforce against the collateral. Whether the issuer would act on a foreign court order is undocumented, but the capability exists.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A secondary transfer settles on buyer/seller agreement alone — no issuer, platform or regulator sign-off is required, and the docs state secondary trading 'does not require direct interaction with the issuer'. The prospectus recognises the ledger transfer as the legally effective transfer of the security.

attestations.statement: Each xStock is a bearer debt instrument classified as a tracker certificate issued by a Jersey SPV; it is not equity in the reference company.

Base Prospectus s.4.1.1: the securities are Ledger-Based Securities under Art. 973d CO, transferable only via the Securities Ledger, which 'serves as the source of truth in relation to transfer records'.
Investors' creditors' rights 'do not consist of any shareholders' rights', excluding attendance, dividends, participation and voting rights.
Named custodians/brokers for TSLAx: Alpaca Securities LLC, InCore Bank AG, Maerki Baumann & Co. AG, GTN Europe Financial Services Limited.

Collateral is held in dedicated per-Product (sub-)securities accounts at the custodian with no commingling between products; InCore Bank AG must provide a separate account or subaccount per Underlying.

Custodian-level only: InCore Bank AG as custodian 'is neither allowed to do any securities lending nor any other proprietary transactions with the Underlyings'. The Issuer's own right to lend Underlyings to a Prime Borrower is recorded as a finding, not covered here.

Investors have a sole claim to the Collateral allocated to their specific Product via a first-ranking lien (reguläres Pfandrecht) in favour of Security Agent Services AG as direct representative, and no residual claim against the Issuer once pro-rata Net Realisation Proceeds are paid.

attestations.attestor: The Network Firm (relayed on-chain by Chainlink Proof of Reserve)
attestations.statement: The Network Firm operates Backed's attestation API with read-only access to the custody bank accounts; figures are relayed on-chain by a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed daily or on a >10% change in reserve volume. The Solana feed address is unconfirmed and there is no public REST endpoint.
Issuer states products are 'fully collateralized on a 1:1 basis' with balances adjusted to always reflect 1:1 exposure; the prospectus adds an overcollateralisation requirement for Other Collateral.
Base Prospectus approved by the FMA under EU Prospectus Regulation 2017/1129 on 8 May 2026, valid to 7 May 2027, notified into 29 EEA member states.
TSLAx/AAPLx mints show defaultAccountState=initialized and transferHook programId=null: no allowlist and no hook gating secondary transfers, as the issuer documentation describes.

Mints carry permanentDelegate 5aMNNLQJwAEeoemTEMkv5NVjqKwvvefRYCQ5Z67HFvEq (can move or burn any holder tokens) plus freezeAuthority and pausableConfig authority JDq14BWvqCRFNu1krb12bcRpbGtJZ1FLEakMw6FdxJNs.

Full base prospectus, securities note, registration document, supplements and archive are published free of charge; the on-chain token metadata itself points to the terms page. Note the per-product Final Terms PDFs are unpopulated placeholders.

findings.statement: Under a Master Securities Lending Agreement the Issuer may lend all or part of a Product's Underlyings to Alpaca Securities LLC as Prime Borrower where the Final Terms allow. Lent Underlyings leave the Standard Collateral Accounts, are released from the pledge and cease to qualify as Collateral; they are replaced by cash counter-collateral equal to Outstanding Value, marked to market daily.

'Physical delivery of the Underlyings and/or Collateral is excluded and Investors' interests are settled in FIAT currency and/or cryptocurrencies.' Redemption is KYC-gated, returns cash at T+5 with a fee up to 0.50%, and the issuer may reject the request.

The JFSC has consented under the Control of Borrowing (Jersey) Order 1958 and the issuer is AML-registered, but the prospectus states expressly that 'this consent does not give the issuer a regulated status', and neither the Registrar nor the JFSC takes responsibility for the Issuer's financial soundness.
No published third-party smart-contract audit for the xStocks contracts was located as of 2026-09-16 (secondary source only; treat as unverified rather than proven absent).
The single mint authority for all 142 xStocks mints is a plain funded wallet doing daily mintTo issuance, with no multisig program in its transaction history.
The shared freeze and pause authority transacts through the Squads v4 multisig program, so that power is not held by a single signer.

The freeze/pause key's newest transactions (2026-04-29) were mass setAuthority calls via Squads: an authority rotation event across the mint set. The permanent-delegate/hook-authority key is the deployer that initialises new mints (8 new mints on 2026-09-03).
Organic share of 24h DEX volume across xStocks was 6.7% on 2026-09-16 (Jupiter stats24h), so most reported volume is bot and arbitrage flow. 70 of the 156 xStocks mints had zero 24h DEX volume.
Median top-10 holder share per xStocks token was 99.9% on 2026-09-16 (Jupiter audit.topHoldersPercentage): supply sits in CEX omnibus and pool wallets, not in end-holder wallets.

Only 5 of 441 tokens had an entitled Pyth feed, so xStocks premiums were computed against an underlying price implied from a competitor's API (Ondo's marketCap/sharesOutstanding), which is daily-ish and, for ETFs, shares-based rather than NAV.

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Authority keys in practice / Multisig evidence, 2026-09-16): one key each for mint, for freeze+pause and for permanent-delegate+hook-authority across all 142 mints. The freeze/pause key JDq14BWvqCRFNu1krb12bcRpbGtJZ1FLEakMw6FdxJNs transacts via the Squads v4 program (mass setAuthority rotation on 2026-04-29). The mint key 7pt9tkctJPK7PPNQJ77GKg8ZffSF6QxoMiCFYHxrtaCj is a plain funded wallet running daily mintTo, with no multisig in its history. The permanent-delegate/hook key 5aMNNLQJwAEeoemTEMkv5NVjqKwvvefRYCQ5Z67HFvEq is the deployer that initialises new mints; its type was not characterised, hence unknown.
